rows.key_quote: Q3 net sales of $752 million were roughly flat YoY (down <1%) but adjusted operating income rose 45% to $57 million with 240 bps of adjusted operating margin expansion to 7.6%, and adjusted EPS of $1.03 grew nearly 40% versus $0.74. Results exceeded the company's profitability outlook and U.S. retail comps were up 0.4%, but Q4 net sales guidance was cut to $860-880 million (mid-single-digit decline) with adjusted EPS of $1.37-1.55 versus $1.90 a year ago, citing softer quarter-to-date demand. Full-year net sales were lowered to $2.91-2.93 billion (~1% growth) while full-year adjusted operating income growth (low- to mid-single digit) and adjusted EPS (down high-single to low-double digits) guidance were maintained. The key change versus the prior period is the downward revision to demand assumptions, driven mainly by U.S. retail.

Q3 FY2026 produced an economic return of -11.6%, driven by a 16.1% decline in book value per share, though monthly dividends of $0.12 were paid. EAD fell to $0.47 from $0.50 quarter-over-quarter, largely due to repositioning the swap portfolio, while the economic debt-to-equity ratio rose to 8.3 turns from 7.5 and the total portfolio market value fell 2.3%. Management cited sharply higher Treasury yields (10-year +81 bps) and a jump in the MOVE index to 110 from 83 as the backdrop, and noted quarter-to-date book value is up roughly 4% for a ~6% economic return. The dividend is under board review given market conditions, current earnings, and the current payout relative to book value.

Olin reported Q3 FY2026 with adjusted EBITDA guided to $80-100 million for Q4 and approximately $550-570 million for full-year 2026. The quarter absorbed roughly $30 million of negative impact from reduced Freeport VCM operating rates, a $32 million year-over-year VCM headwind, and a $25 million year-over-year penalty from the 45V hydrogen tax credit change. Management expects sequentially higher maintenance turnaround costs (~$25 million in CAPV, $30 million in epoxy), lower domestic caustic pricing, and year-end destocking at higher-than-normal levels in Q4, while noting a firming caustic market into 2027 with announced price increases expected to be realized in Q1 2027. The Huntsman merger close is now expected in Q1 2027, with more than $400 million of cost synergies still targeted.

Oil States reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $170 million and adjusted EBITDA of $20 million, up 8% and 6% sequentially, which management said exceeded guidance. Adjusted EPS was $0.15 versus GAAP $0.05, the latter including executive transition and facility exit charges. Revenue growth was led by Offshore Manufactured Products ($104 million, 18% segment margin) and Downhole Technologies ($42 million, up 6% sequentially), while Completion and Production Services declined 5% sequentially to $23 million on softer U.S. land activity. Backlog rose 7% sequentially and 21% year-over-year to $482 million, the highest in almost 12 years, with a 1.3x quarterly book-to-bill; Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $172-184 million and adjusted EBITDA of $20-23 million.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $4.0M versus $2.2M a year ago, driven by service, ion channel and xPloration revenue; nine-month revenue rose to $31.8M from $10.3M on milestone timing. Net loss narrowed to $15.7M ($0.12/share) from $16.5M ($0.14), and total opex was flat at $20.4M. Guidance was raised: FY2026 revenue to $35M-$39M from $32M-$36M, with opex guidance cut $1M and year-end cash now $53M-$57M, roughly cash-flow break-even for the year. Key changes include the new Lilly ion channel license (up to $370M milestones) with service revenue starting in Q4, and xPloration guidance of $2M-$3M in 2026, doubling in 2027 and again in 2028.

Newell reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 3.7% to ~$1.9B and core sales up 3.3%, both above the high end of the 2%-3% guidance range. Normalized gross margin rose 70 bps to 35.2% and operating margin rose 90 bps to 9.8%, yielding normalized EPS of $0.20 versus $0.17 a year ago. Full-year net and core sales guidance was raised to 2%-3% and 1%-2% respectively, but the operating margin outlook of 10%-10.4% and the $0.74-$0.76 EPS midpoint of $0.75 were only maintained, with a $20M increase to the in-year inflation headwind (now $220M). Guidance for Q4 calls for 1%-3% sales growth and EPS of $0.17-$0.19.

NatWest reported Q3 income ex-notables of GBP 4.6bn, up 3.1% QoQ, operating profit of GBP 2.2bn and RoTE of 21.6%, with customer assets and liabilities up 14.2% YoY and a cost-income ratio of 45.1%. Full-year 2026 guidance was unchanged at ~GBP 17.9bn income, ~GBP 8.5bn costs and impairment below 25bps, with only a small enhancement to the Jan-2027 RWA expectation (~GBP 210bn). The key shift was NIM commentary: management guided to a broadly stable margin through 2027 and declined to give 2027 income guidance, which the Q&A dwelt on heavily amid a large share-price reaction. CET1 came in at 13.5% after distributions, with 208bps of capital generation and the Pillar 2A reduction of 43bps confirmed.

nVent reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $1,515M, up 44% both reported and organic, well ahead of guidance, with adjusted operating income of $335M (+57%), return on sales of 22.1% (+190 bps), and adjusted EPS of $1.52 (+67%), ahead of the high end. Full-year guidance was raised again: reported sales growth to 48%-49% from 37%-39%, organic to 38%-39% from 32%-34%, and adjusted EPS to $5.36-$5.39 from $5.00-$5.10, incorporating the closed Maverick Power acquisition (adding ~10 points to sales growth). Q4 guidance calls for reported sales growth of 45%-48%, organic growth of 26%-29%, and adjusted EPS of $1.30-$1.33 (+45% at midpoint), with margins up ~60 bps but Maverick investments and supply-chain pacing tempering the sequential trajectory. Free cash flow was $268M and $100M of buybacks plus a 5% dividend increase were cited.

Q3 revenue was $76 million, up 11% YoY but down $4 million sequentially and below expectations, driven by a nearly $6 million sequential decline in Texas rental and service revenue on exceptionally dry weather; adjusted EBITDA was $20 million at a 26.2% margin, up ~400 bps YoY but down 530 bps sequentially, and adjusted EPS was $0.09 vs $0.07. Management revised FY2026 guidance down to $300-305 million revenue and $90-93 million adjusted EBITDA, citing the seasonal rental impact and utility customer Q4 purchasing priorities, with product sales now expected flattish for the year. Q4 rental and services are guided to mid-teens YoY growth with margins returning to first-half levels as fleet utilization recovered to the mid-70s exiting October.

Nexa reported Q3 2026 revenue of $937 million, up 3% QoQ and 23% YoY, with record-of-year Adjusted EBITDA of $301 million (32% margin, up 62% YoY) and free cash flow of $73 million. A net loss of $47 million ($0.47/share) was driven by a $124 million non-cash impairment at Juiz de Fora and Três Marias, while adjusted EPS was $0.87. CapEx guidance rose 10% to $420 million and cash cost guidance was lowered on higher byproduct prices, but production and sales guidance were unchanged, with copper expected at the low end. Net leverage fell to 1.24x from 1.4x in June, and S&P downgraded the issuer rating to BB+ with a stable outlook ahead of the Boliden transaction expected to close in Q1 2027.

MasTec reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.152 billion, up 30% YoY, adjusted EBITDA of $486 million, up 30%, and adjusted EPS of $2.96, up 19%, with record backlog of $24.5 billion (up >$7 billion YoY and $3 billion QoQ). Power delivery revenue grew 65% with EBITDA up 132% and Superior backlog of $1.8 billion, while pipeline and communications were hurt by permitting delays (projects pushed ~60 days) and customer spending uncertainty. Q4 guidance is framed as a base and upside case tied to pipeline ramp timing, with no specific figures given, and management said it is 'comfortable' with 2027 consensus while flagging communications as likely flattish with better margins. Cash flow from operations was $267 million in Q3 and $388 million YTD, with over $1 billion expected for 2026.

Minerals Technologies reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $555 million, up 4% YoY, operating income of $72 million and EPS of $1.53. Total operating income came in slightly below guidance as Consumer & Specialties absorbed a price/cost lag from energy, diesel and raw material inflation; Engineered Solutions posted 9% sales and operating income growth at a 17.6% segment margin, while Consumer & Specialties operating income fell to $25 million. Q4 guidance is roughly $525 million in sales, $60-63 million operating income and $1.15-1.20 EPS, with six fewer days YoY; full-year mid-single-digit revenue growth is intact and margin recovery to ~14% company-level is guided for Q2 2027 assuming costs stabilize. Cash from operations was $171 million YTD, up 32%, net leverage fell to 1.5x, and the quarterly dividend was raised 8% to $0.13.

Q3 FY2026 sales were $2.8 billion, up 1% as reported and essentially flat adjusting for FX and an extra shipping day; volumes fell 4% while price/mix rose 4%. Adjusted EPS was $2.72, adjusted operating income $200 million (down $5 million YoY), and adjusted EBITDA margin 12.7%, with operating results described as in line with expectations. Q4 guidance calls for adjusted EPS of $1.35-$1.45 and low-single-digit adjusted net sales growth despite four fewer shipping days (a ~6% headwind) and softer demand exiting the quarter. Management introduced a new strategic framework, cut full-year capex to ~$445 million from $460 million, and authorized a new $500 million buyback after repurchasing $261 million in the quarter.

Magna reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $10.1B, down ~4% YoY (down 2.1% organic), but adjusted EBIT rose 11% to $683M, adjusted EBIT margin expanded 90 bps to 6.8%, and adjusted EPS jumped 38% to $1.83, exceeding expectations. Free cash flow was $584M and operating cash flow $950M; the company repurchased $529M of shares and returned $658M total to shareholders. Full-year 2026 sales guidance was lowered (due to reduced China production and unfavorable program mix), adjusted EBIT margin narrowed to 6.3-6.5%, adjusted EPS midpoint maintained at $7.00, and free cash flow guidance raised to $1.85-1.9B. Management highlighted operational excellence and commercial recoveries, noted commodity headwinds (~50 bps) and tariff impacts, and expects Q4 margins to step up despite lower volumes and commercial items flipping negative.

MFIN reported Q3 FY2026 net income attributable to shareholders of $2.4 million, or $0.10 per diluted share, down from $7.8 million, or $0.32 per share, a year ago, as the provision for credit losses rose to $30.8 million from $18.6 million. Net interest income grew 5% YoY and interest income 10% on a 15% larger loan book, but NIM compressed to 7.34% from 8.21%. No formal forward EPS or revenue guidance was given; management said it expects NIM not to step down significantly in Q4, plans to raise loan rates across the board in Q4, expects home improvement growth to outpace rec, and reaffirmed its $3 billion to $5 billion asset goal. The key change versus prior periods is the sharp earnings decline driven by day-one provisioning and reserve builds ($6.9 million hit versus $2.7 million a year ago) from faster portfolio growth.

Methanex reported Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $543 million and adjusted net income of $284 million on an average realized price of $510/t and 2.3 million tons of produced methanol sales; EBITDA fell versus Q2 on lower realized pricing, partly offset by higher volumes, and included a $10 million New Zealand restructuring accrual. Equity production of 2.1 million tons included record North American volume of 1.6 million tons, and cash ended above $900 million. Management guided October-November realized prices to $525-$550/t and expects Q4 adjusted EBITDA above Q3 assuming sustained pricing and similar volumes, while flagging significant uncertainty over how long Middle East supply disruption and the resulting demand destruction persist. Capital allocation skewed to deleveraging, with $300 million of 2027 notes already repaid, the remaining $400 million to be redeemed in Q4, and a new buyback for up to 5% of shares.

LYB reported Q3 EBITDA of $1.5 billion (18% margin), EPS of $2.54, and free cash flow of $1.4 billion at roughly 100% of EBITDA, with EBITDA up over 80% YoY but down sequentially on lower polymer prices. I&D set record EBITDA of $795 million (27% margin) on strong oxyfuels and the Bayport restart, while O&P EAI collapsed to $13 million and O&P Americas fell to $641 million from record Q2 levels. Q4 guidance is for sequential moderation: O&P Americas operating rates ~85%, O&P EAI cut to ~60%, I&D to ~75%, with Europe notably more pressured. Supporting items include a $320.5 million Houston refinery site sale to Valero expected to improve cash flow by $50-100 million annually and lift the full-year effective tax rate to the upper end of prior guidance.

Alliant reported Q3 2026 GAAP EPS of $1.52 and narrowed full-year ongoing guidance to $3.41-$3.46, the top half of the original range. It initiated 2027 ongoing EPS guidance of $3.63-$3.73 (8% growth off the original 2026 midpoint of $3.41) and a $2.25 dividend target, a 5% increase, moderating dividend growth to fund a larger plan. The 2027-2030 capital plan rose 19% to $15.9 billion, lifting rate base plus CWIP CAGR to 13% and long-term earnings growth to 8%+ from 2027-2030, though equity dilution of about 375 bps plus 50 bps from parent debt refinancing widens the gap between rate base and EPS growth.

Q3 FY2026 sales rose 2% to $5.8 billion against a Lear-weighted industry production decline of 2%, with core operating earnings up 6% to $256 million and adjusted EPS up 33% to $3.71 helped by $175 million of buybacks. Seating margins expanded 20 bps to 6.3% and E-Systems 60 bps to 4.8%. Full-year core operating earnings guidance was maintained, but revenue guidance was cut about $225 million (~90% of the revision from China production deterioration) and restructuring costs were raised $25 million, with operating and free cash flow outlooks adjusted down to fund it. Management guided Q4 to roughly the midpoint of the range and reaffirmed 2027 net performance targets of 40 bps in Seating and 80 bps in E-Systems.

Quaker Houghton reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $545 million, up 10% YoY on 3% volume growth and a 7% price/mix contribution, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.39 (up 15%) and record adjusted EBITDA of $90 million at a 16.5% margin. Gross margin fell 130 bps YoY to 35.5% on raw material inflation, though it was flat sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps sequentially. Management guided Q4 revenue and profitability above the prior year and full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA up a high-single-digit percentage versus 2025, while flagging a possible slightly more pronounced seasonal volume decline and incremental raw material inflation into Q4. Operating cash flow of $48 million YTD and Q3 cash from operations of $14 million (versus $51 million prior year) were pressured by higher working capital tied to network transitions and receivables.

KRG reported Q3 FY2026 Core FFO of $0.52/share with same-property NOI growth of 3.6% (3.7% YTD), driven by 183 bps of embedded rent bumps and 115 bps from rent spreads and occupancy gains. Management raised 2026 Core FFO guidance by $0.01 at the midpoint to $2.08-$2.12 and lifted same-property NOI growth guidance by 15 bps to 3.4%-3.9%. Leasing was the standout: over 1.2 million sq ft signed at 14.6% blended cash spreads, with new lease spreads of 33.7% and retail lease rate up 140 bps YoY to 95.3%; Fitch upgraded KRG to BBB+. The main offset is balance-sheet caution, with $230 million of excess proceeds held for optionality rather than deployed, and management citing a $0.03 non-cash drag and lost interest income into 2027.

OneMain reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.7 billion, up 7% YoY, with GAAP EPS of $1.60 and C&I adjusted EPS of $1.51. Managed receivables grew 9% to $28.1 billion (accelerating from 7% last quarter) and originations rose 17% to $4.5 billion; capital generation was $284 million, up 4% YoY. Credit improved markedly: 30-89 delinquency fell 12 bps YoY, 90+ fell 9 bps, and C&I net charge-offs dropped 96 bps sequentially to 7.2%, with management guiding to lower YoY losses in Q4 and into 2027. FY2026 guidance was narrowed to the high end of prior ranges for both receivables growth (9%) and C&I net charge-offs (7.4%-7.9%), while the ~6.6% OpEx ratio guide was maintained.

Oxford Square reported Q3 2026 net investment income of ~$4.9M, or $0.04/share, down from $5.1M, or $0.05/share, in the prior quarter, while total investment income rose to ~$9.9M from ~$9.4M. NAV per share fell to $1.21 from $1.29, and combined net unrealized and realized losses widened to ~$3.3M ($0.03/share) from ~$1.1M ($0.01/share). The board declared monthly distributions of $0.015 for January, February, and March 2027, a step down referenced on the call as in line with current and prospective near-term earnings power, alongside a stated intent to moderately delever (debt-to-equity fell from 1.26x at Q1 to 1.07x at Q3, and lower intra-quarter).

Q3 results far exceeded the high end of outlook for a third consecutive quarter: same-property hotel EBITDA rose 15.1% to $115.2M ($10.7M above the high end), adjusted EBITDA was $107.9M ($11.4M above the high end), and adjusted FFO per share was $0.63 ($0.11 above the top end), with same-property RevPAR up 8.3% on 7% ADR growth and hotel EBITDA margins expanding 205 bps to 28.8%. Full-year guidance was raised by more than the Q3 beat: same-property RevPAR growth to 7.6%-8% (midpoint up 280 bps), same-property hotel EBITDA growth of 12.9%-14.1% (midpoint up 420 bps), and adjusted FFO to $1.88-$1.92 per share (midpoint up $0.17). Q4 guidance calls for same-property RevPAR growth of 4%-6% and adjusted FFO per share of $0.26-$0.30. Management flagged Q1 2027 revenue pace as currently negative on convention timing and Super Bowl shifts, but up 8% or more in each of Q2-Q4 2027.

W&T reported Q3 2026 production of 38,200 BOE/d, 4% above the high end of guidance, with Adjusted EBITDA over $51 million, free cash flow of $33 million, and net debt down 20% QoQ to $160 million (0.9x trailing EBITDA). GAAP net loss was $13.6 million ($0.09/share), driven by roughly $16 million in hedging losses. Management raised full-year 2026 capex to $35-38 million from prior levels and guided Q4 production to about 33,700 BOE/d at the midpoint, citing a one-week Mobile Bay shutdown and Hurricane Isaias downtime totaling about 2,600 BOE/d; Q4 LOE is guided to $65-72 million.

RBC reported Q2 FY2027 net sales up 15.2% YoY to $524.6M, adjusted EPS up 29.9% to $3.74, and adjusted EBITDA up 20.4% to $175M (33.4% of sales). Gross margin expanded to 45.6% from 44.1% reported / 44.9% adjusted, with A&D segment margin up to 42.2% from 38.7%. Q3 guidance is $520-525M (12.7%-13.7% growth), with nine-month sales of $1.564-1.569B (15.6%-16%), and management reiterated full-year gross margin expansion of ~100 bps. The quarter was led by Aerospace & Defense (+15.8%) and Industrial (+14.8%), though marine production remains behind plan and is expected to catch up in Q4.

Cavco reported Q2 FY2027 net revenue of $656.4 million, up 18% YoY from $556.5 million, with record shipments of 5,972 homes and diluted EPS of $7.17 versus $6.55. Factory-built gross margin was 21.1%, down from 22.9% a year ago on higher input costs but up roughly 30-40 bps sequentially as pricing offset materials inflation. Backlog rose 63% YoY with 8-10 week coverage, aided by newly disclosed data-center workforce housing orders, though management declined to quantify that pipeline or give margin guidance. Buybacks totaled $30 million with $272 million unrestricted cash; no formal guidance was provided beyond commentary that material inflation remains a risk to margins.

Capri reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $809 million, down 5.5% reported (4.9% constant currency), but operating income rose 55% to $31 million (3.8% margin, up 150 bps) and EPS came in at $0.42 versus a $0.03 loss last year, with results above management's expectations on revenue, operating income and EPS. Michael Kors revenue fell 8.6% to $663 million, weighed by ~$50 million of inventory delays, a ~40% cut in markdown inventory and ~50% fewer promotional days, while Jimmy Choo grew 11.5% to $146 million and expanded operating margin 830 bps to 1.4%. Guidance was raised: FY2027 revenue now ~$3.42 billion, operating income ~$175 million (+50%) and EPS $2.20 (+45%), with weighted shares cut to ~108 million on $300 million of planned buybacks; Q3 revenue guided to just over $1 billion and EPS $0.95. Gross margin expanded 230 bps to 63.3%, and net debt fell to $336 million from $1.6 billion last year after $150 million of repurchases (10.3 million shares, a ~9% share count reduction).

Q1 FY2027 net sales fell 5.7% YoY to $127.9M, but gross profit jumped to $12.5M from $3.4M and gross margin expanded to 9.8% from 2.5%. The net loss narrowed more than $9M to $2M and adjusted EBITDA was $6.1M, an $8.6M YoY improvement, with $2.5M of free cash flow. Brazil sales rose 14.4% while Americas sales fell $8.2M and Asia fell $3.7M on pricing pressure. Full-year fiscal 2027 outlook is unchanged, with sales and profitability expected to improve YoY and H2 better than H1; the $55.5M term loan was repaid from a real estate sale.

Standex reported record Q1 FY27 sales of $232.6 million, up 7% total and 12.4% organically, with adjusted EPS of $2.41 (+21.1%), record electronics organic growth of 29.5% and a company book-to-bill of 1.17 on record $273 million order intake. Adjusted gross margin rose 240 bps to 44.4% and adjusted operating margin rose 110 bps to 20.2%, with margin expansion in every segment. Management raised FY27 total sales growth to high single digits from mid-to-high single digits and reiterated high-teens adjusted EPS growth, and announced a new $100 million share repurchase authorization. Offsetting the strength, engraving and hydraulics revenue fell 14.9% on North American auto softness and corporate expense rose about $3 million year-on-year.

Strattec reported Q1 FY2027 sales of $147.2 million, down 3.4% year-over-year from $152.4 million, as lower customer production volumes reduced sales by $6.2 million, partly offset by $1 million in net pricing. GAAP EPS fell to $1.19 from $2.07 and adjusted EPS to $1.85 from $2.22, while gross margin contracted 80 bps to 16.5% and adjusted EBITDA declined to $13.5 million (9.2% of sales) from $15.6 million. Management guided full-year gross margin to 15%-16%, below the 16.5% just reported, citing lower volumes, and expects adjusted SAE of $16.5-$17 million per quarter, with North American production forecast down about 2% for the fiscal year. The company generated $10.8 million in operating cash flow, repurchased roughly 68,000 shares for $5 million, and ended with $111.8 million in cash and no debt.

ExxonMobil reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP earnings of $15.4 billion and cash flow from operations of $25.7 billion, with global fuels utilization at a record excluding Middle East impacts and diesel yield up 3.5% versus 2019, which management said represented another $1.5 billion of quarterly margins. The company raised the dividend 4% (44th consecutive annual increase) and said it plans to maintain $20 billion of buybacks in 2027, while net debt fell more than $9 billion and net debt to capital remained the strongest in the industry. Middle East disruptions, concentrated in Qatar LNG train damage and deferred UAE sales, are expected to keep the 350 KBD volume impact unchanged in Q4, and management did not host a December corporate plan update, deferring 2027 metrics to a press release and the January call.

Weyerhaeuser reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP earnings of $61 million, or $0.08 per diluted share, on net sales of $1.9 billion, with adjusted EBITDA of $248 million, up 14% YoY. Wood Products adjusted EBITDA fell $38 million sequentially to $91 million on lower pricing across most products and record-high diesel/transportation costs, including an $18 million OSB loss, while Timberlands EBITDA rose 8% QoQ to $133 million and Strategic Land Solutions fell $43 million to $86 million on real estate timing. Q4 guidance calls for Wood Products EBITDA moderately lower, Timberlands comparable, and SLS down roughly $45 million, with housing expected to remain subdued through year-end as mortgage rates move back over 7%. Management flagged increased Q4 share repurchase, an $146 million / ~81,000-acre Arkansas timberland divestiture, and full-year SLS guidance of ~$450 million; 2026 Monticello capex was lowered to ~$250 million from a $300 million prior estimate.

WisdomTree reported record AUM of $171 billion, up 5% sequentially, with $4.6 billion of net inflows and 13% annualized organic growth. Revenue rose 43% YoY to $179.4 million, and adjusted operating margin expanded 750 basis points to 43.1%. Adjusted EPS was $0.32. Full-year discretionary spending guidance was narrowed to $83-87 million, a modest $2 million reduction at the high end, while interest income guidance rose $1 million to $9 million; all other guidance elements were unchanged.

Piper Sandler reported Q3 2026 adjusted net revenues of $456 million (up modestly YoY), a 19.8% operating margin, and adjusted EPS of $0.87; advisory revenues rose 18% YoY to $250 million, while corporate financing fell YoY (though up 50% sequentially) and municipal financing dropped 36% YoY on higher rates. Management guided Q4 advisory to be the strongest quarter of the year but below the prior-year record fourth quarter, expected corporate financing to slow, and flagged a full-year non-compensation expense ratio above last year. The quarter was mixed: record corporate IB/advisory and strong fixed income were offset by sharp public finance weakness and a softer financing and brokerage outlook into year-end.

Q3 total sales grew 7.5% year-over-year with 5.1% core growth, led by Water Quality at 6.4% and PQI at 3.2%; adjusted EPS rose 19.2% and free cash flow was $304 million. Both segments accelerated core growth sequentially, and management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.49-$4.52 (15%-16% growth), with Q4 core growth guided to 5.5%-6.5% and total sales growth of ~10%-11%. Q4 margins are modeled roughly flat to up ~30 bps year-over-year, with Cost Optimization Program savings and Cleanwater1 dilution offsetting, and 2027 detail deferred to the February guide.

Vale reported Q3 2026 proforma EBITDA of $3.5 billion, down 20% year-on-year, as realized iron ore prices fell 10% and C1 cash cost rose 12% YoY to $23.1/t, with all-in cost up 21% to $60.4/t. Iron ore production fell 6% YoY on Serra Norte depletion, cave-related restrictions and fleet ramp-up issues, though sales held at 86.3 Mt; management now guides to the low end of iron ore production guidance for the year. Vale Base Metals grew EBITDA more than 60% YoY to $1.1 billion, and management is confident on the upper half of copper and nickel production guidance, with 2026 cost guidance reiterated. Free cash flow was $2.2 billion after $1.25 billion of capex, and expanded net debt fell about $200 million to $16.4 billion even after $1.7 billion of dividend and interest-on-capital payments.

Cable & Sky segment revenue fell 3.8% YoY to MXN 14.1 billion, but operating segment income rose 5.6% to MXN 6.0 billion with margin up 380 bps to 42.6% on a 9.7% OPEX decline. Sky revenue dropped 25.5% and residential revenue was flat, while enterprise grew 6.8%; broadband net adds were ~9,000 and video lost ~48,000 subs. TelevisaUnivision revenue grew 9% to $1.4 billion (6% ex-FX) on a 51% Mexico surge from World Cup, but U.S. revenue fell 14% and adjusted EBITDA was flat at $461 million. The company announced a $2 billion agreement to acquire AT&T's Mexico wireless business through a 50/50 JV, expected to close Q1 2027, lifting net debt/EBITDA to 1.9x from 1.6x.

Adjusted diluted EPS rose ~40% to $1.67 from $1.20 and operating income grew 17% to $180 million on revenue before fuel surcharge of $1.9 billion, up 8%, with consolidated operating margin of 9.7% (up 80 bps) and the second straight sub-90% consolidated OR. Truckload was the standout at a 86.7% adjusted OR (560 bps improvement) with operating income nearly doubling to $100 million, and logistics operating income rose 59% to $49 million on 19% revenue growth. LTL was flat at $678 million with a 91.3% adjusted OR, and management described U.S. LTL as broken, with the OR there closer to 97% versus a sub-75% Canadian operation. Q4 adjusted EPS guidance of $1.30-$1.40 was set alongside OR expectations of 400-500 bps truckload improvement, 100-200 bps logistics improvement, and a 0-100 bps LTL deterioration.

The Bancorp reported Q3 2026 core EPS of $1.47, up 25% YoY, with core ROA of 2.42% and core ROE of 34.7%; average loans grew 18.2% YoY and GDV growth was 23% with fintech fee growth of 19%. The company maintained its 2026 core EPS guidance of $5.95-$6.04 but issued a 2027 baseline of $7-$7.20, reduced from prior expectations due to the Chime/Stride Bank acquisition impact, updated pipeline phasing, and rate environment, partly offset by buybacks and a lower tax rate. It initiated 2028 guidance of $8-$8.20. Management also announced a restructuring with an $4.3M charge, 80 position reductions, and $14M annual savings, along with a tax credit strategy lowering the core tax rate to ~24%.

Sanofi reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of EUR 14.4bn, up 14.3% at constant rates, with business EPS up 19.6% and BOI up 19.7% as gross margin expanded 2.1 points on favorable mix and gross-to-net pricing. Dupixent surpassed EUR 5bn for a second straight quarter at EUR 5.7bn, new launches grew 19.2% to about EUR 2.2bn, and vaccines fell 7%, better than the low-to-mid-teens decline flagged in Q2. Management upgraded 2026 guidance to low-teens sales growth (13-15%) and mid-teens business EPS growth (15-17%), but flagged that 2027 pricing returns to a slightly negative contribution and that Cheplapharm and Medley divestments cut sales by about EUR 1.3bn. The quarter also carried a real negative: amlitelimab and itepekimab were discontinued and the pipeline was described as lagging peers.

Q3 FY2026 adjusted sales rose 2.8% with adjusted EBITDA of $67M (13% of net sales, $4.9M above last year) and non-GAAP diluted EPS up 13.2% to $1.54. Vehicle Control grew 6% to $209.5M, Nissens rose 7.6% on Europe's hot summer, Temperature Control fell 4.1% to $138.7M against a record prior-year quarter, and Engineered Solutions grew 4.9%. Full-year guidance was unchanged: low-to-mid-single-digit sales growth and an 11%-12% adjusted EBITDA margin, with tariff pass-through and warehouse ramp costs cited as drags. Leverage reached 1.8x EBITDA, ahead of the 2x target by a quarter, while CFO Nathan Iles departed and former CFO/COO Jim Burke returned as interim CFO.

Silvercrest reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $32.7 million, up $1.4 million YoY, with GAAP net income of $1.2 million ($0.08 per Class A share) and adjusted EPS of $0.16. Adjusted EBITDA was $4.4 million, or 13.5% of revenue, while the compensation ratio stayed elevated at 66.3% for the nine-month period amid the firm's investment program. Discretionary AUM fell $939.2 million to $23.8 billion on weaker markets ($753 million revenue effect), though net flows were roughly flat at $58.3 million and organic new client accounts of $182.2 million were the best quarter of 2026. No formal guidance was issued; management said the compensation ratio should stay elevated as investments mature and pointed to 2027 for revenue contribution, with a dividend of $0.21 per share declared.

JinkoSolar Q3 FY2026 revenue was $2.03 billion, up 10.2% sequentially but down 15.7% year-over-year, as the year-over-year decline reflected lower module shipment volume. Gross margin expanded sharply to 12.3% from 4.2% in Q2 and 7.3% a year ago, narrowing net loss to $25.4 million and adjusted net loss to $1.2 million; energy storage reached roughly 1.75 GWh recognized and posted its first positive quarterly operating profit. Guidance calls for Q4 module shipments of 16-18 GW and full-year 2026 storage shipments of about 10 GWh, but management flagged Q4 gross margin pressure from heavier China shipments, legacy long-term contracts, and elevated freight/energy costs. Management said module ASPs appear to have bottomed and called current margins unsustainable, expecting a recovery next year.

Regeneron reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $5.1 billion, up 36% YoY, and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $20.07, up 70%, marking a third consecutive quarter of double-digit top- and bottom-line growth. DUPIXENT global net sales reached a record $6.5 billion (+35% constant currency) with U.S. sales of $5.1 billion (+40%), EYLEA HD U.S. net sales hit $699 million (+62%), and LIBTAYO global sales reached $550 million (+51% cc). Sanofi collaboration revenue hit an all-time high of $2.7 billion including a 77% increase in profit share, aided by the completed repayment of the Sanofi development balance. Fourth-quarter color was mixed: EYLEA HD unit demand expected up ~10% sequentially with full-year net sales growth over 50%, while legacy EYLEA demand is guided down low-to-mid teens sequentially amid biosimilar competition, and LIBTAYO/LYNOZYFIC growth was framed as modest to incremental.

Record Q3 revenue of $24.2 million rose 14% YoY and 18% sequentially, with GAAP EPS of $0.51 and non-GAAP $0.55 versus $0.41/$0.46 in Q2. The 3870 pump ramp drove the quarter — over 400 systems produced, a 125%+ sequential production increase, with over 300 shipped — and gross margin improved two points sequentially to 76%, though it was down from 78% a year earlier on initial 3870 production inefficiencies. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed and its top end cut to $91.7M-$93.2M from $91M-$96M, and non-GAAP EPS to $2.06-$2.10 from $2.06-$2.21, with management citing the difficulty of ramping production without sacrificing quality. Q4 guidance of $25M-$26.5M implies a roughly $100M+ annualized run rate, and management pointed to upper-teens growth in 2027 without formal guidance.

BP reported a strong third quarter with upstream production held around 2.2 mmboe/d, improved plant reliability, and a 'very strong' refining result amplified by higher trading contribution, which management said let it capture the higher commodity price environment. Net debt fell below the targeted range and structural cost reductions are now within the target range, with line of sight to the remaining two of four primary targets ahead of end-2027. Q4 guidance is weaker on nearly every line: lower production (including a 20 mbd Gulf of Mexico weather hit and BPX phasing), lower refining throughput after Gelsenkirchen completion, seasonally lower customer volumes, softer prices, a typically weaker trading quarter, higher CapEx of ~$1-1.5bn, and $800m higher cash tax payments. The quarter also carried a further $4bn impairment, primarily transition businesses (Lightsource bp and offshore wind), and management declined to quantify the Deepwater Horizon acceleration mechanics ahead of the December strategy update.

Buenaventura reported Q3 2026 revenue of $545M, up 27% YoY, driven by higher realized prices and copper volumes from El Brocal; EBITDA from direct operations rose 34% to $261M (48% margin) and net income rose 50% to $268M. Free cash flow reached $242M, cash totaled ~$1B with a net cash position of $307M, and the board approved an interim dividend of $0.5508 per share. However, gold production fell 6% to ~29,000 oz and silver fell 21% to 3.4M oz, while San Gabriel's ramp-up remains constrained by tailings drying, with nameplate capacity now expected only by end-2028 and 2026 recovery near 70% versus an 85% ultimate target. No formal guidance was provided, though management outlined San Gabriel production of ~600,000 tons in 2027 and ~800,000 tons in 2028.

Exelon reported Q3 2026 adjusted operating earnings of $0.87/share versus $0.86 in Q3 2025, a $0.01 increase driven by $0.06 from approved distribution and transmission rates net of depreciation plus $0.03 of lower costs, offset by $0.07 of storm activity and $0.04 of interest and tax. Results came in ahead of the expectations outlined on the Q2 call, and the company narrowed full-year guidance to $2.85-$2.91 with a goal of delivering at the midpoint or better. Management reaffirmed annualized adjusted operating earnings growth near the top end of the 5%-7% range through 2029, backed by the $41.7 billion capital plan and 7.9% rate base growth, and flagged $12-17 billion of incremental transmission and $3-7 billion of potential regulated storage upside beyond the plan. Regional PJM supply solutions remain slow, with the reliability backstop auction delayed again as PJM filed a revised proposal.

Erie Indemnity reported Q2 2026 net income of $180 million, or $3.45 per diluted share, up from $175 million/$3.34 a year ago, with operating income up 2.5% to $204 million and management fee revenue up 4.7% to roughly $39 million higher. Exchange combined ratio improved 13 points to 103.9% (from 116.9%) on lower catastrophe losses (15-point impact vs 22 points prior year), but direct written premium growth decelerated sharply to 3.3% from 9.2%, policies in force fell 2%, and retention slipped to 87.5%. Management reiterated that growth is the primary challenge amid competitive pressure, with no explicit numeric guidance provided.

Cboe reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue up 18% YoY to $712 million with adjusted diluted EPS up 36% to $3.63 and GAAP diluted EPS a record $4.08, helped by a $71.5 million gain on the Cboe Australia sale. Adjusted operating EBITDA rose 28% to $522 million with margin up 5.8 points to 73.3%, and adjusted opex fell 3% to $204 million. Guidance was raised on both organic net revenue growth (high teens vs. prior mid-to-high teens) and DataVantage (mid-teens vs. prior low teens), while adjusted opex guidance was revised to $830-845 million. The 25-year S&P DJI license extension through 2051 carries a de minimis stated 2027 revenue impact, with SPX pricing optimization flagged to offset royalty resets.

Cameco reported Q3 FY2026 results that were lower year over year and roughly in line with management's stated expectations, due to a longer planned maintenance outage at the Key Lake mill that cut production and raised unit costs, plus inflationary pressure. Guidance was fine-tuned rather than fundamentally changed: uranium production narrowed to 19.5-20.5 million pounds, deliveries to 29.5-30.5 million pounds, direct admin costs and unit cost of sales moved higher, and CapEx was lowered on project deferrals. The 2026 annual dividend was held at CAD 0.24, flat with 2025. Management spent most of the call arguing nuclear fundamentals remain intact and that volatile nuclear equities should not be confused with demand, with contracting still below replacement rate.

The transcript is largely a Q&A with the prepared remarks and numbers referenced but not included, so hard figures are sparse. Management disclosed Q3 came in slightly below its original guidance because Tritan and PET line startups slipped about a month, adding cost and lost volume, and that Q4 carries a roughly $15 million price-cost headwind versus an expected $15 million-plus tailwind, a swing from the July outlook. Full-year operating cash flow guidance was cut to about $850 million from $900 million on higher working capital ($560 million built year-to-date), while 2027 is framed as stable-to-better with AM, AFP and Fibers volume growth and mid-single-digit tow price declines offset by utilization gains.

Q3 FFO per share of $0.71 beat the guidance midpoint by $0.02 and rose 2.9% YoY, with same-property cash NOI up 3.2% YoY (5.3% for nine months). Management raised the midpoint of 2026 FFO guidance by $0.02 to $2.80, same-property NOI growth to 4.25%, capital committed to new investment to $375 million, and capital invested to $240 million. Vacancy leasing of 222,000 sq ft was 50% above the trailing five-year quarterly average, prompting an increase in the full-year vacancy leasing target to 625,000 sq ft while tenant retention guidance was cut 250 bps to 80% to recapture space from three suboptimal tenants. Anthony Mifsud flagged roughly $8 million ($0.07/share) of higher interest expense in 2027 from a higher SOFR curve and $125 million more variable-rate debt.

Centerra reported Q3 adjusted net earnings of $72 million ($0.37/share) on 74,000+ ounces of gold and 13.2 million pounds of copper sold, at realized prices of $3,483/oz gold and $5.74/lb copper. Mount Milligan produced 44,000+ ounces of gold (up 15% QoQ) and lowered full-year AISC guidance to $1,100-$1,200/oz from $1,200-$1,300/oz on strong copper byproduct credits, while gold production guidance of 140,000-155,000 ounces was reaffirmed. Consolidated Q3 AISC was $1,775/oz with full-year guidance of $1,650-$1,750/oz, and the company repurchased a record $53 million of shares, bringing YTD buybacks to $125 million. Thompson Creek remains on track for first molybdenum production in mid-2027 at a total CapEx of $425-$450 million.

Q3 FY2026 operating EPS was $1.28, including $0.05 from RNG 45Z credits and $0.05 from better-than-normal weather; GAAP EPS was $1.30. Management now expects full-year results in the top half of the original guidance range, driven by better-than-budgeted sales, weather and 45Z credits, while reaffirming credit, dividend and long-term growth guidance. Other existing guidance was unchanged, so the raise is a narrowing toward the upper half rather than a new range. LTM weather-normal electric sales grew 3.4%, data center capacity in contracting reached over 54 GW (over 12 GW under ESAs, up 6 GW or 13% since year-end), and CVOW is about 85% complete with 44 turbines installed and budget held at $11.65 billion.

Church & Dwight reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 1% and organic sales up 5.1%, well above the ~3% outlook, driven by 4.6% volume and 0.5% price/mix. Gross margin expanded 170 bps to 46.8% and adjusted EPS rose 13.6% to $0.92 versus the $0.89 outlook. Full-year organic sales guidance was raised to ~5% (high end of the prior 4%-5% range) while adjusted EPS guidance was tightened to ~7% from 6%-8%, with Q4 organic sales guided to ~4% and EPS up 17%-19%. Inflation expectations rose to ~$150 million, $20 million above the July outlook, including roughly $15 million of Q3 tariff refund benefit.

Chevron reported Q3 FY2026 earnings of $9.9 billion ($5.06/share), with adjusted earnings of $10.4 billion ($5.28/share), down $1.6 billion quarter over quarter on lower upstream realizations, liftings, and timing effects, partly offset by lower DD&A and taxes. Adjusted downstream earnings rose on higher refining margins and volumes. Operating cash flow ex-working capital was $16.6 billion and adjusted free cash flow $14.2 billion; net debt/CFFO was 0.4x, debt fell over $3 billion, and CapEx is tracking to the low end of annual guidance with buybacks maintained at $2.5-3 billion. Management was confident on operational records and growth (Venezuela doubling to ~600,000 bpd by 2031 at under $20/bbl total cost, Bakken midstream tariff cut, 50% exploration spend increase) but offered no explicit updated EPS or production guidance and flagged volatile prices as a reason not to change capital allocation.

Consolidated freight revenue rose 17.2% to $315.1 million, driven largely by the Q4 2025 brokerage acquisition, while adjusted operating income grew 5.7% to $15.8 million and adjusted net income rose 14.6%. Adjusted EPS increased both sequentially and year-over-year for the first time since 2022, aided by $5.7 million of pre-tax income from the TEL minority investment versus $3.6 million prior year. However, truckload margins disappointed: Expedited's adjusted OR of 94.1 was 50 bps worse year-over-year and Dedicated's 96.1 was 140 bps worse and 'fell short of our expectations' on unseated tractors, driver pay, equipment costs and heat-driven agricultural volume headwinds. Q4 guidance calls for only modest sequential adjusted EPS improvement on better truckload margins, partially offset by lower TEL contribution ($3.7-4.0 million vs $5.7 million).

Civeo reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $193.1 million, up 13% YoY, and net income of $5.2 million ($0.50 per diluted share) versus a $0.5 million net loss in the prior year. Adjusted EBITDA rose 5% to $30.1 million and operating cash flow nearly doubled to $26.4 million, driven by Canada revenue up 38% and Canadian EBITDA up 47%. Guidance was raised to $710-720 million revenue (from $675-700 million) and $89-92 million adjusted EBITDA (from $85-90 million), with CapEx also raised to $30-35 million. Australia remains soft with local-currency revenue down about 4% and management expecting continued cost-driven weakness into early 2027.

Colgate reported a third quarter with organic sales growth in all four categories and four of five divisions, base business EPS ahead of expectations, gross margin expansion, and free cash flow up 7% with $2.2 billion returned to shareholders year-to-date. Management raised full-year gross margin guidance to up year-on-year from roughly flat previously, driven by productivity (funding-the-growth offset over 290 bps of material inflation) and pricing (80 bps favorable). Material costs remained a roughly $300 million headwind with resins, petrochemicals, pulp/paper and freight elevated, expected to persist through Q4 and into early 2027; tariffs peak in Q4 and no 2027 guidance was given. Latin America grew 6% but Mexico slowed on a difficult consumer backdrop and retailer challenges, and the U.S. business remains a work in progress with only early toothpaste share improvement.

Cousins reported Q3 FY2026 same-property cash NOI up 7.4% YoY (8.6% excluding 201 North Tryon) on 5.5% revenue growth and 2% OpEx growth, its strongest since Q1 2020, and raised full-year FFO guidance $0.02 to a $2.95-$2.99 range (midpoint $2.97, ~4.6% growth vs 2025) on better leasing and fee income. Leasing totaled 546,000 sq ft including 220,000 sq ft of new/expansion, with second-generation cash rent roll-ups of 19.8% (best in five years), and leased occupancy reached 93% with a 3.5-point gap to 89.5% occupied. Management reiterated a path to 90% occupancy by year-end and expects double-digit roll-ups to continue, while committing ~$50 million of equity to a 2401 McKinney land JV in Uptown Dallas with a potential 2027 start. Cash NOI at the redeveloping 201 North Tryon fell 35% YoY and 2027 will carry downtime from phased commencements, including the Legacy Union backfill starting late 2027.

Sensient reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $455.8 million, up from $412.1 million, with 10% local currency revenue growth, 15% local currency adjusted EBITDA growth and 18% local currency adjusted EPS growth; operating income rose to $72.4 million from $57.7 million. Color Group grew local currency revenue 17% with adjusted EBITDA margin of 25.1% (+40 bps), Flavors & Extracts grew 3% with margin of 18.5% (+80 bps), and Asia Pacific grew 15% with margin of 27.5% (+330 bps). Full-year guidance was essentially reiterated (high single to low double digit local currency revenue, mid-to-high teens EBITDA and EPS growth), but the low end of the GAAP EPS range was raised to $4.15 from $4.10 and the range narrowed to $4.15-$4.20. Natural color conversion revenue reached roughly $30 million in the quarter versus $45 million cumulative through Q2, with management now framing the incremental $1 billion run rate as being reached as it exits 2028, citing state-law timing shifting from January to mid-2028.

CN reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS of CAD 2.16, up 18% YoY, on 4% RTM growth and 15% revenue growth; adjusted operating ratio improved 40 bps to 61.0% despite a 50 bps fuel headwind. Guidance for mid-to-high single-digit adjusted EPS growth on low single-digit RTM growth was reaffirmed, with management noting it is tracking toward the upper end of the range. Year-to-date free cash flow rose 25% to CAD 2.9 billion and the company repurchased roughly 4 million shares for about CAD 675 million. Management flagged a ~$0.03 EPS impact in 2027 from the Elk Valley Resources interchange change and ongoing Prince Rupert terminal labor disruption affecting coal and petroleum coke volumes.

CNO reported Q3 2026 operating EPS of $1.90, up 47% YoY, or $1.42 excluding the $56.3 million favorable annual actuarial review, up 48% YoY on that adjusted basis. Management raised full-year 2026 operating EPS guidance to $5.05-$5.15, a 9% increase at the midpoint from prior guidance, driven by a lower expense ratio (18.6%-18.8%) and tax rate (~20.5%). Other guidance improvements included a higher operating ROE trajectory, now on track to exceed the 12% 2027 target, and full-year free cash flow of $220-240 million, though the latter reflects a tighter range with a slight reduction at the high end due to higher FHLB capital consumption. Sales momentum continued with a 17th consecutive quarter of sales growth and 15th consecutive quarter of producing agent count growth.

Ingersoll Rand reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 6% YoY to $2.1 billion, with 4% organic growth, adjusted EBITDA of $584M (including $32M IEEPA tariff refunds; $552M ex-refunds, 1% YoY growth) and adjusted EPS of $1.07 ($1.01 ex-refunds, up 17%). Organic orders grew 18% (high single digits ex a ~$195M data center ETO order), book-to-bill 1.14x, and ITS margins expanded 100 bps sequentially while PST margins rose 180 bps YoY. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to 5.5-7% growth (organic 2-3.5% vs. prior lower expectation) and adjusted EPS raised to $3.58-$3.70 on a lower tax rate (~20%) and reduced share count (~390.5M), though adjusted EBITDA guidance is unchanged at $2.13-$2.19B with the expectation to finish in the bottom half. The board authorized a $2 billion increase to the buyback, and the company closed the IVEK acquisition (~$40M revenue).

rows.company_name: BrightSpring Health Services, Inc. Common Stock
rows.key_quote: BrightSpring reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $4.2 billion, up 26% YoY, adjusted EBITDA of $228 million, up 42% YoY, and adjusted EPS of $0.54, up 80% YoY, with management stating revenue and adjusted EBITDA were above forecast. Specialty and infusion revenue grew 34% on 29% script growth, Provider Services grew 31%, and operating cash flow was $204 million with leverage down to 1.79x. Full-year 2026 guidance was set at $15.9-$16.125 billion revenue and $850-$860 million adjusted EBITDA, implying 37.6%-39.3% EBITDA growth at the high end, with over $700 million operating cash flow. Management reiterated at least 15%-20% organic adjusted EBITDA growth for 2027 on a higher 2026 base, and noted the $35 million Amedisys/LHC contribution expectation was unchanged.

CubeSmart reported Q3 2026 same-store revenue growth of 1.9%, up from 0.8% in Q2, with average occupancy up 60 bps, realized rent up 50 bps, and other property income up 16.8%, yielding same-store NOI growth of 2.1% and FFO per share of $0.66, at the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year same-store revenue guidance to 1.0%-1.4% (up 33 bps at the midpoint) and improved same-store expense growth guidance to 2.8%-3.8% (58 bps better at the midpoint), now implying positive full-year revenue, NOI, and FFO growth at the midpoint. The quarter marked an inflection to positive NOI and FFO per share growth, supported by decelerating new supply and positive move-in rate momentum into October. No 2027 guidance was provided.

BayFirst reported a Q3 FY2026 net loss of $677,000, a sharp improvement from the prior quarter's $32.7 million loss but still a loss; no formal guidance was provided. Net interest margin expanded 59 bps to 4.07% (from a Q2 figure that the CFO noted was 4.70% normalized excluding one-time Asset Resolution Plan impacts), though average loan balances actually fell $17 million as new originations were booked late in September. Total loans held for investment rose 2.3% sequentially to $903 million (down 9.1% YoY) and deposits rose 2.6% to $1.01 billion (down 13% YoY); provision was a $69,000 release vs $29 million in Q2, and net charge-offs fell to $3.2 million. Management framed the quarter as a turnaround milestone, citing an immaterial provision, falling nonperforming loans ($13.4 million, 1.56%), a $14 million rights offering, and preferred conversions and redemptions, but did not commit to a positive-earnings timeline.

Q3 distributable earnings fell to $14.8 million, or $0.08 per share, excluding $21.7 million of realized losses, as a sharp rate move accelerated delinquencies and slowed resolutions. Non-performing assets rose roughly $200 million to about $1.25 billion ($750 million delinquencies plus ~$500 million REO), the board suspended the common dividend effective immediately to preserve $31 million a quarter, and management guided that earnings will likely bottom over the next two quarters while similar reserve and impairment levels continue for four to six quarters. Book value per share was $10.92 at September 30, agency gain-on-sale margin compressed to 1.12% from 1.33%, and full-year origination volume is now targeted at $3.5-$4 billion.

Innovex reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $265 million (up 8% sequentially, 10% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $55 million at a 21% margin, versus 20% in Q2 and 18% a year ago; revenue landed at the guidance midpoint with EBITDA in the upper half of the range. Gross margin reached 36%, up slightly from 1H26, and free cash flow of $32 million was 58% of adjusted EBITDA with $189 million cash and no bank debt. Q4 guidance is $260-270 million revenue and $53-58 million EBITDA, reflecting a rebound in Eastern Hemisphere subsea offset by lower Saudi drilling activity and a seasonal U.S. land dip. Management indicated a high-level view of roughly 10% revenue growth for 2027 without formal annual guidance.

Imperial reported Q3 net income of CAD 2.454 billion, up CAD 1.915 billion YoY and CAD 264 million sequentially, with Downstream earnings of CAD 1.555 billion (up CAD 768 million QoQ) at record levels offsetting Upstream earnings of CAD 941 million (down CAD 358 million QoQ) on lower realizations. Cash flow from operations was about CAD 3.2 billion (nearly CAD 3 billion ex-working capital), cash reached CAD 2.9 billion, and CAD 2.1 billion went to accelerated share repurchases plus CAD 420 million of dividends. Guidance was cut at Kearl to 280,000 bpd gross for the year due to third-party pipeline outages, while Cold Lake and Syncrude remain on track for the low end of the Upstream range and Downstream guidance was reaffirmed. Management flagged a widening WCS differential into Q4 (freight up 8x-10x) but called absolute WCS prices constructive and pointed to strong October market conditions.

Healthcare Realty reported Q3 FY2026 normalized FFO of $0.42/share, same-store cash NOI growth of 5.1%, and same-store occupancy of 93.1%, up 30 bps sequentially. Cash leasing spreads reached 8.6%, the highest in nearly a decade, and 1.5 million sq ft of leases were signed. Management raised full-year normalized FFO guidance to $1.65-$1.67 (up 2 cents at the midpoint) and lifted same-store cash NOI growth guidance to 5.0%-5.25%, the third raise this year. The company repurchased $75 million of stock at about $17.75 and completed JV acquisitions totaling $338 million ($67 million at share) at a mid-7% initial cash yield.

Q3 FY2026 net income was $81M ($0.81/diluted share) versus $136M ($1.32) a year ago, and operating income rose to $180M ($1.78) from $123M ($1.20); the swing came from a $56M fixed-income loss versus a $43M gain prior year plus a 6.1% Two Sigma return. Underwriting deteriorated sharply: combined ratio 97.3% versus 87.8%, loss ratio 62.0% (up 8.7 points) on 8.0 points of Ukraine and 1.1 points of Middle East cat losses, and underwriting income fell to $16M from $64M. Management held the mid-50s underlying loss ratio guidance (55% group, 54.5% international, 56% Bermuda) and still expects low double-digit full-year premium growth, while flagging a $12M net specialty reserve charge and continued property rate pressure. Gross premiums written grew 17% with International up 20% and Bermuda up 14%.

GLPI reported Q3 FY2026 total income from real estate up almost $38 million YoY, driven by ~$47 million of increases in cash income from acquisitions and escalations, with AFFO growth again exceeding 10%. Full-year 2026 guidance is $1.22-$1.225 billion, or $4.11-$4.12 per diluted share/OP unit, including ~$265 million of additional development funding that lifts total 2026 development spend to $800 million; the release does not frame this against prior guidance. Leverage sits at 4.8x versus a 5x-5.5x target, master lease rent coverage ranges 1.61x-2.46x, and Bally's leases are covered at 1.98x and 2.13x. The key overhang is Bally's going-concern language in its 10-Q, which management said did not change its credit view, plus a $3.3 million percentage rent decline in 2027.

GD reported Q3 FY2026 EPS of $4.49 on revenue of $14.57B, up 15.7% and 12.9% YoY respectively, with operating earnings up 14.7% and net earnings up 16.1%. Operating margin expanded 20 bps to 10.5%, and EPS beat consensus by $0.37. The company raised its full-year EPS guidance for the fourth consecutive quarter, to $17.20-$17.30 from $16.80-$16.90, on revenue of $56.5-$56.8B and ~10.5% operating margin. Backlog reached a record $220B, roughly double a year ago, on nearly $99B of new orders led by submarine awards, and free cash flow conversion was 137% year-to-date.

AbbVie reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $3.82, $0.07 above the guidance midpoint, on net revenues of $17.4 billion (+10.5% operational, a $200 million beat). Management raised full-year EPS guidance by $0.11 at the midpoint to $13.95-$13.99, lifted total revenue guidance by $200 million to about $67.8 billion (now $800 million raised since the start of the year), and increased the quarterly dividend 5.2% to $1.82. Immunology grew 16.6% operationally on SKYRIZI +22.9% and RINVOQ +24.3%, neuroscience rose 19.5%, while oncology was flat at +0.9% and aesthetics fell 1.8%, with Humira down 30.6% and IMBRUVICA down 26.1%.

Federal Realty reported Q3 FY2026 FFO per share of $1.87, up roughly 6% YoY and $0.03 above the midpoint (and above the high end) of prior guidance, on adjusted comparable POI growth of 4% cash / 2.5% GAAP. Management raised and tightened full-year FFO guidance to $7.54-$7.58 (a $0.04 midpoint increase, ~7.1% growth), lifted cash comparable growth guidance by 25 bps to a 4.5% midpoint, and kept the GAAP comparable midpoint at 3.5%. The company deployed ~$508 million on The Summit in Birmingham (low-6s contractual / near-7 GAAP yield, forecast >5% NOI CAGR) and repurchased ~870,000 shares at under $109, funded partly by $460 million of 3.5% exchangeable notes, with over $600 million of dispositions in process targeting mid-to-upper 5% yields. Leasing was strong: 96.5% lease rate (highest since 2007), 93.8% physical occupancy, and a 14% cash rent spread on 117 comparable deals.

Gates reported Q3 FY2026 sales of ~$904M, up 5.5% core, with adjusted EBITDA of $215M at a record 23.8% margin (+90 bps) and record adjusted EPS of $0.47, up ~21% YoY. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $1.66–$1.72 ($0.03 higher at the midpoint) while core sales growth was narrowed to 3.2%–3.8% and the 3.5% midpoint maintained. Q4 guidance calls for ~6.5% core growth at the midpoint with ~120 bps of EBITDA margin expansion. Industrial end markets accelerated to high single-digit growth from mid-single digits, led by diversified industrial, personal mobility (+~35%/+40% by segment) and commercial on-highway (>20%), partly offset by weak agriculture and a ~100 bps variable comp headwind in Q4.

FMC reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $106 million, including roughly $639 million of impact from commercial actions; underlying sales were $745 million, below the low end of original guidance on weaker volumes. Adjusted EBITDA was -$559 million (underlying $113 million, also below the low end), and adjusted EPS was -$4.41. The company took $672 million of EBITDA charges tied to transitioning the North America pricing/rebate model (~$500 million, non-cash) and repricing high-cost channel inventory (~$175 million, the only cash-reducing piece). Q4 guidance of $1.04B-$1.14B revenue and $210M-$230M EBITDA is below prior guidance on a larger pricing headwind, and full-year free cash flow is now guided to -$350M to -$150M. Preliminary 2027 EBITDA of $650M-$730M and 2028 of $760M-$840M were provided.

Adjusted EPS of $5.11 rose 2% YoY, the seventh straight quarter of adjusted EPS growth, but that growth was driven by $0.64 from share repurchases and $0.65 combined from after-sales and AutoNation Finance rather than vehicle operations. New retail units fell 3% and used fell 5% (total retail down 4%), used wholesale profitability and SG&A operating leverage were unfavorable, and Q3 CFS gross profit declined to $349 million from $375 million with GPU down 2.7%. Offsets were record after-sales gross profit of $617 million and AutoNation Finance operating profit of $15 million versus $2 million, plus a new $1 billion buyback authorization and a $40 million CapEx reduction to $280-290 million. Management called the environment sluggish, disclosed self-help actions on SG&A and used inventory, and gave no explicit EPS or revenue guidance.

FISI reported Q3 FY2026 net income available to common of $19.6 million, or $0.99 per diluted share, which management said was lighter than the linked quarter. NII hit a record $54.3 million (up 2% QoQ), NIM was stable at 3.70% and up 5 bps YoY, loans grew over 2% QoQ and nearly 6% YoY, and the efficiency ratio stayed below 57%. Core full-year guidance was affirmed, but swap fee guidance was cut to $0.75-1.2 million from $1-2 million, the tax range was narrowed lower, and the net charge-off outlook was set at roughly 30 bps. Non-interest income fell 4.5% QoQ on lighter swap activity.

Federated Hermes reported Q3 total revenue up $4.6 million, or 1%, vs Q2, with operating expenses down $15.9 million, or 4%, helped by the absence of $11.2 million in prior-quarter FCP transaction costs and lower comp; management noted operating margin went over 30%. Record equity AUM of $110.5 billion rose $949 million on $1.9 billion of equity net inflows led by MDT, while money market assets fell $27 billion, or 4%, to a 6.6% fund market share from 6.7%. The $6.5 billion institutional pipeline (equity funding expected over two quarters) is offset by $2 billion of Q4 fixed income redemptions through October 23, including a $1.7 billion Total Return Bond client exit. Management flagged higher Q4 comp and continued systems/comms spending but gave no 2027 expense outlook.

Aptar reported Q3 FY2026 reported sales up 6% to just over $1 billion and core sales up 5%, with core growth in all three segments (Pharma +1%, Beauty +8%, Closures +11%). Adjusted EPS fell 6% to $1.52 versus $1.62 prior year on lower adjusted EBITDA ($217 million, -2%) and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 21.3% versus 23.2%, as emergency medicine (naloxone) destocking and indexation pass-throughs weighed on margins. Q4 adjusted EPS guidance is $1.39-$1.47, a midpoint reflecting roughly 17% growth as the emergency medicine headwind laps, but no full-year EPS guidance was reiterated. The quarter also included a $61.2 million pre-tax charge ($0.94 per share) from deconsolidating the Russian subsidiary, excluded from adjusted earnings, plus a 4% dividend increase and $180 million of year-to-date buybacks.

FET reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $237 million, up 5% sequentially and at the midpoint of guidance, with EBITDA up 14% to $36 million (15%+ margin, up 120 bps) and net income up 33% to $18 million. Both EBITDA and net income hit the top end of guidance, book-to-bill was 103% on $244 million of orders, and free cash flow of $30 million came in well above the high end. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $900-920 million revenue, $123-129 million EBITDA, and $52-58 million net income, all above prior guidance, and guided Q4 revenue of $230-250 million, implying ~19% YoY revenue growth. The company also completed the $33 million Premiere Torque Rings acquisition (~4x EBITDA) and reduced net debt to $97 million (0.9x leverage).

First Business Financial reported record pretax, pre-provision and bottom-line earnings, with EPS up 6% linked-quarter (15% excluding $0.14 of prior-quarter one-time benefits) and up 15% year-over-year; year-to-date EPS grew 20%. Loans rose 10% annualized (20th consecutive quarter of growth) and core deposits rose 14% annualized, pushing NIM to 3.80% and the Q3 efficiency ratio to 55.12% versus 57.87% year-to-date. Guidance was constructive but not raised: management reiterated ~10% loan growth for 2026 and 2027 and positive annual operating leverage, while flagging Q4 NIM will decline from 3.80% toward the 3.60-3.65% range as prepayment fees normalize and deposit costs rise. NPAs rose $2.2 million on an added $5.7 million non-accrual in the Southeast Wisconsin multifamily relationship ($22.7 million total), whose resolution now slips into Q1 2027, and loan pipelines softened entering Q4.

Reported sales fell 1% and comparable sales fell nearly 6%, with Technology Peripherals down low double digits on weak laptop (-20% global) and console demand. Adjusted gross margin rose 290 bps to 35.9% but only because $21 million of tariff refunds added 520 bps and $0.11 to EPS; underlying adjusted EPS was at the low end of guidance and underlying margins fell on unfavorable product/customer mix and fixed-cost deleveraging. Full-year 2026 outlook was raised to 4%-6% reported sales growth and $0.98-$1.02 adjusted EPS, reflecting tariff refunds and the Trust acquisition rather than organic improvement. The company completed the Trust acquisition (~$100 million annual revenue, modestly accretive) and expects $5-$8 million of synergies in 18 months.

AstraZeneca reported 9M total revenue growth of 7% and core EPS growth of 14% at CER, with Q3 product revenue up 6% overall; oncology grew 16% to $21.9 billion (Q3 +17%) while biopharmaceuticals declined 6% in the quarter on Farxiga (-23%) and Brilinta LOE headwinds. Full-year guidance was reiterated at mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth and low double-digit core EPS growth, with core gross margin stable to slightly higher than 2025. The company announced a three-year 'Reshaping for Sustainable Growth' restructuring program with up to $2 billion in one-time costs and $1.5 billion annualized pre-tax run-rate savings, to be reinvested in the pipeline. Cash flow from operations of $10.9 billion was lower year over year on the Lynparza milestone comp and Farxiga working capital effects.

Kimco reported Q3 FY2026 FFO of $0.47/share, up 6.8% YoY, on same-property NOI growth of 4.9% that accelerated from 3.5% in Q2 and 1.7% in Q1. Management raised full-year FFO guidance to $1.84-$1.86 from $1.83-$1.84 and same-property NOI growth to 3.5%-3.8%, while tightening the credit loss assumption to 50-60 bps. Lease occupancy hit a record 96.6% with small shop occupancy at a record 92.9%, blended cash spreads of 12% and new lease spreads of 31.5%. Consolidated NOI margin surpassed 70% for the first time in roughly a decade, and the company repurchased $150 million of stock at an average $23.80 plus ~$74 million of preferred.

Q3 revenue of $485M and Adjusted EBITDA of $147M both came in ahead of guidance, aided by $29M of FX tailwind; on a constant-currency basis adjusted for academic calendar shifts, revenue rose 6% and Adjusted EBITDA 14%. Adjusted EPS of $0.52 doubled YoY, and new/total enrollments grew 8%/6% for the intake cycle, with Mexico primary intake +8% and Peru secondary intake +9%. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed (revenue $1.92-1.93B, Adjusted EBITDA $593-599M, adjusted EPS $2.04-2.10) despite peso/sol weakness that gave back the Q3 FX upside, and Q4 revenue guidance of $546-556M is lighter on FX and $20M of calendar timing. The board added $150M to the buyback, bringing $225M remaining; management flagged online-driven Peru price mix and higher online attrition as a Q4 headwind.

Landmark reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $5.5 million and diluted EPS of $0.89, up from $4.9 million in Q3 2025, on record revenue of $19.2 million. Net interest margin expanded 13 bps QoQ to 4.35% (up 52 bps YoY) and cost of deposits fell to 1.29%, but non-interest income fell $493,000 QoQ on lower mortgage gain-on-sale and non-interest expense rose $292,000 to $12.3 million. Gross loans declined $22.2 million and deposits fell $59.0 million (public funds down $61.7 million seasonally, core customer deposits up $4.9 million), with borrowings up $49.5 million. No formal guidance was given; management called loan payoffs lumpy rather than a trend and expects public fund outflows to reverse in Q4, and declared a $0.21 dividend plus a 5% stock dividend.

Pre-revenue clinical-stage quarter: no collaboration revenue recognized in Q3, with none expected for the rest of 2026 after Sanofi and Gilead milestones and deferred revenue were fully recognized by Q2. R&D expense was $117.6M excluding $10.9M stock comp, up 8% QoQ, and adjusted cash G&A was $10.8M, down 14% QoQ, with $1.6B in cash and investments funding runway into 2029. The call centered on positive KT-579 Phase I healthy-volunteer data — median IRF5 degradation above 90% in the top five MAD cohorts, 87–94% cytokine reduction, 98% median inhibition of TLR7/8-stimulated interferon beta, and a placebo-like safety profile — supporting a Phase Ib lupus trial (LUMORA) starting by early next year. KT-621 Phase IIb AD data remain guided to year-end, with Phase III planned by mid-2027 subject to data and FDA alignment; there is no change to prior timelines.

rows.company_name: KKR Real Estate Finance Trust Inc.
rows.key_quote: KREF reported a Q3 2026 GAAP net loss of $6 million (-$0.11/share) and a distributable loss of $152 million (-$2.64/share), driven largely by a loss on the Boston life science loan that was assigned back to its non-recourse lender; distributable earnings before realized losses and strategic review expenses were $5 million ($0.09/share), covering the $0.10 dividend only before those items. Book value stood at $10.14/share. Management flagged more challenging liquidity and valuations, said some asset sales previously expected before year-end will likely slip into 1H 2027, and warned reserves could increase near term. Positives: $2.4 billion of year-to-date repayments (above the $2 billion expectation), $853 million of liquidity, and leverage cut to 3.1x from 4.3x; the strategic review continues with no further commentary. No formal guidance was given beyond qualitative direction on originations, leverage and reserves.

Q3 2026 total revenue fell 3% and net income fell 5% versus a prior-year period that included the Watercrest sale, while operating income rose 16%. Hospitality revenue hit a third-quarter record $66 million, up 9%, with hotel revenue up 7% and club revenue up 14%. Nine-month revenue rose 8%, net income 7%, and operating income 26%, and the board raised the quarterly dividend 13% to $0.18 per share. Buybacks totaled $27.2 million in the quarter and $64.9 million year-to-date (up 161%), leaving shares outstanding at roughly 56.6 million, the lowest in nearly 30 years.

Kinross delivered Q3 production of 425,000 oz at cost of sales of $1,485/oz and AISC of $1,947/oz, with adjusted EPS of $0.50 and Q3 adjusted operating cash flow of $831 million; margins were approximately $2,750/oz. Guidance was reaffirmed rather than raised: Q4 production of 430,000-450,000 oz supports full-year 1.84-1.86 Moz at updated AISC of $1,850-$1,900/oz, and 2027 production is also expected at 1.84-1.86 Moz. The quarter follows a September guidance update driven by La Coipa and Round Mountain; Round Mountain mill recovery improved to 60% from 44% sequentially and La Coipa has stabilized after weather and high copper grade issues. Return of capital was accelerated with 8.6 million shares repurchased for $230 million, and GenGold flagged Great Bear capital will exceed the PEA figure.

KBR reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of ~$2.03B, up 5% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up $28M to $268M (13.2% margin, +80 bps) and adjusted EPS of $1.12 (+10%). Sustainable Tech revenue rose 26% to $762M on record backlog of $5.8B (up >50% YoY, 1.3x book-to-bill), though its segment margin fell to 19.3% from 21.2% on a tougher LNG JV comparison; Mission Tech revenue fell 5% to $1.27B on NASA insourcing but margins expanded 110 bps to 11.5%. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed on all metrics, while management flagged ~$25M-$50M of cash flow that could slip past year-end on Middle East collections and a larger NASA insourcing headwind for 2027.

KB Financial reported Q3 net profit of KRW 1,907.5 billion and cumulative Q3 net profit of KRW 5,792.1 billion, up 13.1% YoY, with cumulative ROE of 13.89% (+1.1pp YoY). Group NIM contracted 2 bps QoQ to 1.92% (bank 1.72%) on funding cost pressure, while net interest income rose 11.6% QoQ to KRW 3,507 billion and cumulative non-interest income grew 27.3% YoY to KRW 4,758.8 billion, though net fee income fell 29.7% QoQ on lower trading volume. Credit cost was 43 bps in Q3 (40 bps cumulative), with full-year guidance kept in the mid-40 bp range, and the BOD approved a Q3 dividend of KRW 1,167 per share (+25.5% YoY). Management guided Q4 asset-yield repricing and NIM rebound, but flagged continued fee income slowdown and conservative provisioning ahead.

Invitation Homes reported Q3 FY2026 same-store NOI growth of 1.1% and core revenue growth of 1.6%, with blended rent growth of 3.0% (renewals +4.3%, new leases -0.2%) and core FFO per share of $0.48, up 2.4% YoY. Management raised full-year 2026 core FFO guidance by a penny at the midpoint to $1.94-$1.98 and lifted same-store NOI growth guidance to a 1.2% midpoint, while lowering same-store expense growth guidance by 30 bps on favorable property taxes. Buybacks totaled roughly $989 million (about 37 million shares, 6% of shares outstanding) at an average $26.78, funded largely by disposition proceeds, and the board authorized a new $500 million repurchase program. October preliminary blended rent growth moderated to 2.2% and new lease rents fell to -2.2%, with management citing seasonal patterns and flagging watch items around shadow supply and elevated mortgage rates.

L3Harris reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $6.1B, up 7% YoY (organic +9% despite one fewer week), GAAP EPS of $3.28 (+33%), operating margin of 13% (+200 bps), and free cash flow of $1.3B (+195%). Bookings of $19.3B drove a 3.2x book-to-bill and backlog of $53.2B, up 27% sequentially and 47% YoY, led by $11B in PAC-3 and THAAD awards. FY2026 revenue guidance was raised at the bottom end to $23.5-23.7B and EPS raised to $12.25-$12.35 from $11.80-$12, with segment margin reaffirmed at low 16% and FCF held at $3B. The 2028 framework was reaffirmed on organic growth (8%) but segment margin was trimmed to ~16% from 16.3% and 2028 FCF cut to $3B from $3.5B, citing cash-funding of 401(k) contributions, lower margin, and CapEx timing.

Royalty revenue rose 51% YoY to $70.3 million, with legacy royalties up 25% to $58.1 million and XOMA-acquired assets adding $12.3 million since the July 14 close. Adjusted diluted EPS was $2.67 versus $3.09 a year ago, which had included $24.5 million of one-time ZELSUVMI out-license income; GAAP was a net loss of $1.43 per share on $35 million of one-time XOMA transaction and integration costs. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was reaffirmed (royalty $225-250 million, total $270-310 million) while adjusted diluted EPS guidance was raised to $9.50-$9.75 from $9.00-$9.50. Management noted Q4 revenue will be weighted more heavily due to a full quarter of XOMA royalties and tiered royalty step-ups, and deferred an updated five-year outlook to the December 8 Investor Day.

Mastercard reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue growth of 14% and net income growth of 18% on a non-GAAP currency-neutral basis, with EPS up 21% to $5.31 (including a $0.16 benefit from buybacks). Revenue came in above expectations on broad-based strength plus timing of services projects and payment network deals pulled from Q4 into Q3, a shift management said would reverse in Q4. Guidance was maintained, not raised: full-year 2026 revenue growth seen at the high end of low double digits (in line with the prior expectation set in Q2), with Q4 also at the high end of low double digits, opex growth at the high end of low double digits, and a ~1 PPT FX tailwind for the year. GDV grew 7%, cross-border volume 11%, switched transactions 9%, and value-added services revenue 19%; $3 billion of stock was repurchased in the quarter.

Linde reported record Q3 FY2026 sales of $9.4 billion (up 9% YoY, 5% underlying), operating profit of $2.8 billion (up 8%) and EPS of $4.59 (up 9%). Operating margin of 29.4% fell 30 bps YoY and was flat excluding cost pass-through, with gas segment gains offset by engineering and Global Other. Q4 EPS guidance of $4.40-$4.50 (5%-7% growth) implies roughly a 3% sequential decline versus the Q3 actual, with no economic improvement assumed and no meaningful Lincare profit change embedded; the full-year guide of $17.82-$17.92 simply rolls Q4 into year-to-date. The company recorded a $425 million restructuring charge and is evaluating strategic alternatives for Lincare, which cost about 2% of YTD EPS growth.

Q3 revenue fell 5.1% to ~$3.3 billion with parts and services organic revenue down 5.4%; GAAP diluted EPS was a loss of $0.09 (including $111M of impairments) versus $0.69 prior year, and adjusted EPS was $0.50 versus $0.84. Europe organic revenue fell 9.8% with segment EBITDA margin of 4.6% versus 10.0%, a $94M year-over-year EBITDA decline, of which ~$43M was attributed to the German ERP disruption and ~$95M of quarterly revenue loss. North America organic revenue fell 2.4% but EBITDA margin expanded 40 bps to 14.4% on a 42.3% gross margin; Specialty grew 0.9% organically with margin down ~180 bps to 5.5%. The company suspended full-year 2026 guidance, replaced the CEO (Sal Abbate effective December 15), engaged Alvarez & Marsal on Europe, and suspended the strategic review including the Specialty sales process.

Revenue grew 39% YoY in Q3 FY2026, with Mounjaro and Zepbound together posting over $16 billion (up $6 billion YoY) and key products outside cardiometabolic doubling. Non-GAAP EPS was $7.48 including $4.57 of acquired IPR&D charges versus $7.02 a year ago, gross margin rose 80 bps to 84.4%, and non-GAAP performance margin expanded 5.9 points to 54.2%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $91-92 billion and non-GAAP EPS to $35-36, an increase of $4.07 per share at the midpoint. The quarter included approximately $900 million of one-time items, and the 2026 revenue base benefited from roughly $2 billion of one-time items not expected to recur in 2027.

Cheniere reported Q3 2026 consolidated adjusted EBITDA of approximately $1.9 billion, distributable cash flow of approximately $1.2 billion, and net income of approximately $1.2 billion, with record quarterly production of 188 cargoes (684 TBtu), up about 17% year-over-year.
