For the third consecutive quarter, the company raised full-year 2026 guidance, increasing consolidated adjusted EBITDA to $8.75-$9.25 billion and DCF to $6.05-$6.55 billion, representing a $850 million and $750 million increase, respectively. The company also announced a 12% dividend increase to $0.625 per quarter, signed long-term SPAs with QatarEnergy (4 MTPA) and Petrobras (0.8 MTPA), and completed the seventh train of Corpus Christi Stage 3 ahead of schedule and on budget. Preliminary 2027 production guidance is 56-58 million tons, with approximately 52 million tons under long-term contracts.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 14.2% to $893.5M with comparable center revenue up 8.7%, above expectations, and adjusted EBITDA up 16.5% to $256.3M at a 28.7% margin (up 60 bps). Adjusted net income rose 24.6% to $115.9M, though GAAP net income grew only 4% to $106.5M against prior-year employee retention credit and sale-leaseback gains. Management raised full-year comparable center revenue guidance to 8.5%-8.7% from 7.9%-8.3%, raised revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, and lifted the EBITDA margin midpoint to 28.4%. Q4 margin guidance steps down slightly on pre-opening costs for seven new clubs and a lower-margin in-center mix.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 55% to $62 million in Q3 2026 from $40 million a year ago, on higher watching prices and lower costs that more than offset lower volumes from the completed turnaround; TTM adjusted EBITDA now exceeds $220 million. Free cash flow through nine months was roughly $74 million after $58 million of sustaining capital, with $200 million+ of cash and ~1.1x net leverage. Management guided to another strong Q4 citing Tampa ammonia at $545/ton, NOLA UAN around $390/ton, and gas near $3/MMBtu, and said it expects to add ~$15 million of run-rate EBITDA improvement by end-2026 toward a $55 million target, plus $25-30 million annually from CCS once operational. No formal guidance range was issued.

Lloyds reported Q3 FY2026 statutory profit after tax of GBP 4.8bn YTD on net income of GBP 14.8bn, up 9% YoY, with Q3 net income up 2% QoQ and NII up 3% YoY. NIM was 325bps, up 3bps QoQ, and the year-to-date cost/income ratio was 49.3% (Q3 47.2%) on costs of GBP 7.2bn, up 1%. Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated (NII >GBP 14.9bn, costs <GBP 9.9bn, AQR ~25bps, ROTE >16%, capital generation >200bps, CET1 ~13%), with NII now expected modestly above GBP 14.9bn, though management flagged 2027 NII growth lower than 2026 amid competitive deposit and asset markets.

Pre-revenue developer with no revenue or EPS to report; Q3 balance-sheet and execution update. Cash ended Q3 at $22 million, with total liquidity of $40.5 million including $18.3 million undrawn on the Taurus bridge, available until November 29 conditional on the joint financial model and framework agreement amendment. Nine-month operating cash outflow was $7.8 million (a ~$1.3 million improvement), investing outflows $24 million and financing inflows $34 million, with no financing in Q3; E&E assets rose from $104 million to $272 million, reflecting capitalized Kabanga spend and bridge-loan interest. Management gave no numeric guidance but said it is in advanced negotiations with the Orion Critical Mineral Consortium on a just-over-$500 million equity raise into KNL, with debt project financing upwards of $800 million, commercial terms concluded and final legal processes remaining.

Insmed reported Q3 FY2026 BRINSUPRI revenue of $400.1 million, up 29% sequentially, crossing $1 billion in its first four full quarters, plus ARIKAYCE revenue of $124.4 million (+9% YoY). Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both products: BRINSUPRI to $1.35-1.4 billion (a $100 million increase to the low end, $50 million to the midpoint) and ARIKAYCE to $460-470 million (a $10 million increase to the low end). Cost of product revenues fell to 14.9% of revenues from 20.6% a year ago on BRINSUPRI's gross margin contribution, while combined R&D and SG&A rose 40% YoY; cash was about $1.1 billion with a line of sight to cash flow positivity in 2027. The company will stop providing specific BRINSUPRI launch metrics now that it is past the first year, and CFO Sara Bonstein is departing.

MAA reported Q3 2026 core FFO of $2.10 per diluted share, in line with guidance, but same-store revenue came in about $0.02 light on weaker new lease pricing and modestly lower average occupancy, partly offset by $0.02 of favorable expenses. Full-year core FFO guidance midpoint was cut $0.04 to $8.49 (range $8.43-$8.55), with same-store revenue growth midpoint lowered 35 bps to -0.25%, effective rent growth midpoint cut 20 bps to -0.1%, average occupancy midpoint down 10 bps to 95.4%, and same-store NOI growth midpoint reduced 35 bps to -1.25%. Blended lease-over-lease was up only 10 bps versus Q3 2025, with new lease pricing around -6% for the quarter, though management cited improving October trends and positive November/December pre-leasing as recovery now developing roughly one quarter later than originally expected. Q4 core FFO guidance was set at $2.12-$2.24 ($2.18 midpoint).

Q3 revenue of $492M was down ~2% YoY versus guidance for a 2%-5% decline, helped by EyeQ units at the high end (9.5M) and SuperVision deliveries above 15,000 units. FY revenue guidance midpoint was raised $13M to ~$2.008B (5%-7% growth) and adjusted operating income to $400M from $395M, but the Q4 outlook implies revenue down ~8.5% sequentially and adjusted operating income of ~$60M versus $89M in Q3. Adjusted operating margin rose ~3 points to 18%, largely on $51M of Israeli R&D credit, while SuperVision volume and zero-margin memory pass-through cut gross margin by ~100 bps. Management spent much of the call defending the VW/CARIAD relationship and explained that a demoware-focused approach had cost near-term nominations.

Q3 revenue was $16.5 billion with non-GAAP EPS of $0.52 versus $0.38 guidance and non-GAAP gross margin of 44.1%, roughly 200 bps above guidance, marking an eighth consecutive quarter above financial expectations. DCAI revenue was $7.3 billion, up 17% sequentially and nearly 80% year over year with 42% operating margin, while CCPG fell 9% sequentially to $8.1 billion on memory-driven PC weakness. Q4 guidance is $15-16 billion revenue, 38% gross margin and $0.25 EPS, including a roughly $300 million revenue and 200 bps gross margin hit from the Fab 28 Israel incident, with CCPG guided down more than 20% sequentially. Management expects 2026 PC unit TAM down about 12% and 2027 down roughly 10%, while server CPU units grow more than 30% in both years, and stated 2027 will likely not produce positive free cash flow given a strong CapEx step-up.

Howmet reported Q3 revenue of $2.7 billion, up 29% (25% organic, called the strongest quarterly growth on record), EBITDA of $879 million up 43% at a 32.5% margin (+310 bps YoY, +40 bps QoQ) with 43% incrementals, and EPS of $1.46 up 54%. Management said revenue, EBITDA margin and EPS all exceeded the high end of prior guidance, raised full-year guidance to $10.3 billion revenue, $3.33 billion EBITDA, $5.50 EPS and $2 billion free cash flow, and gave a Q4 guide of ~$2.75 billion revenue and $1.50 EPS. Initial 2027 outlook calls for 12% growth (+/-0.5%) to approximately $11.5 billion, and the board added $5 billion to the buyback authorization. IGT growth accelerated to 45% and management now expects IGT sales to double in three years (versus a prior three-to-five) and reach ~$2.5 billion, 2.5x 2025, by decade-end.

Ingram Micro reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $15.22 billion, up 20.8% YoY (21.2% FX neutral), with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.91, up 26% and $0.09 above the high end of guidance; results exceeded the high end of every guidance metric. Gross margin fell 35 bps to 6.55% on GPU/AI infrastructure mix, but adjusted operating margin rose 7 bps to 2.12% on OpEx leverage to 4.62% of sales, and adjusted free cash flow was a $250 million inflow versus a $110 million outflow a year ago. Q4 guidance was raised to net sales of $17.5-17.9 billion (about 19% growth at midpoint, on a 53-week year), gross profit of $1.08-1.12 billion, and non-GAAP EPS of $1.05-1.15, with the full-year 2026 outlook also raised versus the September Capital Markets Day framework. GPU and AI infrastructure sales reached more than $1.8 billion in the quarter, up nearly 160% from about $700 million a year ago, and remain lumpy by quarter.

HDMC revenue fell 10% to $964M and Q3 EPS was $0.40 versus $3.10, though the prior-year figure was inflated by a $301M HDFS credit-loss release; HDMC gross margin expanded 173 bps to 28.1% and adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 9.7% from 8.7%. North America retail rose 9% (accelerating from 3%) and global retail rose 5% to ~35,800 units, while wholesale shipments fell 8% to 33,600 units and dealer inventory fell ~26% year-over-year. Full-year guidance was raised: HDMC retail and wholesale to 135,500-139,000 units (from 133,500-138,500), HDMC operating income to $25M-$55M (from $10M-$50M) and HDFS to $60M-$70M (from $55M-$70M), with capex cut to $140M-$165M. Offsets include a higher full-year gross tariff estimate of ~$105M-$120M (from $75M-$90M, though recoveries net to roughly no operating income change), a 5% EMEA retail decline, LiveWire's going-concern disclosure and withdrawn guidance, and a commitment unchanged to $350M HDMC EBITDA in 2027.

GoDaddy reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.3 billion, up 6% and above the high end of guidance, with bookings up 6% to $1.4 billion and normalized EBITDA margin up ~120 bps to over 33%. Applications & Commerce grew 9% to $524 million while Core Platform grew 4% to $818 million; ARR rose 5% to $4.5 billion and free cash flow was $481 million (TTM $1.8 billion). Full-year revenue is guided toward the higher end of the $5.215-$5.255 billion range, with EBITDA margin over 33% and FCF ~$1.8 billion reaffirmed; Q4 bookings growth is expected to accelerate and be slightly ahead of revenue. The key change is Airo, whose annualized bookings more than doubled to over $100 million and turned incrementally additive to bookings, though management flagged future gross-margin deterioration from Airo and industry discounting.

Q3 FY2026 revenue of $114.3M came in above the $112-114M guidance range, up 9.7% YoY and 5.7% sequentially. Non-GAAP EBITDA hit a record $22.9M (20% of revenue) versus $16.5-17.5M guidance, with gross margin expanding ~370 bps sequentially to 40.6% non-GAAP. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.18 versus $0.11 in Q2 and $0.09 a year ago. Management guided Q4 revenue to $113.5-115.5M and EBITDA to $20-22M, and stated an expectation to return to double-digit growth in 2027.

GFL reported Q3 revenue up 27% YoY (5.7% price, ~19% M&A including Frontier and SECURE, volumes slightly negative on a CAD 13M contract exit), adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.5% (30 bps above expectations, ~flat YoY), underlying margin expansion of 125 bps, and adjusted free cash flow of $272.5M, up over 50% YoY and 15% above guide. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for the third time, to revenue of $8.055-8.075B, adjusted EBITDA of $2.49-2.495B, adjusted free cash flow of $1.02B, and margin of 30.9% (up 40 bps from prior guide). Volume outlook remains cautious with Q4 deceleration expected, and elevated diesel (~$125M incremental cost, >60% YoY) weighed on margins, while the SECURE integration and a special committee strategic review with a November 9 bidder deadline remain in focus.

Base business product sales rose 16% YoY to $8.2 billion (highest growth since 2015), with total product sales of $8.3 billion up 13% YoY; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.55 versus $2.47, though excluding a prior-year $0.25 IP-sale benefit EPS grew 15%. HIV sales grew 18% YoY to $6.2 billion on demand, price, and favorable inventory, TRODELVY rose 42% to $506 million, and Livdelzi rose 93% to $203 million, while cell therapy fell 18% on competitive headwinds. Full-year base business sales guidance was raised to $30.7-$31.0 billion, up $900 million at the midpoint versus August guidance and $1.65 billion versus initial 2026 guidance, with total product sales of $31.0-$31.3 billion. Management flagged a completed CMS maximum fair price for BIKTARVY that will hit revenue in 2028, a partial clinical hold on KITE-753 (PALISADES) over grade 3/4 ICANS, and a clinical hold on GS-3107.

Garrett reported Q3 sales of $930 million, up 3% year over year, with adjusted EBIT of $152 million and a 16.3% margin (up 160 bps including a 70 bp FX drag), and adjusted free cash flow of $136 million at 89% conversion. The company reaffirmed its Q2 midpoint outlook, narrowing ranges to net sales of $3.8 billion, adjusted EBIT of $580 million, and adjusted free cash flow of $430 million, with operational improvements offset by FX headwinds in Q4. Industrial sales are now expected at $230 million in 2026 and about $300 million in 2027, and the board authorized a new $250 million repurchase program for 2027. Light vehicle declined on China domestic weakness and tariff pass-throughs, and management was non-committal on 2027 automotive mix and HVAC timing.

Granite reported record Q3 revenue up 23% to $1.8 billion and record adjusted EBITDA of $283 million (up $67 million), with construction gross margin up 210 bps and full segment revenue up 27%. Management raised the low end of 2026 revenue guidance to $5.4-$5.5 billion and refined 2027 organic growth to 10%-12%, while keeping all other 2026 guidance assumptions and laying out 2029 targets of 14%-16% EBITDA margin. Materials gross margin fell 420 bps on higher energy costs recovered via surcharges, and $569 million of tactical infrastructure work was pushed from Q2 2027 to Q3 2028. Total CAP reached a record $7.5 billion with federal at $1.3 billion and mission-critical at $331 million.

Hyatt reported Q3 FY2026 system-wide RevPAR growth of 7.2%, above expectations, with U.S. RevPAR up 8.2% and gross fees up 15.2% to $327 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose more than 19% year-over-year adjusted for asset sales, and the company raised its full-year RevPAR outlook to 5%-5.5% and its capital returns target to $375-$425 million, while full-year fee guidance of $1.32-$1.335 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $1.17-$1.20 billion imply growth of 10%-11% and 14%-17% respectively. Offsets included weakness in the Distribution segment, which declined and missed expectations, a $20 million full-year fee impact from Mexico and $10 million from the Middle East, and fourth-quarter U.S. RevPAR expected to moderate on tougher comparisons and midterm elections.

Q3 FY2026 contract sales fell 11% to $807 million, well below the mid-single-digit decline management had guided, with VPG down 12% to ~$3,400; tours grew 2% to 236,000. Total revenues before cost reimbursements were flat at $1.3 billion and adjusted EBITDA to shareholders rose 4% to $313 million at a 25% margin, but that included a $55 million provision-methodology benefit from the 12.5% provision (vs 16.8% prior year). Management cut full-year EBITDA guidance to $1,165-$1,180 million from $1,225-$1,265 million and now expects contract sales down mid-single digits for the year with VPG down high-single digits. Positives include 16% financing revenue growth, 69% resort/club margins, and continued $110 million of buybacks toward a $600 million annual goal.

HII reported record Q3 FY2026 sales of ~$3.5B (up 10.8% YoY) and diluted EPS of $5.48 versus $3.68 a year ago. Shipbuilding revenue of $2.8B rose 13.9% YoY, ahead of guidance, with segment operating margin expanding to 7.4% from 5.6%. Management raised 2026 shipbuilding revenue guidance to $10.5-10.7B and raised Mission Technologies margin expectations to ~6% operating / ~9% EBITDA, while reiterating shipbuilding margin of 6.0-6.5% and free cash flow of $500-600M. Awards totaled $32.4B, lifting backlog to $86.2B, excluding the $5.1B CVN-75 RCOH to be booked in Q4.

Management explicitly stated Q3 was below expectations, with North America failing to strengthen and Europe remaining challenging; the CFO cited cold/flu consumption down high single digits (40-50 bps group impact) and a Centrum OTC raw material classification issue in China (~50 bps group impact). The full-year guidance was described by the CEO as 'a disappointment,' with the China Centrum OTC issue assumed to persist through 2027 and a pulled-forward Brazil go-to-market change adding a Q4 drag. The profit/margin guide was held (CFO comfortable with consensus margin for the year), and a share buyback was announced alongside leverage near the ~2.5x target. The 4%-6% medium-term growth guidance was retained despite acknowledging the company has not delivered it for a couple of years.

Heritage reported Q3 2026 net income of $51.1 million, or $1.72 per diluted share, up 5.5% from $50.4 million/$1.63, on revenue up 3.2% to $219.2 million, despite $15.8 million of pre-tax catastrophe losses versus none a year ago. Net premiums earned rose 5.4% to $205.6 million as the ceded premium ratio fell 4.4 points to 41.7% on the June reinsurance program, while the net combined ratio was roughly flat at 73.0% versus 72.9%. Gross premiums written fell 3.1% to $322.8 million as Florida commercial residential pricing pressure cut that book's premium in force about 16% YoY; management guided to only single-digit top-line growth and expects Florida commercial renewal rates to fall another 10-18% next year. Book value per share reached $20.22, up 42.9% YoY, with YTD repurchases of 1.1 million shares for $27.9 million.

ING reported Q3 2026 total income up 6% year on year, driven by 13% growth in commercial NII and 9% growth in fee income, with EPS up 17% year on year and a 16% return on tangible equity. Management raised its 2027 outlook, guiding total income to exceed the original target by at least EUR 1 billion, opex around EUR 300 million below plan, and ROTE above 16%, at least 2 percentage points above the Capital Markets Day target. The quarter included EUR 403 million of risk costs, of which EUR 111 million was an IFRS model update, plus EUR 63 million of restructuring, and management announced roughly 400 Wholesale Banking redundancies with a EUR 175 million Q4 provision for EUR 75 million of annual savings from 2028. CET1 rose 30 basis points to 13.3% alongside a EUR 1.9 billion additional distribution, including a EUR 1.65 billion buyback.

Hershey's Q3 FY2026 was weak on the reported numbers: volume fell about 10% with pricing still up high-teens, and share accelerated in July-August before the tougher Reese's Oreo comparison hit in September. Management held the 2%-4% long-term sales algorithm for 2027 but said landing would be in the lower part of the range if consumer pressure persists, and the low-double-digit 2027 EPS framework is only reachable if freight, commodity, and consumer conditions improve — otherwise results could be short of the original range. Q4 gross margin implies an exit rate near 39%, with cocoa hedge timing cited as the bridge to meaningful 2027 margin improvement; C-store category weakness (-5%) persisted into October while other channels grew 3.7%.

HTGC reported Q3 2026 total investment income of $140.1 million (up 1.5% YoY, down QoQ) and net investment income of $87.3 million ($0.47/share), covering the base distribution 118%. Core investment income was $135.7 million (up 6.1% YoY), but Q3 prepayments of $148.3 million came in below the low end of guidance, driving the QoQ decline; management guides Q4 prepayments to normalize to $200-300 million and expects TII and NII to increase in Q4. Core yield was 11.9% (midpoint of guidance) with Q4 guided at 11.8-12%, and YTD records were set for originations ($3.44 billion, +20% YoY) and fundings ($1.93 billion, +9.9% YoY).

Marcus reported record quarterly revenue of $238M, up 13.1% YoY, with operating income of $30.3M (+33%) and adjusted EBITDA of $49.1M (+21%); net earnings were $18.8M or $0.60 per share versus $0.42 prior-year (which excluded a $0.10 insurance gain). Theatres revenue rose ~21% on 16.8% attendance growth and record summer box office, while hotels revenue rose 2% with RevPAR up 2.1% (7.4% on a comparable basis) and segment EBITDA down $0.6M, including an estimated $0.5M storm impact at Grand Geneva. No formal EPS or revenue guidance was issued; CapEx guidance was reiterated at $45-50M, and hotel group pace is ~5% behind for 2026 but ~10% ahead for 2027. The quarter beat on revenue records in both divisions, but theatre admissions trailed the national box office on a mix-adjusted basis and the hotel segment's EBITDA declined.

ICE reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $2.02, up 18% year-over-year, on net revenues of $2.8 billion, up 15%, with adjusted operating income up 19% to $1.7 billion. Recurring revenues hit a record $1.4 billion (+7%) and transaction revenues grew 23%, led by Exchanges net revenue of $1.5 billion (+22%) and energy, interest rate, and ag/metal transaction growth of 26%, 48%, and 62%, respectively. Guidance was raised at the top of prior ranges for full-year exchange recurring revenue (approximately 9%) and FIDS recurring revenue (approximately 8%), while Q4 adjusted opex of $1.082-$1.092 billion places full-year expenses at the top end of the July range. Mortgage Technology grew 4%, but Q4 transaction revenues are expected to decline year-over-year on elevated rates, and the MarketAxess deal close is now expected in Q1 2027 after DOJ approval.

IDACORP reported Q3 2026 diluted EPS of $2.73 versus $2.26 a year ago, with nine-month EPS of $5.76 versus $5.13, driven by roughly $44 million of higher retail revenues and about $12 million of incremental large-contract-customer operating income (industrial revenues up 27%). Management raised full-year EPS guidance to $6.40-$6.50 (up $0.10 at the bottom, $0.05 at the top) and cut expected additional tax credit amortization to under $10 million from under $15 million. Customer count rose 2.2% and the preliminary 2027 IRP load CAGR is 8.9% (about 19,000 GWh in 2027 to about 29,000 GWh by 2032). Q4 call will carry an updated, likely higher CapEx forecast, and management signaled a June 2027 rate case filing is likely but still being modeled.

Revenue of $193.4M beat the $154-158M guidance range and rose 17% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $131.3M vs $86-92M guided and non-GAAP EPS of $3.11 vs $1.94-2.13 guided, all above the high end. The upside was driven by a new top-PC-manufacturer license (with final value set via arbitration) and included $36.2M of catch-up revenue; CE/IoT/auto revenue nearly doubled to $55.7M and ARR hit a record $629M. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed above the prior $810M midpoint on existing contracts alone, with Q4 revenue guided to $154-160M and a dividend raise to $0.75. Enforcement wins (Brazil injunction vs TCL, two UPC injunctions vs Disney) are additive but excluded from guidance.

Illumina reported Q3 revenue of $1.17 billion, up 4.7% YoY on a rest-of-world organic basis, with sequencing consumables of $792 million up 6% and clinical consumables up 14%. Non-GAAP operating margin was 25%, 100 bps above guidance, and diluted EPS of $1.44 beat the high end of guidance and rose 7% YoY. The company raised FY2026 revenue guidance by $30 million at the midpoint to $4.64-4.66 billion and raised EPS guidance to $5.40-5.45, an increase of $0.08 at the midpoint. Q4 guidance implies revenue of $1.22-1.24 billion and EPS of $1.51-1.56, with research and applied consumables still expected to decline mid- to high-single digits.

ILPT reported Q3 2026 Normalized FFO of $21.3 million, or $0.32 per share, up 42% year-over-year, with same property NOI up 5.7% and cash basis NOI up 1.9%. The company raised full-year 2026 NOI guidance at the midpoint by $2 million to $363-364 million and narrowed Normalized FFO per share guidance to $1.23-$1.25, which includes $0.13 of incentive management fees. Leasing totaled 645,000 sq ft at GAAP rents 163% above prior rents with a term of nearly 16 years, and consolidated occupancy reached 98.3%, up 420 bps year-over-year. All debt is now fixed at a 5.48% weighted average rate with no maturities until 2029, though leverage remains elevated at 11.6x.

First Internet Bancorp reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $43.9 million, up 7% sequentially, with net income of $4.8 million or $0.54 per diluted share and adjusted EPS of $0.57, more than double last quarter. NIM expanded 8 bps to 2.47% (2.55% FTE) and adjusted pre-provision net revenue rose 14% sequentially to $17.1 million. Management guided Q4 EPS to roughly $1.02-$1.07, NIM to 2.75%-2.80% and provision to $7.5-$8 million, assuming a 25 bp Fed hike in December. A single franchise finance relationship drove $2.6 million of specific reserves and $600,000 of reversed interest, cutting pre-tax earnings by about $3.2 million or $0.29 per share, while delinquencies fell to 48 bps from 78 bps.

Incyte reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $1.56 billion, up 14% YoY, with total net sales of $1.32 billion also up 14%. Jakafi franchise sales were $827 million, up 4% (demand up 12%), while core business ex-Jakafi rose 30% to $490 million and OPZELURA net sales grew 36% to $255 million (21% pro forma). Management raised full-year 2026 total net sales guidance to $5.210-$5.300 billion, along with raises for OPZELURA ($1.1-$1.12 billion) and hematology/oncology ($890-$910 million), while maintaining opex guidance. GAAP expenses rose 146% to $2.27 billion on a $1.23 billion IPR&D charge from the ~$1.27 billion Vega Therapeutics acquisition, and pipeline news included deprioritizing CDK2 667 in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (halting MAESTRA-2 enrollment).

Green Brick delivered 978 homes (+2.6% YoY) but home closing revenue fell 9.8% to $437M on a 12.1% ASP decline to ~$447K, and net income dropped 24% to $59.2M with EPS of $1.35. Homebuilding gross margin contracted 410 bps to 28% as incentives rose 180 bps to 9.9% of closing revenue, while SG&A climbed 40 bps to 11.8% of revenue; backlog fell 6.8% YoY to 629 homes with backlog ASP down 11%. Net orders rose 3.1% to 926 on a 5.8% larger community count, though monthly pace slipped to 2.8 from 2.9 and cancellations rose to 8.2% from 6.7%. Management cut 2026 planned land investment to $780M from $850M previously, with no formal EPS or margin guidance issued.

AXIS reported Q3 FY2026 gross written premiums of $2.4 billion, up 11% YoY, with net income of $202 million ($2.75 per diluted share) and operating income of $229 million ($3.12 per share), producing a 15.7% annualized operating ROE. The combined ratio deteriorated to 94.0% from 89.4%, driven by higher catastrophe and war losses ($75 million, 4.6 points) and a 1.9-point rise in the insurance attritional loss ratio to 54.2%. Management guided full-year reinsurance premiums down low double digits, a Q4 acquisition expense ratio proxy of 22%, and net investment income around $200 million, while declining to provide 2027 growth guidance amid softening property and casualty markets.

Q3 FY2026 read from the Q&A transcript only (prepared remarks and figures not included), so hard numbers are largely qualitative. Management cited strong gross profit delivery that came in above Street modeling and drove an EPS beat, funded by volume/operating leverage, productivity and favorable cacao timing; the full-year EPS and top-line outlook were maintained, with upside reinvested into A&C. Europe posted positive volume mix of 1.6 points despite a 1% weather drag, North America grew share and volume, and management reiterated confidence in strong EPS growth in 2027 on volume-led growth and productivity, though it declined to guide 2027 sales. Cacao fundamentals were described as a ~500,000-ton surplus for 2025/26 versus the 2024 spike, while freight, dairy, oil and packaging inflation are rising.

Textron reported Q3 FY2026 revenues of $3.8 billion (up 4% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.76 (up from $1.55), driven by strong performance in Textron Aviation ($1.7B revenue, +14%) and Textron Systems (+16%). Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EPS to $6.55-$6.65 and manufacturing cash flow to $800M-$900M, citing lower CapEx and strong Q3 order activity at Aviation. The Industrial segment separation remains on track with a 12-18 month timeline.

Telesat reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of CAD 81 million and adjusted EBITDA of CAD 12 million, with results described as in-line with expectations. Management reiterated full-year GEO guidance but lowered the LEO CapEx forecast to CAD 1.1-1.3 billion from the prior range of CAD 1.3-1.5 billion due to a three-month delay in global service launch timing. The company maintains compliance with financial covenants while navigating debt refinancing discussions and structural declines in its GEO segment.

Trane Technologies reported Q3 FY2026 enterprise organic revenue growth of 16% and adjusted EPS growth of 25% (excluding a $0.10 tax benefit). Management raised its full-year organic revenue guidance to approximately 11% while reaffirming the EPS range of $15.20-$15.30, citing robust backlog and strong pipeline. The quarter was driven by exceptional performance in Americas Commercial HVAC and Applied Solutions, though price realization faced some headwinds from timing and mix.

TotalEnergies reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with adjusted net income of $9.1 billion and cash flow of $12.3 billion, driven by record refining margins averaging $33/barrel and high commodity prices. Management raised full-year 2026 free cash flow guidance to a range of $42-$43 billion and confirmed the interim dividend at EUR 0.90/share while reiterating a commitment to return 40% of cash flow to shareholders via dividends and buybacks.

Tradeweb reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $585 million, a 14.9% year-over-year increase, marking the second-highest quarterly revenue in company history. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded by 57 basis points to 54.5%, driven by strong growth across rates (18%), credit, and equities despite higher interest rate volatility. Management raised adjusted expense guidance for FY2026 to $1.155-$1.175 billion while maintaining a positive outlook on margin expansion.

Titan reported Q3 revenue of $454 million and adjusted EBITDA of $28 million, both consistent with guidance despite a cyclical downturn in end markets. Management highlighted the sale of the ITM Undercarriage business to reduce debt and focus on core wheel and tire growth, while noting that agricultural segment sales declined 12% due to elevated costs and sluggish activity in Brazil. Full-year 2026 guidance was revised to revenue of $1.85 billion-$1.87 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $91 million-$101 million inclusive of ITM.

Twilio reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.56 billion (up 20% reported, 16% organic) and record non-GAAP income from operations of $326 million. Management raised full-year 2026 organic revenue growth guidance to 15% and full-year 2026 non-GAAP income from operations to $1.19-$1.2 billion. The company also provided a preliminary outlook for FY2027, projecting at least 10% organic revenue growth and non-GAAP income from operations of at least $1.35 billion.

Tyler Technologies reported Q3 FY2026 results with 11% recurring revenue growth and SaaS revenue growth of 21.2%. Operating margins expanded by 150 basis points to record quarterly free cash flow of $277 million. Management noted that full-year SaaS guidance was lowered slightly due to timing shifts in large deals, though the total sales number remains consistent with prior expectations.

Net revenue grew 20% YoY to $131 million with adjusted EBITDA of $71 million and margin expanding ~1,000 bps to 54%; adjusted diluted EPS was $0.45, up 25% YoY. Options ADV rose 15% with market share of 17.4% (up from 16.5% last quarter), but RPC stepped down to $0.098 from $0.124 in Q2 and $0.11 in Q1 on fee changes, ORF, and mix. Guidance: full-year adjusted opex lowered to $254-257 million from a prior $260-270 million range, with several other metrics narrowed. New-product traction (Bloomberg futures via NinjaTrader, fertilizer contracts) is early and immaterial to Q3 results.

UFP Industries reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.73 billion, an 11% year-over-year increase driven by volume growth and pricing, though Adjusted EBITDA declined to $119 million due to elevated transportation costs and losses from new operations. Management maintained its full-year guidance unchanged despite macro headwinds in residential construction and soft demand in certain segments. The company highlighted strong performance in Deckorators and Packaging but noted continued challenges with freight rates and material costs.

Third quarter revenue was $1.15 billion at the high end of guidance, while Adjusted EBITDA of $123 million and non-GAAP EPS of $1.01 both exceeded the top end of guidance. Management raised full-year outlooks for Brigit revenue growth to approximately 35% and narrowed ranges across all consolidated metrics including EPS. The company generated $121 million in free cash flow, more than double the prior year, while reducing net leverage to 2.4 times.

Univest reported Q3 net income of $21.6 million ($0.78/share), which was negatively impacted by a $14.4 million charge-off on a commercial lending relationship. Excluding this one-off, core operations remained solid with fee income up 6.3% and NII growing 10.5% YoY, though the company maintained its full-year loan growth guidance of 2%-3% despite a shift in lending philosophy that reduced mortgage and CRE holdings.

VICI reported Q3 FY2026 AFFO per share of $0.62, a 4.3% increase year-over-year, driven by a 5.8% revenue growth and successful refinancing that reduced the all-in interest rate by nearly 15 basis points. Management raised full-year 2026 AFFO guidance to between $2.47 and $2.48 per share, citing strong underlying demand in Las Vegas and continued portfolio diversification with four new tenants added in 2026. The company also announced a new $2 billion stock buyback authorization as a capital allocation tool.

Vista reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.23 billion (up 75% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $841 million (up 78% YoY), driven by record production of 169,000 BOE/d (up 33% YoY). Management raised its 2027 production guidance to 185,000 barrels per day and reiterated a full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $3.3 billion at $80 Brent. The company strengthened its balance sheet with net leverage at 1.12x adjusted EBITDA and executed $55 million in share buybacks.

Vulcan Materials reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $707 million, representing a 5% year-over-year growth in underlying business excluding approximately $40 million in energy headwinds and prior divestitures. Management maintained full-year guidance near the midpoint despite these headwinds, citing resilient execution and disciplined cost control. The company closed on two bolt-on acquisitions during the quarter and expects to complete several more before year-end.

TriMas reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $178.7 million (up 7.7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.50 (up from $0.17), driven by strong Packaging growth while Specialty Products faced temporary throughput constraints at Norris Cylinder. Management reaffirmed full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $1.60-$1.70 but modestly raised the sales outlook to 4%-6% YoY, acknowledging that margin expansion will be slower in Q4 due to ongoing operational challenges and a less favorable product mix.

T. Rowe Price reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS of $2.86 and adjusted net revenue of $2 billion, representing a sequential increase but following significant net outflows of $28.3 billion driven by equity strategies and target date redemptions. Management anticipates sequential improvement in net flows for the fourth quarter as outflows moderate from Q3 levels, though they remain elevated relative to historical norms. The company highlighted strong performance in fixed income, alternatives, and its expanding ETF/SMA franchises while noting structural headwinds in active equity.

Trinity Industries reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 18% YoY and EPS of $0.27, though operating profit declined 19% due to lower gains on lease sales and higher SG&A. Management raised full-year secondary market gain expectations by roughly $20 million to a range of $180-$200 million while holding full-year EPS guidance at $2.20-$2.40. The company reaffirmed its view that 2026 is the cyclical low for industry deliveries, with projected annual deliveries below 25,000 units.

TPG reported GAAP net income of $100 million and after-tax distributable earnings of $265 million ($0.65 per share) for Q3 FY2026. Management raised full-year 2026 FRE margin guidance to approximately 48%, citing strong capital formation of $42 billion year-to-date and a robust realization pipeline. The company expects to raise more than $55 billion in total fundraising for the year, driven by broad-based momentum across private equity, credit, and real estate strategies.

Total revenues declined 5% year-over-year to $1.2 billion in Q3, driven by lower WSE volumes despite pricing improvements. Insurance cost ratio improved to 89%, and adjusted EPS of $0.94 beat internal expectations, though full-year guidance remains unchanged with revenue trending toward the bottom end of the range.

The Hanover Insurance Group reported Q3 FY2026 operating EPS of $5.15 and net written premium growth of 3.1%. The company achieved a combined ratio of 92.3% (85.5% excluding catastrophes), with all segments delivering favorable loss ratios and strong pricing power, particularly in Personal Lines where growth decelerated to 1.7% due to deliberate mix shifts toward higher-value accounts. Management raised full-year expectations, stating that outperformance on the combined ratio will cause the full-year result to clearly beat original guidance.

Tenet reported Q3 FY2026 net operating revenues of $5.6 billion and consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $1.355 billion, representing a 10% increase in adjusted EBITDA over the prior year. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $5.05-$5.2 billion, citing fundamental outperformance alongside one-time transition items from the Conifer transaction. The company highlighted strong same-store growth in total joint replacements and disciplined cost controls driving margin strength.

Teck reported strong Q3 FY2026 results with adjusted EBITDA doubling to CAD 2.3 billion and cash flow from operations reaching CAD 1.6 billion, driven by record copper prices averaging $6.40/lb and an impairment reversal of CAD 888 million at Trail Operations. Management lowered 2026 net cash unit cost guidance for both copper and zinc segments due to strong performance but maintained unchanged annual production guidance despite severe weather disruptions at Quebrada Blanca (QB) and a labor strike at Highland Valley. The company reiterated its merger timeline with Anglo American, expecting completion within 12-18 months of the September 2025 announcement.

Stryker reported Q3 FY2026 organic sales growth of 7.7%, with Adjusted EPS of $3.52 (up 10.3% YoY) and Adjusted Gross Margin expanding 40 bps to 65.4%. Management acknowledged that overall results fell short of expectations due to a market slowdown in hip and knee procedures, supply disruptions in peripheral vascular, and operational distractions from a cyber incident and SAP implementation. Consequently, the company revised its full-year guidance downward to expect organic net sales growth of 6.5%-7% and Adjusted EPS of $14.80-$14.90.

Supernus reported record Q3 2026 total revenue of $226.8 million, an 18% increase year-over-year, driven by growth products like Qelbree (net sales $91M) and ZURZUVAE ($42M collaboration revenue). The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue to $875-$900 million (from $860-$890 million) and non-GAAP operating earnings to $160-$180 million (from $150-$180 million). Management highlighted strong demand across the portfolio, including a 43% growth in combined revenues for key products, and confirmed the merger with Indivior is expected to close on November 2nd.

Sterling Infrastructure reported exceptional Q3 FY2026 results with revenue surging 127% YoY to $4.63 billion and adjusted diluted EPS reaching $7.58, an 118% increase. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($4.63B-$4.73B), adjusted diluted EPS ($21.70-$21.96), and EBITDA ($970M-$981M). The company highlighted a total scoped work of nearly $8 billion, up 90% YoY, driven by strong demand in data centers, semiconductors, and energy infrastructure.

Stoke Therapeutics reported Q3 FY2026 financial results with a net loss of $73.6 million and cash equivalents plus marketable securities of $358.8 million. The company reiterated its timeline for an EMPEROR data readout in Q3 2027 and a planned NDA submission in the second half of 2027 following FDA discussions that accepted a multicomponent Vineland-3 assessment. Management expressed confidence in advancing the pipeline, including dosing the third cohort of the ADOA phase I study underway.

STM reported Q3 FY2026 net revenues of $3.76 billion, beating the midpoint of guidance and driven by strong growth in communication equipment (64% YoY) and industrial segments. Gross margin expanded to 37.3%, up 410 bps YoY, while Non-U.S. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.37. Management raised revenue expectations for AI data centers to well above $2 billion in 2027 and reiterated a path toward intermediate financial model margins of 44%-46% by late 2027/early 2028.

Stagwell reported record third quarter results with revenue of $816 million (up 10%) and adjusted EBITDA of $145 million (up 25%), driven by strong growth in Digital Transformation (+23%) and The Marketing Cloud (+108%). Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA to $490-540 million and adjusted EPS to $1.07-1.21, citing a successful pivot to higher-margin AI-based transformation software.

SPX Technologies reported Q3 FY2026 revenue growth of 21% YoY and adjusted EPS growth of 20%, driven by record HVAC segment performance. However, management lowered the top end of full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.50 (midpoint $8.35) due to growth-related inefficiencies from rapid capacity ramping and elevated input costs impacting HVAC margins. Management expects these headwinds to persist into Q4 but anticipates improved productivity and pricing power in 2027.

SPS Commerce reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $197.6 million (4% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $70.9 million (36% margin), beating expectations despite a 500 bps headwind from the divestiture of the 3P Revenue Recovery business and lower-than-anticipated Amazon take rate revenue due to new policy changes. Management raised full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $267.4M-$269.4M (midpoint margin 34%) and maintained Q4 revenue guidance, stating that without the specific headwinds they would have raised guidance on the year. The company deployed $48.8 million in share buybacks.

Schneider National reported Q3 FY2026 enterprise revenue of $1.35 billion (excluding fuel surcharge), up 3% year-over-year, with adjusted income from operations rising 66% to $63.8 million and adjusted EPS reaching $0.29 versus $0.12 in the prior year. The company updated its full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to a range of $1-$1.10, raising the low end from prior expectations while maintaining the high end. Management highlighted strong pricing execution and productivity gains, though noted sequential earnings moderation due to seasonality, the loss of a large Dedicated customer, and a one-time favorable settlement impact.

Wesco reported record Q3 FY2026 results with organic sales increasing 17% to $7.2 billion and adjusted EPS rising 47% to a record $5.77 per share. Management significantly raised the full-year 2026 outlook, projecting organic sales growth of 13%-14%, adjusted EBITDA margins of approximately 7.2%, and adjusted EPS between $18-$18.50. The company highlighted strong momentum across all business units, with data center sales up 55% year-over-year and backlog surging over 80%.

WEC Energy Group reported Q3 FY2026 earnings of $1.18 per share, a beat driven by warmer weather and rate-based growth. Management raised and narrowed full-year 2026 EPS guidance to a range of $5.60-$5.64, assuming normal weather for the remainder of the year. The company unveiled an updated five-year capital plan increasing total investment to $47.5 billion (2027-2031), primarily driven by new demand from very large customers like Microsoft and Oracle.

WEX reported record quarterly revenue of $780.1 million (up 12.8% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $6.13 (up 33.6%), both exceeding the midpoint of prior guidance. Management raised full-year revenue guidance by $96 million and full-year EPS guidance by $1.50, driven by strong organic growth in Mobility and Corporate Payments segments. The company repurchased $200 million in shares during the quarter, representing 85% of its adjusted free cash flow.

Starbucks reported Q4 FY2026 net revenues of $9.1 billion, down 3.9% year-over-year primarily due to the transition of its China business to a licensed model, while global comparable sales grew 7.2%. Consolidated operating margin expanded 450 basis points to 14%, and EPS rose approximately 54% to $0.80, exceeding the high end of prior guidance. For fiscal 2027, management raised full-year consolidated revenue guidance to a slight decline of approximately 1% (including the 53rd week) and set operating margin expectations at 13.5%-14%, up from the previous year's trajectory.

Second quarter net revenues were $995 million, representing a year-over-year increase of 15% in USD terms, though overall growth moderated compared to previous quarters due to headwinds in the Learning Device business. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded significantly to 24.9% from 12.5% prior year, driven by operating leverage and disciplined cost allocation. Management expects revenue growth to continue moderating as the company scales and the Learning Device segment faces a contracting industry environment.

Takeda reported H1 FY2026 core revenue of JPY 2.4 trillion (down 1% CER) and core operating profit of JPY 710.6 billion (up 0.7% CER). Management maintained its full-year revenue guidance for a low single-digit decline while raising the full-year forecast for core operating profit by JPY 30 billion and core EPS, citing transaction FX benefits. The company highlighted successful launches of ORZEYFUL in Japan/China and MIMRYLO in the U.S., alongside positive Phase III data for TAK-921 in gastric cancer.

Monro reported Q2 FY2027 comparable store sales declining 1.8% to $283.6 million, driven by mid-single-digit traffic declines and a 4% drop in tire category sales, while gross margins contracted 50 basis points due to higher occupancy costs. Operating income fell significantly to $2.6 million (0.9% of sales) from $12.8 million last year, resulting in a net loss of $1.6 million and a diluted loss per share of $0.05 versus prior earnings. Management maintained full-year guidance for flat-to-slightly-down comparable store sales and flat-to-slightly-down gross margins, citing continued macro consumer pressures.

Total revenue was $3 billion, down 4% year-to-year and slightly below the high end of prior guidance, while adjusted EBIT margin contracted to 6.2%, down 180 bps. Management reduced full fiscal year 2027 organic revenue guidance to a 5%-5.5% decline due to weaker-than-expected second quarter bookings in CES and GIS segments. The company also lowered its full-year adjusted EBIT margin outlook to 5.75%-6.25% and non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance to $2.25-$2.50.

CSW Industrials reported record Q2 FY2027 results with consolidated revenue of $361 million (up 31% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $97 million (up 33% YoY). The company raised its synergy target for the MARS acquisition to $15 million, having already realized that amount. Management noted a slight decline in consolidated gross margin to 42.1% due to freight and raw material costs, but emphasized strong organic growth across segments and a resilient repair/replace demand mix.

Allegro reported Q2 FY2027 sales of $277 million, beating the high end of guidance by $277 million (implied prior range ~$15M-$28M based on context or a typo in transcript where '277' likely refers to absolute beat amount over a much lower base, but text explicitly says '$277 million above the high end'). Non-GAAP EPS was $0.26, doubling YoY. The company raised its Q3 sales guidance range to $278-$288 million (midpoint +23% YoY) and expects gross margins between 51.5% and 52.5%. Key drivers included record design wins (+40% YoY), strong automotive growth (+11% YoY), and data center sales hitting a record $46 million.

Sandisk reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $11 billion, beating the guidance range of $10.3-$10.8 billion, with non-GAAP EPS of $49.51 exceeding the $44-$46 guidance. Gross margin expanded to 85.1% driven by volume and pricing, while data center revenue surged 61% sequentially. Management raised Q2 revenue guidance to $12.2-$12.6 billion and maintained a strong outlook for fiscal year 2027.

ResMed reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $1.4 billion, representing a 6% increase on a reported basis and 7% growth on a core constant currency basis. Non-GAAP earnings per share grew 14% to $2.91, driven by gross margin expansion of 50 bps to 62.5% and productivity gains that offset foreign exchange headwinds. Management reiterated full-year FY2027 guidance for revenue growth of 5%-7% on a core constant currency basis and non-GAAP EPS between $12-$12.25.

OSI Systems reported record Q1 FY2027 revenues of $403 million (up 5% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.66 (up 17% YoY), driven by strong growth in Optoelectronics (+9%) and Security (+4%), partially offset by a Healthcare decline (-14%). Management raised non-GAAP full-year FY2027 EPS guidance to $11.28-$11.64 while reaffirming revenue guidance of $1.875 billion-$1.930 billion, citing the impact of share repurchases and a robust backlog conversion expected in the second half.

Net sales decreased 3.5% to $288.1 million and diluted EPS fell to $1.11 from $1.59 year-over-year due to a 3.6% decline in weighted average watching price and lower consumer volume. Gross profit declined 9.6% to 17% of net sales driven by competitive pricing pressures, unfavorable product mix, and higher operating expenses as a percentage of sales. Management noted that approximately 50%-60% of the private label volume decline was due to previously lost business rather than pure demand weakness.

FedEx Freight reported Q1 FY2027 (four-month transition period) revenue of $3.3 billion, up 9% YoY, and adjusted operating income of $510 million, a 16% increase versus the prior year. Management raised its full-year adjusted outlook relative to June guidance, citing solid performance and tailwinds from fuel prices and pricing strategies. The company reduced debt by $100 million during the quarter, bringing gross leverage to 2.8x.

Covista reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $512 million (up 10.7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $2.19 (up 25.1% YoY), both beating expectations. Management raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance for revenue to $2.06-$2.095 billion and adjusted EPS to $9.00-$9.20, citing strong enrollment growth across all segments including a record at Walden. The company returned $84 million via share repurchases and maintains a net leverage of 0.5x.

Q1 FY2027 revenue was $934 million (up 8% reported, 2% organic constant currency), missing expectations due to muted VistaPrint growth and higher startup costs. Adjusted EBITDA declined 9% year-over-year to $89.8 million, primarily driven by $5.9 million in North American manufacturing startup costs and $4.2 million in duties/tariffs. Management maintained full-year FY2027 guidance of at least 7% revenue growth and $520 million adjusted EBITDA, citing an internal budget higher than public guidance as an insurance policy.

Axos reported Q1 FY2027 net income of $129.6 million and diluted EPS of $2.25, representing a 15.4% and 16% year-over-year increase respectively. Net interest income grew 13.8% year-over-year to $129.6 million (implied from context) with NIM expanding 10 bps to 4.64%, while non-interest income rose 97% year-over-year to $63.8 million driven by acquisitions and fee growth. Management maintained its guidance for low-to-mid-teen organic loan growth in FY2027, noting that the quarter's loan growth was temporarily suppressed by higher payoffs and syndication activity rather than a lack of demand.

Plexus reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $1.43 billion (up 35% YoY) and non-GAAP operating margin of 6.7%, both substantially exceeding guidance. Management raised fiscal 2027 revenue growth expectations to mid-to-upper teens and increased the non-GAAP operating margin goal to 6.5%-7%. The company delivered record free cash flow of $6 million and ended with a net cash position.

West Fraser reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $1.36 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $38 million, a decline from the prior quarter's $59 million due to lower prices in Southern Yellow Pine (SYP) and Oriented Strand Board (OSB), partially offset by favorable inventory valuation adjustments. Management announced the indefinite curtailment of the Huguley OSB mill and the Leola lumber mill to align operations with weak demand, while maintaining shipment guidance at the lower end of previous ranges. The company emphasized a disciplined capital allocation strategy amidst high diesel costs and constrained housing affordability.

Forestar reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $580.8 million and net income of $59.2 million ($1.15 EPS), missing the implied prior year growth trajectory due to a gross margin contraction to 17.8% from 22.3% YoY. The lower margin was driven by $7.6 million in real estate impairment charges and specific project closeout costs, excluding which margins normalized to 20.8%. Management lowered full-year lot delivery guidance to 12,000-13,000 lots for FY2027, citing ongoing affordability constraints and cautious consumer sentiment.

Enerpac Tool Group reported record annual revenue of $652 million for fiscal 2026, driven by a 10% organic growth in the Industrial Tools & Services segment and strong performance in the Americas. The company successfully closed its acquisition of SFE Group, funding the deal with cash on hand and an expanded credit facility, resulting in a net leverage of 0.1x prior to closing. Management provided initial fiscal 2027 guidance expecting revenue between $825 million and $845 million (organic growth of 4%-6%) and adjusted EPS between $2.00 and $2.15.

D.R. Horton reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $9.4 billion and EPS of $2.67, missing expectations due to a 120 bps sequential decline in gross margin driven by higher costs and elevated incentives. Management reduced starts significantly to align inventory with weakening demand caused by sharply rising mortgage rates. For fiscal 2027, the company provided wider guidance ranges for revenue ($30-32B) and homes closed (79k-84k), while expecting continued pressure on Q1 gross margins.

YPF reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $6.6 billion (up 41% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $2.5 billion (up 84% YoY), marking the second-highest quarterly record in company history. The quarter was driven by a shift to shale production, which reached 224,000 bpd (up 32% YoY), and strong downstream performance despite conventional asset divestments. Management highlighted robust cash generation of $901 million and a net leverage ratio of 0.81x, while confirming the company is on track to meet its full-year CapEx target of $5.8-$6.2 billion.

Xerox reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.87 billion (down less than 5% YoY) and adjusted operating margin of 6.6% (up 330 bps YoY), but GAAP EPS was a loss of $7.73 due to a $959 million goodwill impairment. Management lowered full-year adjusted operating income guidance to $450-$475 million from the prior $555-$605 million range and suspended dividends, citing headwinds from rising memory/oil costs ($60M impact), a shift to lower-margin entry equipment, and weaker IT Solutions performance.

XPO reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.4 billion (up 12% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.70 (up 59% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA grew 27% to $433 million, with the LTL segment achieving a record $293 million in adjusted operating income. Management raised full-year guidance for operating ratio improvement to north of 250 basis points and expects free cash flow to nearly double to approximately $800 million.

Xcel Energy reported Q3 FY2026 ongoing earnings of $1.52 per share, up from $1.24 in the prior year quarter, driven by higher electric revenues and lower fuel costs. Management narrowed its 2026 full-year ongoing earnings guidance range to $4.10-$4.16 per share and initiated 2027 guidance of $4.48-$4.62 per share. The company unveiled an updated five-year capital plan totaling approximately $70 billion, extending rate base growth expectations through 2031.

WTW reported Q3 FY2026 organic revenue growth of 4% and adjusted operating margin expansion of 150 bps to 21.9%. Adjusted EPS grew 18% to $3.63, driven by strong Health business performance and technology investments under the Propel AI Acceleration Plan. Management maintained full-year guidance for mid-single-digit organic growth but narrowed the outlook for the Career segment due to Middle East headwinds and Benefits Delivery & Outsourcing implementation delays.

Net income was $11.6 million for Q3 FY2026, representing a 25% increase compared to the prior year quarter and a 17% increase in net interest income. Net interest margin expanded 8 basis points sequentially, while non-interest expenses rose 3% year-over-year. Management noted that loan growth was hampered by customer asset sales but expects this to subside in 2027.

West Pharmaceutical Services reported Q3 FY2026 revenues of $874 million (up 12% organically) and adjusted EPS of $2.66 (up 36%), both exceeding expectations. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a range of $3.41-$3.42 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $9.38-$9.48, citing strong momentum in HVP Components and GLP-1 demand. The company expects Q4 revenues of $820-$830 million with continued margin expansion driven by mix shifts and SG&A leverage.

WPP reported Q3 FY2026 like-for-like revenue growth of 0.5% and organic revenue growth of 0.5%, driven by a return to growth in WPP Media (0.3%) and WPP Production (2.5%), while WPP Creative declined 5.1%. Management reiterated full-year guidance for low-to-mid single-digit declines in H2 like-for-like revenue, with Q4 expected towards the better end of that range, and maintained a full-year operating profit margin guidance of 12%-13%.

Q3 revenue was over $476 million, exceeding expectations, while adjusted non-GAAP EPS of -$0.63 missed the guided range due to deliberate pull-forward of operational readiness costs and manufacturing inefficiencies. Management raised confidence in a dry van recovery for 2027, citing backlog growth from ~12,000 units at quarter-end to nearly 20,000 by mid-October, and expects Q4 revenue between $420 million and $450 million with operating margins of -8% to -5%. The company is accelerating capacity additions in late 2026 to capture anticipated demand earlier than previously planned.

World Kinect reported record third quarter adjusted EPS of $0.99, up 83% year-over-year, driven by a 12% increase in consolidated adjusted gross profit to $279 million. Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $3.52-$3.62 per share from the prior range of $3.20-$3.40 following strong outperformance in marine and land segments. While aviation and land are expected to decline sequentially in Q4 due to moderating market benefits, the company maintains a measured view on remaining opportunities.

Q3 revenue was $431 million, down 4% sequentially, while adjusted EBITDA of $132 million remained flat compared to Q2 despite lower volume and reduced tariff refunds. Management provided Q4 guidance for Pressure Control revenue to be flat to up with margins expected in the 23%-25% range, a decrease from the current quarter's outperformance driven by mix shifts and the non-recurrence of tariff recovery.

Silgan reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of approximately $2 billion (up 2% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.31 (up 7% YoY), beating the high end of the estimated range. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to a range of $3.83-$3.93, representing a 4% increase at the midpoint versus the prior year's $3.72. The company expects Q4 volumes to be comparable to the prior year and anticipates organic EBIT growth in the Dispensing and Specialty Closures segment.

SkyWest reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $120 million ($3.08 EPS) and revenue of $1.1 billion, which beat consensus expectations but was impacted by a significant $13 million headwind from higher prorate fuel costs ($4.56/gallon). Management maintained full-year 2026 GAAP EPS guidance in the $10.60 area despite the quarter's miss and noted that Q4 depreciation expenses will increase due to a fleet life extension. Forward outlook for 2027 remains flat on EPS compared to 2026, assuming similar fuel costs and recognizing less deferred revenue.

Sirius XM reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of approximately $2.2 billion (essentially unchanged YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $694 million, a 3% increase with margin expansion to 32%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($8.55B), adjusted EBITDA ($2.65B), and free cash flow ($1.4B) by $25 million, citing improved subscriber performance and operating efficiencies despite headwinds from elevated memory costs in equipment revenue.

NextDecade narrowed its guidance for first LNG production from Train 1 to the second quarter of 2027, citing a substantial completion date in Q3 2027 that is one quarter ahead of the guaranteed schedule. Management estimates volume-weighted average implied margins on projected uncontracted volumes will average over $6 per MMBtu, exceeding their base case guidance due to strong spot prices and Middle East supply disruptions. The company reaffirmed its project-level distributable cash flow projection of over $2.4 billion during the ramp-up period, representing more than 20% above the prior base case.

Patrick Industries reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated net sales of $975 million, essentially flat year-over-year, driven by strong growth in Marine (+14%) and Powersports (+30%) that offset a significant decline in RV revenue (-37%). Adjusted EPS was $1.03, slightly beating the prior year's $1.01, while reported EPS missed at $0.64 due to accounting dilution. Management maintained a cautious outlook for 2026, forecasting flat-to-down retail shipments in RV and Marine, with full-year adjusted operating margin expected to be flat versus 2025.

Ranpak reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated net revenue growth of 3.4% on a constant currency basis (up 3.8% excluding warrants), driven by strong automation sales which grew 26.9% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA increased $1.1 million to $22.5 million reported, or 6.1% in constant currency terms. Management noted that while Europe and APAC volumes were softer due to channel inventory normalization and macro volatility, North America performance remained robust with a 6.9% revenue increase.

Blue Owl reported fee-related earnings (FRE) of $0.27 per share and distributable earnings (DE) of $0.24 per share for Q3 FY2026, representing 15% and 14% growth over the last 12 months respectively. The company raised a record $12.6 billion in total capital during the quarter, bringing the last 12-month total to $49 billion, with institutional and insurance investors driving nearly three-quarters of equity raises. Management reaffirmed confidence in beating full-year guidance of $1.02 FRE and $0.89 DE per share, citing strong fundraising momentum and a robust pipeline.

OneSpan reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $63.9 million, a 12% year-over-year increase driven by double-digit growth in both Cybersecurity (11%) and Digital Agreements (14%). The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue to $254-$258 million from the prior range of $248-$252 million, citing strong Q3 results and updated expectations. Gross margin expanded to 76.3%, and management highlighted a shift in mix toward higher-margin software and services.

Consolidated sales of $2.8 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.41 missed expectations due to fire truck production challenges in the vocational segment. Management revised full-year guidance for adjusted EPS to a range of $8.50-$9.50, citing potential timing delays on the next NGDV order. While access equipment demand remains strong with a $2.7 billion backlog, the company is resetting near-term expectations for fire truck throughput and margin recovery.

O'Reilly reported Q3 FY2026 comparable store sales growth of 7.2% and diluted EPS growth of 14%, significantly surpassing expectations. Management raised full-year comparable store sales guidance from a range of 4%-6% to 5.5%-6.5% and updated full-year EPS guidance to $3.25-$3.35, reflecting strong execution despite some margin pressures in petroleum categories offset by tariff refunds. The company also announced an acceleration in new store growth with a 2027 target of 265-275 net new stores.

Omnicell reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $308 million and non-GAAP EBITDA of $45 million, both exceeding the high end of previously shared guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 non-GAAP EBITDA and EPS guidance while narrowing total revenue and product/service revenue ranges due to increased visibility. The company highlighted strong operational execution, favorable customer mix, and cost efficiency driving outperformance.

OMA reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of MXN 2.9 billion (up 8.7% YoY) with a margin expansion to 75%, driven by an 8.3% increase in total aeronautical and non-aeronautical revenues. Management raised full-year traffic guidance expectations, anticipating low single-digit growth for 2027 with recovery starting mid-year, while confirming plans to reach 100% tariff compliance by the third year of the five-year plan.

Origin Bancorp reported record net income of $37.8 million and record diluted EPS of $1.22 in Q3 FY2026, driven by record net interest income and margin expansion to 3.94%. Management raised full-year pre-tax, pre-provision ROA guidance to greater than 1.75% and expects low double-digit net interest income growth for the year. While period-end deposits declined slightly due to a large partner deposit flow-out, average deposits grew $221 million in the quarter with strong account opening trends.

NWPX reported record Q3 FY2026 results with net sales of $179.4 million (up 18.7% YoY) and EPS of $1.86 (up 35% YoY). The company delivered strong performance across its Water Transmission Systems segment, which saw revenue rise 27% to a record $131.9 million driven by higher volumes and watching prices. Management expressed high confidence in the outlook, citing a record backlog of $435 million and expectations for full-year 2026 records even without the one-time NDA project.

NovoCure reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $193 million, a 16% year-over-year increase driven by record active patients and new product launches. The company raised its full-year 2026 net revenue guidance to $736-$743 million (12%-13% growth) and updated adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $24-$34 million, marking the first positive adjusted EBITDA quarter in over four years. Management noted headwinds in the Optune Pax launch due to competition from daraxonrasib and practice saturation but remains committed to the indication.

Insperity reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.22 and adjusted EBITDA of $31 million, both beating the midpoint of guidance and reversing prior-year declines. Gross profit increased 6% to $207 million driven by an 8% rise in gross profit per worksite employee, though paid worksite employees declined 1.8% year-over-year. Management maintained full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance while narrowing the range, citing continued margin recovery progress but noting that growth momentum remains constrained by pricing and retention trade-offs.

NN, Inc. reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $131 million, a 26% year-over-year increase driven by higher volumes and watching prices, with adjusted EBITDA rising 50% to $18.5 million. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue to a range of $480-$500 million (midpoint $490m) and adjusted EBITDA to 64-68% of sales, citing strong momentum in data center, defense electronics, and medical segments. The company also announced the full redemption of preferred stock via a PIPE transaction, reducing net debt significantly.

Newmark reported record Q3 FY2026 revenues of $973.2 million (up 12.7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.48 (up 14.3% YoY). Management raised the full-year 2026 revenue guidance range to $3.7B-$3.8B, anticipating record annual results for all metrics. However, due to macroeconomic volatility and potential deal timing issues, management revised the outlook for 2027 earnings to be within a wide range of +/-10% compared to the record 2026 baseline.

Net income beat expectations at $124 million ($13.50 EPS) driven by higher operating profit and a reduced tax rate, while petroleum additives sales grew slightly to $651 million despite an 8% decline in shipments due to market softness. Specialty materials segment showed strong growth with Q3 sales of $62 million and operating profit of $16 million, aided by the Calca Solutions acquisition. Management maintained surcharges to offset supply chain costs and reiterated focus on operational efficiency amidst geopolitical uncertainty.

Pitney Bowes delivered strong Q3 FY2026 results with year-over-year improvements in EPS, adjusted EBIT, and adjusted free cash flow despite increased investment. Management raised the midpoints of revenue and adjusted free cash flow guidance based on these results and the volume tailwind from PCI's exit. The company is pivoting to a growth phase with increased CapEx and investment, acknowledging short-term transition costs.

NCLH reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $937 million and adjusted EPS of $1.12, both exceeding guidance by $63 million and $0.22 respectively. The beat was driven by Net Yield declining 6.7% (better than the expected decline) and occupancy reaching 106.5%, supported by strong close-in demand. Management raised full-year Net Yield guidance to a decline of approximately 4.4% and increased full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook by $50 million.

Third quarter 2026 revenues reached a record $1.26 billion, representing a 32% year-over-year increase driven by the Valley and Comet acquisitions and strong C&I performance. Gross margin expanded to 13.6% from 11.8% last year due to better-than-anticipated productivity and favorable job closeouts, while net income surged to a record $60 million. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations to an 18%-22% growth rate for the C&I segment inclusive of acquisitions.

Myers reported Q3 FY2026 revenue growth of 8.1% YoY, driven by infrastructure (+38%) and food and beverage (+12%), while vehicle and consumer remained flat. Adjusted EPS was $0.32, up 3.2% YoY on lower interest and tax expenses, though adjusted gross margin contracted 360 bps to 28.2% due to a spike in resin costs. Management reaffirmed strong growth expectations for infrastructure and food and beverage but lowered the vehicle outlook to 'down' from 'stable' citing mixed demand indicators.

MVB Financial reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $438,000 ($0.03 diluted EPS), a sequential decline from the prior quarter primarily due to an elevated provision for credit losses of $9.9 million driven by a specific land loan reserve. Underlying performance remained strong with net interest income increasing 18% year-over-year and core net interest margin expanding 15 basis points sequentially to 4.02%. Management maintained guidance confidence, citing continued fintech deposit growth (up 28% sequentially) and expense discipline despite the one-off credit event.

Murphy USA reported Q3 FY2026 results where same-store fuel volumes were flat despite a challenging competitive environment and hurricane activity, while retail margins remained under pressure from rising prices. Management reiterated full-year guidance for store openings of 45 to 50 units, noting that the pipeline is sufficient to sustain this pace into 2027. The company highlighted that non-nicotine same-store sales declined primarily due to lottery and beer categories, with nicotine driving share gains.

Meritage Homes reported Q3 FY2026 results with revenue of $1.2 billion, down 17% year-over-year due to a 14% decline in closing volume and a 4% drop in ASP to $365,000 driven by higher incentives. Adjusted home closing gross margin was 17.9%, excluding $6 million of real estate inventory impairments and walkaway charges, while adjusted diluted EPS was $1.11. Management explicitly declined to provide Q4 or full-year guidance citing a lack of visibility due to rapidly changing macro conditions and elevated mortgage rates.

Strategy reported record Q3 FY2026 results driven almost entirely by Bitcoin mark-to-market: a $20.9B fair value gain on digital assets produced $20.9B operating income, $19.1B net income, and $44.75 diluted EPS, with holdings at 848,517 BTC and treasury assets rising to ~$74B. Management highlighted a stronger balance sheet versus prior cycles — net leverage cut to 2.4% from 8.4% in Q2, USD reserves of ~$5.9B giving 3.4 years of interest/dividend coverage, and $2B of STRC repurchases with $957M capacity left. Offsets included Bitcoin-per-share down 3.7% YTD, a $1B MSTR buyback authorization entirely unused, and the announced CFO departure (Andrew Kang effective Nov 5, with Phong Le reassuming the CFO role). No formal forward financial guidance was given; commentary centered on a 2.2% breakeven / 10.6% hurdle / -17.4% floor ARR framework and a goal to double Bitcoin per share over seven years.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $18.1 billion, up 5% (4% ex-FX), with non-GAAP EPS of $2.49 including a $0.12 SciBrunch charge; gross margin slipped slightly to 81.4% while opex rose 12% to $7.4 billion. Full-year guidance was narrowed and the midpoint of both revenue ($66.8-67.3B, +3-4%) and EPS ($2.77-2.82) was raised. Management flagged that $550 million of Q3 sales came from favorable purchase timing that will largely unwind, and guided 2027 to only modest revenue growth against more than $2 billion of generic/LOE headwinds (BRIDION, JANUVIA, ADEMPAS), moderating KEYTRUDA growth, vaccine hesitancy, and mid-to-high single-digit opex growth. Growth drivers cited include KEYTRUDA family +6% to $8.6B, WINREVAIR +94% to $694M, WELIREG +58% to $307M and GARDASIL +14% to $2B.

MPS reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.2 billion, up 22% sequentially and 63% year-over-year, the first quarter above $1 billion, with gross margin expanding 10 bps and Q4 guided to roughly another 10 bps at the midpoint. The company raised its enterprise data floor to 150% year-over-year growth from 130% and said capacity reached $6 billion of annual revenue support, targeting $8 billion by H2 2027 and $10 billion thereafter. Management declined to give quantitative 2027 guidance but said no signs of slowing exist and comms should be the second-fastest growing end market, while storage/compute is guided to roughly flat to up slightly year-over-year on notebook weakness. Buybacks totaled over $450 million in the quarter.

MPT reported Q3 FY2026 normalized FFO of $0.11 per share, in line with expectations except for the non-payment of September rent from HSA. Results included a $70 million gain recognized on a $123 million net discount from the $2.4 billion secured refinancing, $158 million of gains on asset sales, and roughly $24 million of impairments tied mainly to Colombia earthquake exposure. Management guided portfolio cash rents to remain above $1 billion in 2027 and said Step two refinancing progress should push maturities out to June 2028, but did not project when HSA rent collections resume and cut Priory annual rents by about 18% (GBP 11 million). Key changes versus prior periods: HSA replaced its ownership with Adonis and engaged Ovation to run operations, and Priory received a rent reduction with a lease extension to 2055 at MPT's option.

Altria reported Q3 adjusted diluted EPS growth of 4.8% (5.1% for the first nine months) and raised full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $5.66-$5.74, a 4.5%-6% growth rate versus the prior 2.5%-5% range. Adjusted OCI grew 3.9% to $3.1 billion with margins expanding 0.1pp to 64.5%, while domestic cigarette volumes fell 2.9% reported (~4% adjusting for trade inventory). on! shipment volume rose 13.3% to 47.8 million cans but retail share slipped 0.3pp sequentially to 8.3%, and the oral segment's adjusted OCI declined 3.7% to $443 million on lower MST volumes. The board authorized a $1 billion expansion of the buyback program alongside the 61st dividend increase of 4.7% to $1.11 per share.

Merit reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $416 million, up 8% YoY (9% organic constant currency), exceeding the high end of prior expectations by ~90 bps and following 9% organic growth in Q2. Non-GAAP operating margin rose 160 bps to 21.3%, non-GAAP EPS grew 22% to $1.12 (a $0.04 beat), and free cash flow was ~$53 million, though gross margin fell 81 bps to 52.8%. FY2026 EPS guidance was raised to $4.33-$4.37 from $4.25-$4.35 and operating margin to 21.2%-21.4%, while the China outlook was trimmed ~$4 million for the second half; Q4 revenue is guided to $418-$426 million (6%-8% growth) with EPS of $1.08-$1.12. The company also disclosed the ~$45 million Solo Pace acquisition post-quarter and reiterated its three-year CGI targets ahead of a February 11, 2027 investor event.

Adjusted operating income rose 14% to $707 million ($707M vs. $621M) with EPS up 15% on buybacks; operating revenue grew 6% to $4.2B. Insurance combined ratio improved to 91.9% despite three points of Global Re run-off, ongoing premiums grew 9%, and the three ongoing divisions released $445M of reserves YTD vs. $397M prior year. Non-insurance segments were strong: industrial adjusted operating income +29% on 10% organic growth, financial +30%, consumer +80%. The company announced a $1.2B adverse development cover with Enstar over $4.8B of subject reserves ($2.25B transferred), funded by $120M risk premium and management margin, framed as Q4-neutral; no formal guidance was given for 2027.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 12.1% to EUR 2.5bn, with organic sales growth of 9.6% led by 7.3% volume and 2.2% price; all three regions grew (Europe/ANZ +8.9%, Americas +3.9%, AMEA +17.6%). Management raised full-year organic growth guidance to approximately 5.5% from 3%-5% but maintained margin guidance, citing roughly 100 bps of H2 oil and energy cost inflation. Q4 sales are guided roughly flat year-over-year on seasonality, while full-year adjusted EBITDA margin on a comparable perimeter is still expected to improve 40-60 bps (reported 0-20 bps).

PBF Energy reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net income of $12.78 per share and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $2.3 billion, driven by strong product markets and full system availability following turnarounds. The company reduced net debt by more than $1.2 billion during the quarter and raised its quarterly dividend by 18%. Management provided Q4 throughput guidance of 925,000-985,000 bbl per day and maintained 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $825 million to $875 million.
