Net interest margin came in at 3.03%, above the previously previewed 2.90-3.00% range despite roughly $1 million of interest accrual reversals, with deposit costs trending lower. Classified loans fell from $207 million to $153 million (Jawad cited a 70% reduction in one measure) and reserve coverage rose, while NPLs sit at $22 million against a $70 million ACL (over 3% of loans). Management guided to a full cannabis loan/deposit sale in Q4 (~$70-80 million deposits, ~$70 million loans) and expects $2.5-3 million of elevated transaction expenses to largely fall away, with no formal 2027 expense guidance and DTA recapture only around end-2027.

Brunswick reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.5 billion, up 7% YoY, with adjusted operating earnings up 38%, adjusted operating margin of 10.1% (up 230 bps), and adjusted EPS of $1.58, up 63% and significantly ahead of expectations; all segments grew sales and expanded margins. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to approximately $4.65 from $4.55, the third raise this year (initial $4.10), while revenue guidance of $5.7-$5.8 billion and ~8% adjusted operating margin were maintained. The $0.10 EPS increase reflects roughly half of the Q3 beat passed through, with the remainder offset by unanticipated material inflation (aluminum, copper, memory) and channel stocking caution heading into Q4. Management also disclosed a CEO transition, with Navico President Áine Denari succeeding David Foulkes on January 1.

Attruby U.S. net product revenue was $253.2M, up ~134% YoY and ~14% QoQ, driving total Q3 revenue of $353.2M versus $120.7M a year ago, which included a $75M one-time Bayer milestone for Beyonttra. The operating loss narrowed to $11.6M from $145.2M, though the company flagged that the strong operating line benefited from launch-expense timing and that OpEx will catch up in Q4. Management reaffirmed its $4B Attruby peak sales assumption and cited three prioritized launches in the next seven months (BBP-418 Nov 27, 2026; infigratinib Feb 4, 2027; encaleret May 8, 2027), while noting EU filing for BBP-418 shifted to 1H 2028 pending 36-month data.

Entegris reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.006 billion, up 25% YoY and 14% sequentially, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.23 (up 71% YoY) and adjusted gross margin of 48.9%, up 130 bps sequentially and 530 bps YoY. Both top and bottom line exceeded guidance, driven by execution on production/throughput rather than pricing, with APS up 31% and MS up 16% YoY. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $1.025-1.055 billion (about 26% YoY growth at midpoint), gross margin of 49.2-49.7%, and non-GAAP EPS of $1.32-1.40; Q1 FY2027 revenue is expected down mid-single digits sequentially but up more than 20% YoY. Backlog rose more than 35% sequentially and more than doubled YoY, and the company fully repaid its 2029 term loan ahead of schedule, with net leverage improving to 2.9x.

Q3 FY2026 net sales were $1.8 billion versus $1.6 billion a year ago, GAAP diluted EPS $1.67 versus $0.12, and combined adjusted EBITDA $514 million versus $245 million, with $310 million from Global Ingredients (~$340 million at the high end of last quarter's guide) and $204 million from DGD. Core ingredients EBITDA fell sequentially on ~$30 million of items — a $15 million deferral of half the profit on Darling feedstock sold to DGD and an adverse lower-of-cost-or-market adjustment — plus higher LTI accruals, which management said made up the shortfall versus expectations. Full-year 2026 combined adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.2-2.3 billion was reaffirmed (~$1,250 million core plus DGD at $1.50-2.00/gallon on 1.2 billion gallons); net debt fell ~$420 million with leverage at ~1.7x versus 2.9x at year-end, and ~$76 million of shares were repurchased. DGD's 315 million gallons, ~$1.30/gallon margin and $204 million EBITDA missed the 335 million-gallon guide on a Gulf hydrogen outage and included hedge losses and reduced PTC capture expected to reverse in Q4.

AMERISAFE reported Q3 2026 net income of $7.2M ($0.39/diluted share) and operating net income of $7.4M ($0.40/share), down sharply from $13.8M ($0.72) and $10.6M ($0.55) in Q3 2025. Net premiums earned rose 3% to $73.3M, but gross written premiums fell 4.5% to $76.7M on unfavorable audit adjustments (-$1.6M vs a +$2.5M prior-year swing), and the expense ratio widened to 32.5% from 31.1%. Management reiterated its mid-single-digit growth target for the year but flagged intensifying competition, 'irrational' pricing/commission structures, and loss cost declines of 5-6% heading into 2027; no formal numeric EPS or premium guidance was provided.

TechnipFMC reported Q3 revenue of $2.9B with adjusted EBITDA of $636M (22% margin excluding FX) and free cash flow of $470M. Subsea revenue rose 5% sequentially to $2.6B and Subsea adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record 23.5%, while Surface Technologies grew 7% to $296M at 18% margin. Full-year guidance was raised: Subsea revenue to $9.6-9.8B, free cash flow to $1.45-1.55B, and total company adjusted EBITDA to ~$2.22B excluding FX. The company also gave an early 2027 Subsea view of $10-10.4B revenue at 22.5-24% margin, implying >10% EBITDA growth, and guided to at least $14.5B of Subsea orders over the next five quarters.

Flowserve reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $1.24 billion, up 5% reported but down ~1% organic, with adjusted operating margin expanding 170 bps to 16.5% and adjusted EPS up 19% to $1.07, ahead of expectations. Bookings grew 14% to $1.4 billion (book-to-bill 1.12x) and backlog hit a record $3.5 billion, up 20% year-over-year. However, guidance was cut on the top line: full-year organic sales now expected to decline 1.5%-2.5% (from prior expectations), with total sales growth of 2%-3%, reflecting worsening Middle East disruption that added a ~$40 million Q3 sales headwind and is expected to persist in Q4. The low end of EPS guidance was raised to $4.10-$4.20, but full-year free cash flow conversion guidance was lowered to ~80% from prior expectations due to working capital headwinds.

Floor & Decor reported Q3 FY2026 sales up 3% to $1,214.6 million with comparable store sales down 1.4%, an improvement from -2.1% in Q2 and -3.7% in Q1. Diluted EPS rose 15% to $0.61 (up 11% excluding a ~$0.02 tax benefit), and gross margin expanded 30 bps to 43.7% on ~$14 million of IEEPA tariff refunds that offset a ~100 bp diesel-driven supply chain headwind. Full-year guidance was narrowed to sales of $4,765-$4,835 million, comps down 3.5% to 2.0%, and adjusted EPS of $1.88-$1.98, while management cut planned 2027 new store openings to 10-15 from 20 in FY2026 and noted Q4-to-date comps down approximately 3.8%.

Farmland Partners reported Q3 2026 net loss of $15.5 million ($0.36 per share) versus net income of $0.5 million ($0.00 per share) a year ago, and AFFO of negative $2.1 million (negative $0.05 per share) versus positive $2.9 million ($0.07 per share) in Q3 2025. Results were driven by a $12 million impairment on California farms earmarked for sale, an increased credit loss reserve on an FPI Loan Program borrower, and an adverse Louisiana litigation outcome. Full-year 2026 AFFO guidance was cut by $0.10 per share to $0.21-$0.25, with management attributing 9.5 cents of the reduction to the two non-recurring charges. Lease renewals about a third of the way through come in roughly flat to slightly up, and the company repurchased about 1.7 million shares at an average of $10.32.

Net sales were approximately $1.2 billion, down about 23% year-over-year on lower third-party module volumes, but gross margin expanded roughly 20 percentage points to about 58% on a richer U.S.-produced product mix plus lower freight, underutilization, and tariff costs. Net income was $571 million (up ~25% YoY), adjusted EBITDA $744 million at a ~60% margin near the upper end of the prior Q3 preview range, and diluted EPS $5.30 versus $4.24. Full-year 2026 guidance was lowered to reflect reduced India domestic, international Series 6, and U.S. finishing volume, with India domestic volume cut by roughly 0.7 GW and associated revenue and EBITDA reduction; net cash guidance was unchanged. The board authorized a new $500 million buyback, and backlog stands at 44 GW / ~$13.5 billion, but recent bookings were only ~1.4 GW U.S. at ~$0.36/W and management described a transitioning post-Section 232 market with delayed 2029 procurement.

Federal Signal reported record Q3 FY2026 results: net sales of $656 million (up 18% YoY), adjusted EPS of $1.34 (up 18%), adjusted EBITDA of $140.4 million (up 21%, 21.4% margin, up 50 bps), and orders of $620 million (up 33%). ESG sales grew 21% with orders up 43% (high-teens organic), while SSG grew 2% with orders down 6% YoY. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.20-$5.32 from $5.12-$5.30, but the net sales range was narrowed to $2.61-$2.64 billion from $2.58-$2.67 billion due to delivery delays on third-party Labrie refuse trucks; CapEx outlook maintained at $45-$55 million. GAAP gross margin slipped slightly to 28.9% from 29.1%, and backlog of $967 million was down about $25 million YoY.

Adjusted EBITDA of $348.3 million rose 17% year-over-year and 15% sequentially, driven by a record Aerospace Products quarter ($910 million revenue, up 76% YoY; $282.4 million EBITDA, up 57%, at a 31% margin in line with 30% guidance) and Aviation Leasing EBITDA of $104 million, up 18% sequentially. 2026 and 2027 segment guidance was reaffirmed, including the $2.3 billion 2027 EBITDA target comprising $1.4 billion Aerospace Products, $450-750 million Power, and $450 million Leasing. Full-year free cash flow before growth initiatives was revised down $61 million to $1.1 billion on opportunistic engine acquisitions, while growth initiative spend rose $173 million to $463 million, mostly Power R&D and facilities. The company announced a new $500 million accelerated share repurchase completing by year-end, alongside $80 million already repurchased and an authorization increase to $1 billion, with net debt/EBITDA at 2.2x.

Fortrea reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $691.5M, down 1.4% YoY but up 2.0% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $58.0M (8.4% margin, up 120 bps YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.28 versus $0.12 a year ago. Book-to-bill was 1.12x (1.06x in Q2) and full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $2.665-2.690B and adjusted EBITDA to $210-218M with both midpoints raised. However, total backlog fell to $7.3B from $7.8B in Q2, driven by a $558M cumulative downward adjustment plus slightly elevated cancellations, and management flagged a sequential Q4 revenue slowdown on fewer working days. Free cash flow turned strongly positive at $52.5M for the quarter and $47.4M year-to-date versus a negative prior-year period.

FTI reported record Q3 revenue above $1 billion, up 6% YoY with growth in all five segments, adjusted EBITDA of $153.7 million (+18%, 15.2% margin, +150 bps), and record adjusted EPS of $3.84 (+48% YoY vs $2.60). Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $9.50-$10.00 from $9.10-$9.70 while reaffirming revenue of $3.94-$4.1 billion; GAAP EPS guidance is $7.55-$8.05. Results included unusual positive items — record $40.7 million CorpFin success fees, a 17.8% tax rate, and Econ PTO/bad-debt benefits — which management normalized to roughly $2.90 of adjusted EPS. Third and fourth quarter headcount actions (about 4% of employees, $46 million Q3 charge plus $7 million expected in Q4) are expected to yield ~$80 million in annualized cost savings, and management flagged volume declines in restructuring, M&A, and regulatory entering a seasonally slower Q4.

Q3 revenue of $90.9M came in above the $80M-$88M guidance range but was down 15.8% YoY, with marketplace revenue down 24.7% to $55.4M offset by services up 3.4% to $35.5M. Adjusted EBITDA was $14.5M (16% margin) versus guidance, and FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $374M-$380M and adjusted EBITDA to $61M-$65M. However, Q4 guidance of $80M-$86M revenue and $6M-$10M adjusted EBITDA implies sharp margin compression, and management flagged a steeper marketplace traffic decline through 2027 with downward pressure on 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin. Active buyers fell 25.8% YoY, though spend per buyer rose 12.9% and $1,000-plus projects reached 16% of gross order amount.

GATX reported Q3 diluted EPS of $2.92 versus $2.25 a year ago, with year-to-date EPS of $8.11 versus $6.46; the 2025 figures included a $0.15 net benefit from tax adjustments and other items. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to modestly exceed the prior $9.90-$10.30 range, driven by a strong secondary market (net disposition gains of $50.3 million in the quarter, $167.8 million YTD) and a jump in Brookfield portfolio management fees to almost $15 million from about $2.8 million in each of the prior two quarters. Rail North America renewal success was 86.1%, fleet utilization 98.4%, and the lease price index renewal rate change was +12.4%, which management said was softer than expected due to GABX mix and sand cars. Buybacks totaled 442,000 shares for $78.5 million in the quarter.

LENZ reported Q3 FY2026 total product revenue of $2.6 million plus $0.8 million in license revenue from Arrotex, with over 38,000 paid scripts, representing roughly 50-51% sequential growth over Q2 and a gross-to-net of about 93%. SG&A fell 10% sequentially to $35.8 million, R&D was zero, net loss was $31 million ($0.99 per share), and the company ended the quarter with $197.3 million in cash. Management announced a consumer-marketing-led reorganization cutting headcount to about 40 employees and reducing 2027 operating expenses to $70-75 million (over 50% lower), alongside the CEO's departure effective December 1, 2026, with the CFO becoming interim CEO. No revenue or cash runway guidance was provided, and profitability timing was not addressed.

EPR reported Q3 2026 revenue of $204.1 million, up 12% from $182.3 million, with FFO as adjusted per share of $1.49 versus $1.37 (+8.8%) and AFFO per share of $1.54 versus $1.39 (+10.8%). Management raised 2026 FFO as adjusted guidance to $5.49-$5.57 from $5.41-$5.57 (up 8% at the midpoint) and lifted investment spending guidance to $675-$725 million from $600-$700 million, while also raising percentage rent guidance to $21.5-$24.5 million. Q3 investments totaled $172.4 million at an ~8.3% average initial cash yield, bringing year-to-date to $664.5 million, and portfolio rent coverage rose to 2.1x. Theatres are now about one-third of the portfolio versus a long-term ~20% target, and education remains a headwind area.

Hippo reported Q3 FY2026 gross written premium of $498 million, up 60% year-over-year, with net written premium up 26% to $149 million, revenue up 29% to $156 million, and adjusted net income up 9% to $20 million ($0.74 per diluted share). The combined ratio improved 1 point to 98.4%, and net income was $9 million ($0.33 per diluted share), down $89 million year-over-year due to a $91 million prior-year gain on sale. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance across the board: GWP to $1.7-$1.75 billion, revenue to $585-$590 million, adjusted net income to $77-$80 million, and lowered the combined ratio range to 97%-98% (from 99%-101%). The company also announced a partnership with Greenlight Re to act as a preferred program carrier for emerging MGAs.

Bel Fuse reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $220.5 million, up 23.2% year-over-year, with gross margin of 40.9% (up 120 bps) and adjusted EBITDA of $52.5 million, up ~34% to a 23.8% margin. ITDS revenue rose 37.8% to $113.9 million on data solutions growth of ~61%, while ADRS grew 10.7% to $106.6 million, though ADRS gross margin fell to 39.6% from 41.1% on mix and FX. Q4 guidance is for net sales of $220-240 million and gross margin of 40-42%, with management citing record all-time-high bookings exceeding sales and expecting Q4 to buck normal seasonality. The company ended with $333.1 million in cash and securities, up from $57.8 million at year-end largely on the Q2 equity raise.

Q3 cash rental income was $75.2 million, up 13.7% YoY, with FFO per share of $0.46 (+2.9% YoY); management flagged the quarter as noisy from a ~$100,000 disputed Oklahoma state tax catch-up, dead deal costs, and expensed credit facility costs. Annualized cash base rent reached $292.8 million at quarter end, occupancy was 99.5%, rent coverage 5.3x, and collections 99.7%. Record YTD acquisitions of $410 million at a 6.6% cash cap rate, including the 102-property Mission Pet Health deal, but management has paused new acquisition volume because private cap rates have not repriced enough relative to its cost of capital. Cash G&A guidance was reaffirmed at $19.2-19.7 million with the expectation of landing at the bottom of the range; a new $100 million buyback and potential dispositions/JV capital are now the stated capital priorities.

Forbright reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $20.6 million, or $0.41 per diluted share, up over 400% from Q2 on net interest income of $72 million (up ~14% sequentially); pre-provision net revenue rose nearly 60%. Loans grew 24% year-over-year (up 9.5% in the quarter), digital deposits rose over $1 billion (up 24% QoQ), NIM held flat despite ~10-11 bps of mix drag from branch-sale liquidity, net charge-offs fell to $1.2 million (3 bps core), and the efficiency ratio improved ~8 points to 69.6%. Management guided Q4 NIM wider, 2027 expenses roughly flat ex pass-throughs, and a Q4 tax rate of ~20% (19% for FY2027); no explicit EPS or revenue guidance was raised. The key change versus prior guidance was NIM holding flat rather than contracting as expected, with management now signaling possible modest spread widening on 2027 originations.

Exponent reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues up 18% to $173.7 million and net revenues up 12% to $153.1 million, with diluted EPS up 16% to $0.64 and EBITDA margin expanding to 29.4% from 28.3%. Utilization rose to 76.7% from 74.1% and realized rates increased about 4%. Management raised full-year 2026 net revenue growth guidance to 10%-11% and EBITDA margin to 28%-28.3% versus 27.6% in 2025, while guiding Q4 net revenue growth of 8%-10% against a tough comparable. Proactive work grew in the high teens and reactive in the high single digits, and management estimated AI is a direct element of roughly 15%-20% of the business this year.

Escalade reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $65.6 million, down 3% year-over-year, with net income of $6.7 million or $0.48 per diluted share. Gross margin expanded 123 bps to 29.4%, EBITDA rose $1.4 million to $10 million (including a $1.6 million tariff recovery), and cash flow from operations swung to $14.9 million from a $1 million use. No explicit forward revenue or EPS guidance was given; management cited softening discretionary demand, an active acquisition pipeline, and upcoming 2027 product launches. The company ended with $24.5 million cash and $13.1 million debt, a net cash position of $11.4 million.

Q3 revenue of $72M rose 33.9% YoY, with U.S. up 119% to $26M and OUS up 9.7% to $46M; adjusted EBITDA reached $6.4M (8.9% margin) versus $1.2M a year ago. The company raised FY2026 revenue guidance to more than $274M from $269-271M and lifted minimally invasive guidance to over $40M from over $35M, and guided to ~25% revenue growth in 2027. Q3 delivered the company's first positive free cash flow at $5.1M. GAAP gross margin fell to 69.1% from 70.1% and full-year adjusted gross margin guidance was cut to ~70.7% from 71.2-72.2% on a higher OUS distributor mix (60% vs. planned 50%). GAAP net loss was $0.35 per share versus $0.38 a year ago.

FBRT reported a Q3 2026 GAAP net loss of $27 million, or $0.36 per fully converted share, with distributable earnings of negative $0.02 per share after roughly $22 million of net realized loss adjustments; before realized losses, DE was $0.24 per share. The quarter included a $37.7 million CECL provision driven by increased specific reserves on legacy multifamily assets, and watch list loans rose to 13 from prior periods with REO up about $140 million to $340 million across 10 assets. Book value was stable at $14.26 per share, up $0.02 sequentially, and the company repurchased about $60 million of stock at an average $8.14, generating $0.55 per share of book value accretion. No formal forward guidance was provided; management emphasized resolving roughly $300 million of equity tied up in non-performing loans and REO, with several assets under signed PSAs and the Houston asset sold after quarter end.

Total Q3 2026 revenues were ~$659M, including U.S. CABO franchise net product revenue of $605M (~11% YoY growth; CABOMETYX $603M, +12% YoY) and ~$52M in partner royalties. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.85 and non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.94, with GAAP net income ~$218M; opex rose to ~$390M from $380M in Q2 and the tax provision increased to ~$64.7M. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was maintained (prior Q2 cut for NET temporality), while cost-of-goods and tax-rate estimates were updated; gross-to-net is now projected at ~30%. The zanza NDA PDUFA date was updated to March 3, 2027, and STELLAR-304 top-line results are now expected in Q1 2027.

Otis reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $3.9 billion with organic sales up 6%, its strongest organic growth in 13 quarters, led by 7% service growth and a 3% increase in new equipment (first positive since 2023). Adjusted operating margin contracted 110 bps to 16%, adjusted operating profit fell $3 million, and adjusted EPS was flat year-over-year. Full-year guidance was unchanged: net sales $15.1-15.3 billion, adjusted operating profit down $30 million to flat, adjusted EPS $4.01-$4.05, and free cash flow around $1.5 billion. New equipment orders grew 1% (5% ex-China), modernization orders rose 10% with backlog up 20%, while China new equipment sales fell more than 20% and maintenance growth slowed to 2% on churn and mix.

Q3 revenue rose 5% YoY to $991 million with adjusted EBITDA up 5% to $128 million, but non-GAAP gross margin fell 90 bps to 25.3% and product gross margin dropped 530 bps to 22.1% on mix and memory costs; EPS of $1.34 was down 4% YoY and free cash flow was a $46 million use. Management cut the full-year outlook to revenue of $3.86-$3.90 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $490-$510 million, FCF of $190-$210 million, and EPS of $4.50-$4.85, citing a $25 million net memory cost headwind, higher retail POS mix, and slower banking product volumes. The company also announced a new $250 million buyback and said 2027 guidance would come in February.

Q3 FY2026 net revenue was $335.6 million, down 70 bps as-reported and 80 bps constant currency, but up 6.7% organic constant currency; adjusted EPS was $1.04 versus $1.08 a year ago, which beat the top of the company's own range by $0.01 but was still a decline YoY. Adjusted gross margin rose 40 bps to 56.4%, adjusted operating margin rose 20 bps to 15.4%, and adjusted net income fell to $31.4 million from $33.4 million due to higher interest expense ($10.5 million vs $6.3 million) after the convertible-note refinancing. Full-year organic constant currency growth guidance was narrowed to 5%-5.5% from 5%-6% (high end cut on a more measured sequential pace and Q3 international distributor order timing not rolled forward), while full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose to $4.54-$4.61 from $4.48-$4.60. Domestic ortho fell 1.7% and U.S. general surgery grew only 1.9%-2% on OEM smoke evacuation pressure, partly offset by high single to low double digit AirSeal and Buffalo Filter direct growth and BioBrace plus international strength (general surgery +15.5%, ortho +12.7% constant currency).

DBV reported Q3 2026 cash and cash equivalents of $165.7 million, including $50 million in gross proceeds from ADS sales to RA Capital under an ATM program, with runway estimated into Q3 2027 on a stage-gated, milestone-based spending plan. Nine-month operating expenses rose to $164.4 million from $107 million a year ago, with sales and marketing up from $1.9 million to $15.7 million. The quarter's focus was the BLA submission for ages four to seven, with a priority review request made and a toddler (one to three) BLA now expected in 2027 under a sequential-review approach agreed with FDA. Fareva Amboise's April 2026 warning letter remains unresolved; the FDA reinspection has not been scheduled, and DBV's stated February 1 PAI-readiness date assumes timely remediation.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue rose 7% to $276.5 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 12% to $39.2 million, both exceeding the high end of July guidance, marking the 22nd straight quarter of record YoY revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth. Adjusted EPS was $0.34 versus $0.30, driven by a 3.3% increase in average guest spend, fleet expansion and higher volumes. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised at the midpoint to $1.033-$1.038 billion revenue and $138-$140 million adjusted EBITDA (midpoints up $7.5 million and $4 million), with Q4 guided to $248-$253 million revenue and $32-$34 million EBITDA. The board approved a new $100 million buyback and a 25% dividend increase to $0.0625 per share.

ONEOK reported Q3 2026 net income of $1.35B ($2.13/diluted share) and adjusted EBITDA of $2.24B, up 6% YoY, with EPS including a $336M one-time non-cash tax benefit and EBITDA including a $53M net transaction benefit. The company raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA midpoint guidance to approximately $8.55B, a $200M increase over last quarter and $450M above original February guidance, driven by ~$75M Brazos contribution, $50M transaction benefits, and $100M of stronger base business. 2026 capex guidance rose to ~$3.5B from ~$3.2B, and leverage target was lowered to approximately 3.25x or below versus the prior 3.5x. Management did not provide 2027 guidance but cited constructive producer plans, completed projects, and hedging as supporting momentum into 2027.

Stepan reported adjusted EPS of $0.94, up 98% from $0.48, and adjusted EBITDA of $66.3 million, up 18% year over year, on 7% organic volume growth across all three segments. Full-year 2026 guidance points to adjusted EBITDA growth, positive free cash flow, and continued deleveraging, with net leverage improved to 2.4x. Project Catalyst savings are now expected to exceed the 60% target, reaching $66 million to $70 million for 2026, and management says 2027 run-rate savings will average above $25 million per quarter. The key change from prior guidance is the upward revision to Project Catalyst savings and the increased dividend, though management flagged lower volume growth in Q4.

Total revenue rose 11% YoY to $2.8B, while core pharmaceutical revenue grew 18% to $2.0B, driven by a growth portfolio up 49% YoY to ~$1.3B (now ~63% of core revenue). The first full Apellis quarter contributed $243M from SYFOVRE and EMPAVELI, and management raised the low end of FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $12.20-$13.00, citing faster-than-expected integration synergies with the Apellis deal now roughly neutral on an operating basis. GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.14 due to $284M in acquired IPR&D and milestone charges tied to Reata. Offsetting the strength, VUMERITY fell 11% YoY on Part D formulary pressure, and SPINRAZA benefited from a one-time high-dose conversion tailwind expected to normalize in Q4.

Q3 constant-currency revenue grew 8.9% (Europe & International +20.4%, North America +2.9%, Greater China -19.3%), gross margin expanded 436 bps to 34.1%, and adjusted EBITDA was $9.4 million versus a prior-year $3.1 million. Full-year constant-currency revenue guidance was maintained at 8%-10%, but adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $16-$20 million from the prior $25-$35 million range, with $7 million at the midpoint attributed entirely to North America fuel and freight inflation, notably a ~70% rise in U.S. diesel since February. Free cash flow was a $18.4 million outflow versus $5.4 million last year, described as largely timing of CapEx, a more than $11 million inventory build, and payables phasing. Management repeatedly declined to quantify the North America price increase effective Q1 2027 or the Europe pricing under review, framing it as surgical and innovation-led.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $256 million, up 14% YoY, with gross profit of $33 million, GAAP net income of $5.5 million, adjusted EPS of $0.12, and adjusted EBITDA of $18 million, up 37% with margin expanding 120 bps. Marine revenue rose 13% to $161 million (11.6% EBITDA margin) and Concrete rose 16% to $95 million (11% EBITDA margin, including ~2% of favorable project write-ups). Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated at $900-950 million revenue, $50-54 million adjusted EBITDA, $0.23-0.30 adjusted EPS, and $25-35 million CapEx, with management tracking toward the upper end of each range. Backlog was ~$645 million with book-to-bill around 0.7x, as the award cycle slowed even though submitted bids awaiting award doubled to ~$2 billion from just over $1 billion at the start of the year.

HF Sinclair reported Q3 2026 net income of $2.0B ($11.38/diluted share) and adjusted net income of $2.1B ($11.75/diluted share), up sharply from $459M ($2.44) a year earlier; adjusted EBITDA was $3.0B versus $870M. Refining adjusted EBITDA reached $2.6B versus $661M, driven by tight fuel supply, elevated crack spreads, and EPA small-refinery RIN waivers, with capture ex-SRE at roughly 105%. Capital guidance was revised to ~$725M sustaining/turnaround plus $150M growth, Q4 crude guidance is 560-600 Mbd (reflecting the El Dorado turnaround), and the Lubes spin remains on track for H2 2027. Shareholder returns totaled $572M ($93M dividends, $479M buybacks) with a $0.525 quarterly dividend declared.

Q3 FY2026 was the first full quarter including Stellar Bank: net interest income rose to $443 million from $273.4 million a year earlier, tax-equivalent NIM expanded 49 bps YoY and 26 bps QoQ to 3.73%, and adjusted EPS was $1.67 on $200 million of net income excluding merger costs, with the adjusted efficiency ratio at 48%. The board raised the Q4 dividend 6.7% to $0.64 per share. Management guided Q4 expenses to $235-238 million and reiterated a 370-375 bps Q4 margin exit rate with 380-385 bps for 2027 average, while projecting flat to slightly up 2027 loan balances offset by $65-70 million of remaining pre-tax cost savings and low-to-mid-teens 2027 EPS growth. The main blemish was credit: non-performing assets rose to $193 million, or 60 bps of loans, from $130.6 million, or 52 bps, at June 30, largely from acquired assets.

OppFi reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $149 million, down 3.8% year-over-year, with originations down about 7% to $229 million. Adjusted net income fell 23% to roughly $32 million and adjusted EPS dropped to $0.37 from $0.46, while net charge-offs rose to about 53% of receivables from 47%. Full-year 2026 guidance was refined by trimming the top end: revenue $600-610 million, adjusted net income $115-120 million, and adjusted EPS $1.34-1.40. Management framed the quarter around strategic progress (line-of-credit launch, LOLA migration, Model 7 upcoming, BNCC deal pending regulatory approval) and an active $40 million buyback, but gave no 2027 guidance beyond saying expectations remain intact.

Q3 Distributable Earnings were $0.17 per share including a $1.5 million realized loss on the Dallas office loan; excluding it, DE was $0.24 per share, at the midpoint of guidance and in line with consensus. The quarter included a net $3.6 million credit reserve reversal, $122.3 million of originations (highest since Q4 2021), $139 million of repayments, and office exposure fell from 19% to 13%. Q4 DE guidance is $0.25-$0.27 excluding an approximately $0.11 Carlsbad realized loss, and the company pushed its sustainable dividend coverage target to the first half of 2027 due to loan closings landing later than anticipated. Weighted average risk rating rose to 3.2 from 2.9, and the Carlsbad office loan was downgraded to risk rating 5 before its post-quarter sale recovered about 90% of principal.

Revenue was approximately $8.0B, up 14% YoY with 9% net from acquisitions/divestitures, and adjusted EBITDA rose 14% to $1.42B at a 17.6% margin, flat to prior year. Adjusted EPS was $0.70, up only 2% YoY, and free cash flow was $769M after ~$200M of Chart-related transaction costs. Full-year EBITDA midpoint was raised to $5.265B and the IET order outlook lifted to $21.5-23.5B (a record year, implying >1.6x book-to-bill), with IET RPO at a record $39.4B, up 23% YoY. Q4 guidance embeds sequential Middle East declines and tougher IET logistics, with dollar-for-dollar quarter guide set at $8.25B revenue and $1.46B EBITDA.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $160 million vs $140 million a year ago, but the year-ago period was depressed by a $9.5 million out-of-period royalty adjustment. Material sales fell to $80 million from $83 million, total gross margin contracted to 73% from 75%, and management guided full-year revenue toward the low end of the $630M–$670M range and gross margin toward the low end of 74%–76%. GAAP EPS was $1.72 but included a $29 million non-cash UDC Ventures gain; adjusted EPS was $1.23, and operating income rose to $54 million (33% margin) from $43 million (31%). For 2027 management flagged tight memory conditions, higher input costs, and gross margin pressure, with only mid-single-digit OLED area growth expected.

Santander reported record underlying profit of EUR 11.2bn for 9M 2026, with Q3 profit up 14% YoY in constant euros, revenue up 7% (NII +8%, fees +7%), and efficiency at 42.6%, its best level in 17 years. Management said it is in a strong position to exceed its 2026 guidance of more than EUR 14.1bn profit excluding M&A, and confirmed a CET1 target at or above 12.8% after absorbing the 147bp Webster impact. The main negative was Brazil, where NII fell on de-risking and mix shift, NPLs rose to 4.1%, and management said it was too early to say when loan growth resumes given the abrupt rate outlook change post-election. The first-time consolidation of TSB and Webster added roughly 1.3pp to P&L lines and drove the US RoTE to 12.6%, on track for 18% by 2028.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 15% YoY to CAD 532 million, adjusted EBITDA was CAD 125 million (CAD 133 million pre-share-based comp) versus CAD 118 million prior year, and net earnings were CAD 21 million versus a CAD 7 million loss a year ago. Canadian activity averaged 73 rigs and U.S. 43, but U.S. daily margins fell to $7,653 from $8,700 due to six rig reactivations costing $2,125 per utilization day, and international day rates dropped 14% to $46,304 with elevated Middle East costs. Q4 guidance points to Canadian margins of CAD 13,500-14,500 and U.S. margins of $9,500-10,500 (a sequential step up), with full-year capex raised to CAD 275-285 million from prior levels. Management cited CAD 31 million of buybacks, CAD 75 million of debt reduction year-to-date, and over CAD 460 million of liquidity.

Q3 FY2026 net sales were roughly stable at ~$1.6 billion but adjusted EPS swung to a loss of $0.09 from $0.48 profit a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA down YoY. Europe segment operating profit collapsed to $2 million from $95 million on ~4% lower price and volume plus ~$15 million of energy/freight above expectations, while Americas held up with sales up over 3% to $970 million and segment profit down ~2% to $137 million. 2026 guidance was cut to adjusted EBITDA of $925-950 million and free cash flow usage of ~$300 million, with year-end leverage of 4.5x-5x, reflecting lower volume (including the U.S.-Canada tariff), higher energy/freight, and reduced Fit to Win benefits now seen at $180 million. Management framed 2027 as higher sales, EBITDA, and free cash flow with at least $170 million of Fit to Win benefits, but deferred formal 2027 guidance to the next call and said Europe stays pressured through Q1 2027.

rows.company_name: Bank of N T Butterfield & Son Ltd
rows.key_quote: Butterfield reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $61.0 million ($1.50/share) and core net income of $64.2 million ($1.58/share), with ROACE of 21.3% and core ROTCE of 25%. NIM rose 2 bps QoQ to 2.76%, NII increased $1.6 million to $97.2 million, non-interest income rose $1.4 million to $64.8 million, and the core efficiency ratio was 57.8%; the $0.50 quarterly dividend was maintained. Management guided quarterly core non-interest expenses to $93-95 million and expects NII/NIM to be roughly flat near term, despite roughly $500 million of notified deposit outflows. Non-accrual loans rose to $119.6 million (2.7% of gross loans) from 2.2%, driven by Channel Islands and U.K. residential exposures, while unrealized AFS losses widened to $187.3 million from $106.7 million.

OceanFirst reported Q3 FY2026 core EPS of $0.48, up 54% QoQ and 131% YoY, with GAAP EPS of $0.17 after $0.30/share of merger costs. Net interest income rose 43% QoQ to $172 million on the first full quarter of Flushing, and core operating expenses of $114 million came in below the prior $120-$125 million guidance range. NIM expanded 13 bps to 3.18% (3.08% ex the non-recurring recovery), and Q4 guidance calls for 1-2% loan and deposit growth, stable-to-modestly-higher margin, and core expenses declining to $110 million with a $105 million run-rate base into 2027. Full 2027 guidance is deferred to the January call, though the 1% ROA target is reiterated.

Aurora reported Q3 2026 revenue of just $3 million, an operating loss of $257 million including $54 million stock comp, and operating cash use of roughly $170 million with $36 million of capex. Management cut its 2026 revenue outlook to approximately $9 million, citing a production ramp running about six weeks behind plan due to material availability, component quality, and end-of-line testing issues, and guided Q4 cash use up to about $250 million. The 20-trucks-per-week run rate target slipped to early December and the 200 driverless truck milestone pushed to end of February, though the company reiterated exiting 2027 with more than 1,000 trucks. Positives include a Charger Logistics MOU for 500 trucks (hundreds of millions in potential multi-year revenue), a five-year FMCSA beacon exemption, and a balance sheet with over $1 billion in cash.

Equinor reported Q3 2026 adjusted operating income of $12.4 billion (nearly double year-ago), cash flow from operations after tax of $8.1 billion, and adjusted EPS of $1.20. Production grew 2% (up almost 5% year-to-date), and management raised full-year production growth guidance from 3% to around 4%, while MMP delivered well above guidance. The board approved a $0.39 quarterly dividend and a fourth $1.125 billion buyback tranche, bringing 2026 buybacks to $3 billion; 2026 CapEx guidance held at around $13 billion and CFFO guidance raised to around $29 billion from the prior $25 billion. Management flagged a higher 2027 decline at Johan Sverdrup, cost pressure from FX, and a tax payment lag pushing year-end net debt ratio to roughly 10% on an adjusted basis versus 3.8% reported.

Old Dominion reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 13.1% to $1.59 billion and EPS up 28.9% to $1.65, with the operating ratio improving 280 bps to 71.5%. Growth was driven by a 13.3% increase in LTL revenue per hundredweight, though LTL tons per day slipped 0.1% for the quarter before turning positive (up 1.6% YoY) in September. Management guided Q4 revenue to $1.54-1.58 billion (above normal seasonality) and an operating ratio around 73.5% +/-20 bps at the low end of the seasonal range, and noted October revenue per day up roughly 22% YoY. Key headwind cited was fringe benefit cost, which rose to 42.8% of salaries and wages from 39.7% a year ago, a ~1 point OR drag expected to persist into Q4.

Avantor reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.698B, up 5.2% organically and 4.6% reported, ahead of expectations, with adjusted EBITDA of $257M (15.1% margin) and adjusted EPS of $0.22. VWR grew 5.8% organically and BMP returned to growth at 3.6% organic despite a ~150 bps serum ordering headwind. Management raised 2026 organic revenue growth guidance to 0.75%-1.25%, adjusted EPS to $0.81-$0.83, and free cash flow to $525-$550M, while leaving adjusted EBITDA margin guidance unchanged. Adjusted net leverage fell to 3.1x from 3.3x, with a target below 3x by year-end.

Chipotle reported Q3 FY2026 sales up 9.6% to $3.3 billion with comps of +2.1% and transaction comp of +0.8%, but restaurant-level margin fell 120 bps to 23.3% and adjusted EPS dropped 7% to $0.27. Management kept its 2026 low single-digit comp guidance and expects Q4 margins just under 22%, about 150 bps below last year, while flagging that October trends softened consistent with the broader industry. Cost of sales improved about 50 bps to 29.5%, but labor rose 50 bps to 25.7% and other operating costs rose about 100 bps to 16% on higher marketing and delivery mix.

Equinix raised full-year 2026 guidance: total revenue up $100M to ~12% YoY growth, adjusted EBITDA up $70M to ~51% margin, and AFFO up $90M (including $31M from atNorth), with AFFO per share growth of 11%-12%. Q3 delivered 12% total revenue and 11% MRR growth (normalized, constant currency), adjusted EBITDA margin of 51.4% (up 180 bps YoY), AFFO per share up 12% normalized (18% including atNorth), and record annualized gross bookings of $533M, up 35%. New deal pricing rose 12% YoY with churn at 1.7%, and the retail capacity plan for the year was raised to nearly 40% above initial expectations with over 13,000 cabinets slated for Q4.

C.H. Robinson reported Q3 revenue growth of 29.5% and adjusted gross profit growth of 14.5% year-over-year, with NAST operating margin up 110 bps to 40.3% and Global Forwarding margin up 660 bps to 36.6%. Truckload AGP per shipment rose 17% YoY and NAST volumes grew 3.5% versus a 0.3% decline in the Cass index, the 14th consecutive quarter of outgrowth. Guidance was mixed: personnel expense guidance was tightened to $1.36B-$1.37B, but SG&A guidance was raised to $585M-$590M from a prior $540M-$580M on higher claims, while the full-year operating income target (at least $6 diluted EPS) held unchanged. The quarter included elevated claims and a $12.5M real estate impairment, and buybacks were paused pending the RXO acquisition, with leverage guided higher on closing.

Total revenue rose 4.6% YoY to $93.9 million and Adjusted EBITDA grew 11.8% to $33.2 million, with margin expanding 200 bps in the quarter. Glo Fiber and commercial fiber revenue grew 19.5% and reached 52% of consolidated revenue, while Glo Fiber data customers rose 32% YoY to ~109,000 on a record 8,600 net adds. Full-year 2026 revenue ($370-377 million) and Adjusted EBITDA ($131-136 million) guidance was reiterated, but CapEx guidance was raised to $255-275 million from $220-250 million for 7,000 extra passings and grant timing. Incumbent broadband remained a drag, with data churn up to 1.76% and ARPU down 3% YoY.

Q3 FY2026 GAAP revenue and adjusted revenue both $1.48B, up 14.5% YoY; GAAP diluted EPS $1.76 (+23.9%) and adjusted diluted EPS $2.03 (+23.8%). Same-store occupancy 84.1% and transitioning 86.1%, with skilled mix revenue up 10.7% and skilled days up 7.2%, growth across all payer categories. Management raised 2026 EPS guidance to $7.94-$8.02 (from $7.75-$7.85) and lifted the low end of revenue guidance to $5.89B, midpoint EPS implying 21.5% growth over 2025. The main caveat is that recent acquisitions, including 22 new operations with nine in Florida, are characterized as challenged turnarounds that are not yet accretive and will take a year or more to contribute.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $75.8 million, up 26.2% YoY, with breast up more than 50% and extremities/OMF/head and neck combined up 10.7%. GAAP net income was $2.3 million ($0.04/share), adjusted net income $13.1 million ($0.21/share), and adjusted EBITDA $13.4 million (17.7% margin, up 2.3 points YoY); gross margin was 74.8%, down 180 bps YoY on 3% higher product cost. Full-year 2026 guidance was revised to revenue growth of at least 29% (at least $290 million, including at least $7 million from BioCircuit), organic growth of at least 26%, gross margin of at least 73%, and positive free cash flow. Guidance embeds a step-down in gross margin sequentially in Q4 tied to production-plan changes for long-length Avance and possible BioCircuit inventory step-up.

eBay reported Q3 FY2026 GMV of $23.2 billion (up ~16% FXN total, 13% organic), revenue of $3.21 billion (up 13% FXN, 11% organic), non-GAAP operating income of $843 million (up 11%) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.51 (up ~12%), all above consensus and the high end of guidance ranges. Q4 guidance calls for GMV of $23.7–24.1 billion (12–14% FXN, 8–10% organic) and revenue of $3.19–3.24 billion (7–9% FXN, 5–7% organic), with EPS of $1.48–1.53 (5–9% growth) — a decelerating revenue trajectory versus Q3. Management also disclosed a ~9% workforce reduction to fund growth investments, and 2027 planning assumes trading card growth moderates off a strong 2026. Focus categories grew 24% and C2C/Recommerce each grew over 20%.

Q3 FY2026 net sales were $1.1 billion, up 7% year-over-year (adjusted net sales up 14%), gross margin 9.4% (up 150 bps), adjusted EBITDA $61 million (up 5%, 5.6% margin), and adjusted diluted EPS $0.50. Foods segment gross margin was 17.5% on improving fill rates (87% to ~98%), and the Foods outlook was raised to ~$650M net sales and ~$45M adjusted EBITDA from $625M/$35M. Full-year adjusted net sales growth (13%-15%) and adjusted EBITDA ($230M-$240M) were reiterated, but banana gross margin guidance was cut to 2%-3% from 3%-4% on weather, cost, and currency pressure, with inflationary headwinds now $55M-$65M. The quarter was carried by Foods and a strong gross profit (+27%), offset by a weaker fresh platform and a reduced banana outlook.

OGE reported Q3 consolidated net income of ~$316M, or $1.52/diluted share, versus $231M or $1.14 a year ago, with the electric utility at $1.54 versus $1.20, driven primarily by significantly warmer weather (45+ days of triple-digit heat versus one last year) partly offset by higher income tax expense. Management raised 2026 consolidated EPS guidance to $2.62-$2.68, assuming normal weather for the balance of the year. Horseshoe Lake units 11-12 came in ahead of schedule and $12M under budget, adding 448 MW, while Unit 15 represents ~$1.75B of investment with a 2031 in-service date. The company established an inaugural ATM program of up to $750M and expects ~$200M of incremental equity over the planning horizon; weather-normalized load growth was ~1%.

Benchmark reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $811 million, up 19% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.84 up 35%; both exceeded the high end of prior guidance. Non-GAAP gross margin was 10.5% (up 40 bps YoY) and operating margin 5.5% (up 70 bps YoY). Management raised its Q4 outlook to $815-855 million (19% YoY growth at midpoint) and now expects full-year 2026 revenue above $3 billion with 16% annual growth. One offset: next-gen HPC contribution shifted from late 2024/early 2027 expectations to mid-to-late 2027, though management frames it as upside layered on current business.

Peapack-Gladstone reported Q3 FY2026 net income available to common of $18.5 million, or $0.99 per diluted share, up 17% sequentially from $15.8 million/$0.86. Total revenue was $88 million, up 2% QoQ and 24% YoY, with NII of $68 million (+6% QoQ, +33% YoY) and NIM of 3.34% (+2 bps QoQ, in line with prior guidance). Loans grew $403 million to $7.1 billion and deposits $301 million to $7.4 billion, both above the $200 million/$200 million quarterly objectives, and the efficiency ratio improved to 63%. Management reiterated its 2-2-2 quarterly objectives, guided to 2-3 bps of NIM expansion per quarter into 2027, and said mid-to-upper single-digit expense growth is expected next year; the $0.99 EPS includes a one-time $1.8 million tax benefit (20.5% effective rate vs 28.4%) not expected to recur.

Connection reported Q3 FY2026 record net sales of $874.3 million, up 23.3% YoY, with record gross billings of $1.3 billion (+19.4%) and record gross profit of $161.9 million (+16.7%). Gross margin contracted 110 bps to 18.5% on large-project customer mix and lower netted-down software revenue, while operating income rose 35.4% to $41 million and diluted EPS grew 27.8% to $1.24. Management gave no formal EPS or revenue guidance but said Q4 should follow the historical sequential decline of roughly 3-4% from Q3 and expects to outperform the U.S. IT market by 200 bps for the year. Management noted the endpoint device upgrade cycle is largely behind it and expects endpoint demand slightly down in 2027, while saying it has not seen the typical Q4 budget flush.

Santander Brasil reported recurring net income of BRL 2.9 billion and ROE of 11.9%, which management explicitly called below target profitability. Client NII declined ~33 bps in the quarter and market NII also softened, with ~BRL 500 million of wholesale one-offs pressuring cost of risk. Expenses grew below inflation and the efficiency ratio improved to 38.8%, and management guided to better NII and lower agribusiness losses in 2027 versus 2026, but gave no quantitative targets and flagged continued deterioration in agribusiness, low-income, and now middle-income unsecured cards, plus concern that higher-for-longer rates pressure SMEs.

Q2 Holdings reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $225.8 million, up 12% year-over-year and 3% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $67.8 million (30% margin) and non-GAAP gross margin of 62.6%, both above the high end of guidance. Subscription revenue grew 14% to 83% of total, subscription ARR reached $846 million (+13.5%), and total ARR was $989 million (+11%). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $888-$892 million and adjusted EBITDA to $253-$256 million, implying ~500 bps of margin expansion versus prior expectations of ~250 bps, while reiterating 2027 subscription revenue growth of 12.5%-13% and 150-200 bps of margin expansion. The quarter also featured the appointment of CFO Jonathan Price as Co-CEO alongside Matt Flake.

Radware reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $84.4 million, up 12% YoY, and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.32 versus $0.33 a year ago. Cloud ARR reached ~$107 million, up 21%, while total ARR was ~$266 million, up 11%. Gross margin slipped to 81.4% from 82.4% on FX, mix, and supply chain pressure, and non-GAAP net income fell 6% to $13.9 million, with management noting $0.32 EPS would have been $0.41 excluding a $4.6 million shekel impact. Q4 guidance was set at $88-90 million revenue and $0.34-0.35 EPS.

Crane reported total sales up 28% with 8% core growth and 21 points from acquisitions, adjusted operating margin expanding 130 bps to a record 22.5%, and adjusted operating profit up 36%. Core orders rose 11% (PFT +20%) and total backlog increased 9% year-over-year to a record. The company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance by $0.35 at the midpoint to $7.23-$7.38 and lifted the acquisition EPS contribution to ~$0.30 from $0.20, while expecting the 10% ROIC hurdle ~18 months early. AAT core sales rose 9.5% with margin 26.3% (+100 bps), PFT core sales rose 6.2% with a record 24% margin, and the company announced the Trillium Pumps acquisition and BS&U divestiture.

Q3 FY2026 net income was $15.1 million, or $1.61 diluted EPS, up 5% and 13% year-over-year, on record revenue of $179 million, up 8% year-over-year, with the portfolio up 7.6% to $2.2 billion and operating expense ratio improving 20 bps to 12.6%. However, net credit losses of 10.9% came in 20 bps above the July outlook and 70 bps above prior year, with 30+ day delinquency up 50 bps to 7.5% on pressures concentrated in 2025 originations. Full-year net income growth (6%-9%), EPS growth (10%-13%), and portfolio growth (5%-7%) guidance is unchanged, but management guided Q4 net income below Q3 versus prior expectation it would exceed, citing higher credit losses, accelerated bank partnership costs, higher funding costs, and G&A timing. The bank partnership with Column now accounts for just over 40% of October originations, up from roughly 28% in July, and added about 120 bps to total revenue yield with an expected 200 bps pre-tax margin lift.

Q3 FY2026 net income was $22.8M or $0.88 per diluted share, up from $20.8M or $0.80 in the prior quarter, with diluted EPS up 21% YoY on an adjusted basis. NIM expanded 5 bps QoQ and 13 bps YoY to 3.62%, NII rose 2.6% QoQ to $64.5M, and the efficiency ratio improved to 58.3% from 59.6%. Guidance was constructive but incremental: Q4 NIM guided to the mid-3.60% range, full-year expense growth trimmed to 2%-2.5% from the prior range, and the Q4 dividend raised 3.3% to $0.31. Loan balances were roughly flat ($5.31B, down $54M YoY) with continued mix shift toward higher-yielding commercial and mainland production.

RenaissanceRe reported Q3 operating EPS of $12.71 and a 19% annualized operating ROE, but rising rates drove $763M of retained mark-to-market losses, a GAAP loss, and a 2% sequential decline in tangible book value per share. Gross premiums written fell 9% to $2.1B and net premiums written fell 19%, with the adjusted combined ratio at 79% after a 9-point hit from large losses (Middle East war, Ras Laffan LNG explosion, Colombia earthquake). Management expects property cat rates down less than the mid-teens YTD decline seen in 2026, casualty rates no longer exceeding trend in U.S. general liability, and further pullback in casualty. Capital return stayed aggressive with $310M of buybacks in Q3 and $144M in October.

Adjusted EPS of $0.86 rose 12% YoY with adjusted ROA of 1.16% (vs 1.09%) and adjusted ROTCE of 14.5%; the efficiency ratio improved to 57.7%. Linked-quarter EPS declined, which management attributed to a higher $13.3 million loan provision driven by loan growth, while reported NIM fell 6 bps to 3.77% and core NIM rose 2 bps. Loans grew $555.9 million (11.5% annualized) but total deposits fell $73.2 million on public fund outflows, and management reiterated mid-single-digit balance sheet growth rather than raising it. Separately, Renasant announced the roughly $140 million Commercial Bank & Trust merger (75% stock/25% cash), expected about 4% EPS accretive and 1.5% TBV dilutive, closing in Q1 2027.

CPKC reported Q3 FY2026 revenues of CAD 4.2 billion with 6% volume growth, a core adjusted operating ratio of 61.9% (up 120 bps YoY), and core adjusted diluted EPS of $1.28, up 16% YoY. Freight revenue rose 15% and cents per RTM increased 9% on disciplined pricing, with record Q3 intermodal and grain volumes. Management reiterated full-year mid-single-digit volume growth guidance, guided Q4 operating ratio to sub-60, and disclosed a new five-year Elk Valley Resources coal contract reclaiming roughly half of interchanged traffic. Fuel was a 190 bps OR headwind from a 53% average price increase, partially offset by $21 million of fuel efficiency savings.

Revenue hit a record $112.1M, up 3% sequentially and 17% YoY, with record endpoint IC revenue of $97.3M (+24% YoY) and systems revenue of $14.8M (+23% QoQ but -15% YoY). Non-GAAP net income was $22.1M or $0.69 EPS, and adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.9%. Q4 guidance is $104-107M (14% YoY growth at midpoint) and EPS of $0.55-0.60, a favorable end of typical seasonality due to returning specialty IC revenue, but systems revenue will decline sequentially on project timing. Gross margin fell to 54.9% from 60.9% sequentially mostly on prior licensing revenue, though product gross margin rose 130 bps QoQ on M800 mix, and management expects Q4 gross margin up ~100 bps sequentially.

RSI reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $385.9 million, up 39% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $62.2 million, up 73%, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 16.1% (15% excluding a $4.3 million FX gain). North America revenue grew 14% and Latin America 218%; online casino grew 32% and online sports 70%. Full-year revenue guidance of $1.56–$1.60 billion and EBITDA of $245–$265 million was reiterated, but management said October trends put revenue near the low end of the range, citing moderating North American iCasino market growth, while EBITDA trends are near the midpoint. Positive office said 'We are encouraged by the strength of our business and the opportunities ahead, and we look forward to updating you on our progress when we share our fourth quarter and full year results.'

Q3 FY2026 organic revenue grew just 1.5% versus the 3%-5% guide, and adjusted EPS of $0.73 fell 3% versus the $0.80-$0.82 range, with management attributing ~300 bps of the revenue shortfall and $0.07 of EPS to a cybersecurity incident. Adjusted gross margin contracted 300 bps to 68.0% and operating margin fell 150 bps to 26.5%. Q4 guidance calls for organic revenue declines of 1%-3% and EPS of $0.77-$0.79, with full-year EPS of $3.16-$3.18 and organic growth of ~4%; management said 2027 will be 'challenged to grow' sales and EPS excluding Penumbra, citing continued EP and WATCHMAN pressure, a 2027 competitive launch, and escalating China pricing headwinds.

BXP reported Q3 FY2026 FFO of $1.89 per share, beating the prior guidance midpoint by $0.08 and consensus, and raised full-year 2026 FFO guidance by $0.05 at the midpoint to $7.06-$7.08 (3.2% growth). Same-property NOI growth guidance rose 35 bps to 2.35%-2.75%; in-service occupancy climbed 100 bps sequentially to 89.4%, ahead of the 89% year-end target, and management now expects to end 2026 near 90%. Leasing spreads were +6.5% gross/+9.3% net, with dispositions ($520M this year, $1.37B since the investor conference) running well ahead of the $1.9B 2028 target, though 2027 FFO faces roughly $0.08 of sale dilution plus $0.06 more if Times Square Tower closes.

Revenue rose 12.4% YoY to ~$2.1B and net income grew 18.2% to $78M ($0.65 diluted) with Class 8 sales up 24.4% (6.5% share) and aftermarket parts/service up 5.8% to ~$680M at a 128.3% absorption ratio. Management flagged soft new order activity tied to uncertainty over EPA 2027 emission rules, but guided to a strong Q4 and solid Q1 supported by backlog, with supply constraints at tier 2/3 suppliers pushing some deliveries into Q1. Truck margins compressed (8.1% vs 8.5% a year ago) on a fleet-heavy mix, and no formal full-year guidance was provided. The company repurchased $10.3M of stock, paid $16.4M in dividends, declared $0.14/share, and held $226M in cash.

Rush reported Q3 revenue of roughly $2.1 billion, up 12.4% YoY, and net income of $78 million ($0.65 diluted), up 18.2%, with new Class 8 truck sales up 24.4% and Class 4-7 up 9.6%. Parts, service, and collision revenue rose 5.8% to about $680 million and generated nearly 63% of gross profit at a 128.3% absorption ratio. Management guided qualitatively to a strong Q4 and Q1 on backlog but flagged slower quoting/orders amid EPA 2027 emission-rule and pricing uncertainty, tier 2/3 supply constraints that could push deliveries into Q1, and truck margins down to ~8.1% from ~8.5% on mix toward lower-margin fleet business.

Cohu reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $173 million, up 37% YoY and above the midpoint of guidance, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.43, gross margin of 45.7% (above guidance), and adjusted EBITDA margin of 16.6%. Total bookings grew 126% YoY (systems up 318%, recurring up 36%), and the company raised its FY2026 revenue growth outlook to approximately 38% while guiding Q4 revenue to ~$178 million (~46% YoY growth). Management introduced a preliminary 2027 view of 30%-40% revenue growth with gross margin of 46%-48%, but noted Q4 gross margin is projected to decline to ~44% due to higher input costs and supply-chain tightness for specialty components.

Century Communities reported Q3 FY2026 home sales revenue of $842 million with 2,442 deliveries (down 2% YoY and 3% sequentially) and net income of $13 million, or $0.44 per diluted share ($1.01 adjusted). Adjusted homebuilding gross margin of 19.3% fell 70 bps sequentially on higher incentives, and GAAP margin was 15% after $19.6 million in inventory impairments across six underperforming communities. Management lowered full-year 2026 guidance to 9,350-9,650 deliveries and $3.3-3.4 billion in home sales revenue, and guided Q4 incentives 200-250 bps above Q3 levels. Net orders were 2,284 with September and October softening after a ~75 bp rise in mortgage rates, partly offset by a record 343 community count and the October HistoryMaker acquisition adding 29 communities.

Revenue rose 9% to $1.5 billion and adjusted EPS rose 6% to a record Q3 $5.92, but adjusted EBITDA was flat at $348 million and the adjusted EBITDA margin fell 210 bps year-over-year to 23.8% as raw material and freight costs rose faster than price realization. Management pushed price-cost parity out one quarter to exit 2026 (from Q3 neutral / Q4 positive guided in July), citing unanticipated input cost escalation, and guided Q4 to high single-digit revenue growth with flat adjusted EBITDA margin and CCM flat / CWT up ~100 bps. Q4 CCM price realization is expected around 7% versus about 4% in Q3, and the pricing now in place is expected to be a tailwind into 2027, with Vision 2030 targets of $40 adjusted EPS unchanged.

Chemed reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue growth of 10.6% and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 28.1% year over year. VITAS revenue rose 12.2% to $457.4 million on 9.4% days-of-care growth, with adjusted EBITDA ex-Medicare Cap up 31.4% to $92.5 million (20.2% margin), while Roto-Rooter revenue grew 7.5% (same-store +5.5%) but adjusted EBITDA fell 2.5% and margin contracted 213 bps to 20.6% on marketing and fuel costs. Management guided full-year 2026 adjusted EPS to at or slightly above the high end of the prior range, weighted toward VITAS. The key shift versus prior periods is a two-sided mix: VITAS outperformance offset by Roto-Rooter margin pressure and margin-dilutive franchise reacquisitions ($62.5 million California, $96 million year to date).

BrightSpire reported Q3 2026 GAAP net income of $46.9M or $0.37/share, driven largely by a $60.3M gain on the Albertsons NNN sale, but distributable earnings were only $10.3M or $0.08/share (adjusted DE $0.14/share) after $7.5M of specific CECL reserves. Undepreciated book value fell to $7.87 from $8.10 on higher CECL and REO impairments, though GAAP book value rose to $7.08 from $6.81. Management explicitly said it will slow loan book growth, hold more cash, and that full deployment and positive dividend coverage may be delayed given rate and credit-spread volatility; near-term portfolio growth is guided to be modest at best.

Constellium reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.6 billion, up 22% YoY, net income of $119 million versus $88 million last year, and Adjusted EBITDA up 17% to $276 million (or $280 million ex-metal price lag, a Q3 record). It again raised full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance, now $1.03-1.06 billion excluding metal price lag, with free cash flow expected above $300 million. Management flagged a softer implied Q4 versus an exceptional Q4 2025, citing seasonality, a recycling outage moved into Q4, tapering Oswego auto benefits, and Section 338 tariff headwinds, while pointing to significantly stronger aerospace demand and repricing in 2027.

PPG reported Q3 net sales up 7% to $4.4 billion with organic sales up 5% (2% volume), adjusted EPS up 6% to a Q3-record $2.25, and total company adjusted EBITDA margin above 18%. Company-wide commercial actions fully offset COGS inflation for the first time. Industrial Coatings was the weak spot, with segment EBITDA down 11% and margin contracting 260 bps to 14.4% on index-pricing lag. The full-year adjusted EPS midpoint was raised and the range narrowed to $7.90-$8.10, though Q4 organic growth is guided to only low single digits versus Q3's 5%, and management declined to quantify 2027 beyond themes of continued organic growth and margin expansion.

Q3 FY2026 net revenues of EUR 8.3 billion rose 4% year-on-year, marking 21 consecutive quarters of revenue growth, with profit before tax of EUR 2.6 billion up 8% and RoTE of 10.6%. All four divisions contributed, with the Corporate Bank posting record revenues near EUR 2 billion (+9% YoY) and the Private Bank up 8% on record EUR 17 billion net flows. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to above EUR 33 billion while keeping total expense guidance at around EUR 21.3 billion; CET1 was 14.0% and 2026 buybacks totaled EUR 1.5 billion. Loan loss provisions of EUR 501 million included proactive CRE de-risking and an idiosyncratic Asia corporate event, with the CRE run rate expected to decline gradually in 2027.

Bausch + Lomb reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.375B, up 8% constant currency, with adjusted EBITDA of $325M (up 34%) and adjusted EPS of $0.34 vs $0.18 a year ago. All three segments grew: Vision Care +6%, Surgical +9%, and Pharma +11%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for the third time this year, lifting revenue to $5.45B–$5.55B and adjusted EBITDA to $1.09B–$1.14B, with implied margin of ~20.3%, 130 bps above the Investor Day target. Adjusted gross margin expanded 300 bps to 64.7% (63.6% excluding a $14M tariff refund), and free cash flow of $178M was the strongest quarter since the 2022 IPO, bringing net leverage down to 4.1x from 5.7x.

Porch reported Q3 FY2026 Insurance Services revenue of $103 million, up 39% year-over-year, with segment Adjusted EBITDA of $50 million at a 49% margin; total company Adjusted EBITDA excluding the Reciprocal was $44 million, up 116% year-over-year. Reciprocal policies written rose 42% to 68,000 (accelerating from Q2's 38%), and GAAP net income attributable to Porch was $12 million, up $23 million year-over-year. Management raised full-year guidance for Adjusted EBITDA excluding the Reciprocal to $135-140 million (midpoint $138 million, 79% growth) from the prior $102 million starting midpoint, and provided an initial 2027 target of more than $180 million of Adjusted EBITDA excluding the Reciprocal, including a full year of Allied Trust. The company also announced the pending ~$200 million Allied Trust acquisition, expected to add roughly $25 million of Adjusted EBITDA in the first full year.

PROG delivered Q3 FY2026 revenue up ~26% to $725.8M and non-GAAP EPS of $1.06 (up 21.8%), with consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of $80M (11% margin) at the low end of the range, driven by leasing portfolio pressures. The company revised down its full-year 2026 outlook to revenue of $3.015-3.05B, Adjusted EBITDA of $345-355M, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.70-4.85, citing a stressed consumer. Progressive Leasing GMV grew 2.3% to $420.4M but revenue fell 0.7% and gross margin contracted 20 bps to 31.8%; Four grew GMV 103% and Purchasing Power grew GMV 12.3%. The company announced a $100M accelerated share repurchase and a replenished $500M buyback authorization, while net leverage fell to 1.5x.

Parsons reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue up 2% YoY to roughly $6.25-6.45B run-rate, with organic revenue ex the confidential contract up 2%, adjusted EBITDA up 6% to a record $168M and margin expanding 40 bps to a record 10.2%. FY2026 guidance was narrowed rather than raised, to revenue of $6.25-6.45B and adjusted EBITDA of $510-550M, with operating cash flow guidance maintained at $430-490M despite $269M of Q3 operating cash flow. Bookings rose 14% to $1.8B for a 1.1x book-to-bill, backlog hit a record $9.4B with 73% funded, and the company disclosed a CFO transition with Matt Ofilos departing and George Ball serving as interim CFO. Management flagged a $850M award under protest and lapping of the confidential contract as headwinds, guiding Q4 organic revenue to roughly flat.

Seacoast reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $59.9 million ($0.55 per share), up 1% sequentially and 64% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $0.66 (up 9% QoQ, 59% YoY) and adjusted ROA of 1.34%. Net interest margin held at 3.83% (core up 1 bp to 3.66%), loans grew $429 million or 13% annualized, NPLs fell 15% to $73.3 million (54 bps), and adjusted efficiency improved to 53.9% from 54.5%. 2026 guidance was reiterated with management stating it expects to hit the high end of the range, while flagging ~$2.4 million of discrete Q4 expenses and a step-up to roughly 10% annualized loan growth vs. 13% this quarter. The Villages conversion completed, ending M&A charges, and management pointed to margin expansion into 2027 on back-book repricing plus a ~$300 million seasonal public-funds deposit inflow.

Amphenol reported record Q3 FY2026 sales of $10.2 billion, up 65% YoY (37% organic) and 17% sequentially, with adjusted diluted EPS of $0.80 (up 74% YoY) and adjusted operating margin of 29.7% (up 220 bps YoY, down 10 bps sequentially on tougher tariff-recovery comparison). Orders hit a record $12.17 billion for a 1.19:1 book-to-bill, and management guided Q4 to $10.3-$10.5 billion in sales and $0.81-$0.83 adjusted EPS (60-63% and 65-69% YoY growth), lifting full-year sales to ~$36.9-$37.1 billion and adjusted EPS to $2.82-$2.84. Results exceeded the high end of prior guidance, and the board raised the dividend 20% to $0.15 per share and authorized a new $4 billion buyback. The one soft spot is communications networks, where organic sales fell 28% YoY on broadband weakness, with further decline guided for Q4.

Blackbaud reported Q3 revenue of $293M, up 4.1% YoY, non-GAAP EPS of $1.36 (up 24%), adjusted EBITDA of $111M at a 38% margin, and free cash flow of $126M. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed with revenue and adjusted EBITDA expected in the upper half of the range, and EPS and free cash flow at or above the high end; no AI product revenue is included in the 2026 guide. Management flagged a 40% larger 2026 contractual renewal cohort that is moderating recurring revenue growth through 1H 2027, with gross dollar retention expected to return to 91%-92% by end-2027 as the 2027 cohort is nearly 25% smaller. The quarter reflects solid EPS/cash flow execution and heavier AI product announcements (Platform for Good, Lantern, Agents for Good) rather than a revenue beat.

Reported and adjusted earnings were $5.6 billion, or $14.08 per share, with operating cash flow of $7.3 billion ($6.2 billion excluding a $1.1 billion working capital benefit). The company returned $2.8 billion to shareholders, cut debt by $2 billion to $18.5 billion, and reduced net debt to capital to 26%, hitting its 2027 target early, while announcing a second 2026 dividend increase of 10.8% versus Q4 2025. Q4 guidance calls for mid-80s chemicals utilization and mid-90s crude utilization; cumulative shareholder return was 40% through Q3 versus the >50% commitment, with management targeting above 50% in Q4. Refining ran at 98% utilization with record 41% distillate yield, and management cited a widened WCS/WTI differential worth $140 million per dollar.

Dana reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $2.038 billion, up $121 million YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $218 million at a 10.7% margin, up 220 bps from 10.7% prior year. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.41 versus a $0.04 loss last year, though GAAP continuing-operations loss was $10 million on a $64 million tax charge including a $29 million foreign audit settlement. Full-year guidance raised sales midpoint by $50 million to ~$7.8 billion while maintaining adjusted EBITDA at ~$825 million (10.6% margin), EPS at ~$2.00, and adjusted free cash flow at ~$325 million, citing cost inflation and recovery timing uncertainty. The Eaton Mobility split-off remains on track for ~Q1 2027 close with $250 million synergy target and leverage of 1.6x.

ProPetro reported Q3 2026 revenue of $355 million, up 16% sequentially, net income of $13 million ($0.09 per diluted share) versus a prior-quarter net loss of $8 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $60 million (17% of revenue) up 33% sequentially. PROPWR adjusted EBITDA reached roughly $8 million and contracted capacity totals about 510 MW, with 250-275 MW deployed by year-end 2026 and more than 500 MW by early 2028. Completions margins were pressured by higher-than-expected fleet reactivation and rebuilding costs, and management flagged meaningful Q4 seasonality plus continued margin pressure despite a sold-out 13-fleet position. 2026 capex guidance was narrowed for PROPWR to $400-$430 million (from prior) while per-MW cost of $1.4-$1.5 million and PROPWR guidance were reaffirmed and unchanged.

Q3 FY2026 net sales rose 11.2% to $1.135 billion, with organic sales up 10.3% and acquisitions adding ~0.9%; adjusted EBITDA grew to $82.2 million from $65.1 million and adjusted EPS rose to $0.66 from $0.50. Gross margin expanded ~84 bps to 25%, driven by product mix and procurement scale, though fuel costs kept adjusted OpEx roughly flat versus prior year. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of $4.56-$4.61 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $317-$321 million, while flagging some conservatism on the Middle East and a tougher Q4 comp.

Carvana reported Q3 FY2026 retail units of 217,385 (+39% YoY) and revenue of $8.04 billion (+42%), both company records, with net income of $483 million and record Adjusted EBITDA of $800 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.0% from 11.3%, driven by mix toward higher-priced vehicles and give-back to customers in other GPU, while net income margin rose to 6.0% from 4.7%. For FY2026, management reiterated the previously communicated $2.7-3.0 billion Adjusted EBITDA range and expects sequential increases in retail units and Adjusted EBITDA in Q4, contingent on a stable environment. Balance sheet metrics hit records at 0.8x net debt/Adjusted EBITDA and 6.9x EBITDA/interest, aided by a refinancing that saves roughly $45 million annually.

Q3 2026 Core FFO was $0.53/diluted share, up 10.4% YoY, with 9-month Core FFO of $1.57, up 13.8%. Management raised full-year 2026 Core FFO guidance to $2.11-$2.14 from $2.09-$2.13 (midpoint ~14% growth) and lifted the low end of AFFO guidance to $2.22-$2.25, while raising investment volume to ~$472M from a prior $300-400M. Shopping center same-property NOI grew 3.8% for the quarter (6.2% YTD), moderating as late-2025 anchor openings rolled into the comparable base. The company closed a $1B unsecured credit facility, extended weighted average debt maturity to 4.3 years from 1.6, and ended at 5.9x net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA with ~$255M liquidity.

Q3 subscription revenue of $3.988B grew 20.5% cc, 50 bps above the high end of guidance, with cRPO up 21% cc (100 bps beat) and non-GAAP operating margin of 32.5% (150 bps above guidance); free cash flow margin was 20%. Guidance was raised: full-year subscription revenue midpoint lifted $15M to $15.785B (21% cc growth) and FY free cash flow margin raised 100 bps to 36%, alongside a second AI ACV target raise to $1.7B+ from $1.5B. Q4 cRPO guidance of 18.5% cc embeds headwinds from early Q3 renewals that pulled deals forward, higher on-prem mix, and deployment-expertise carve-outs (~50 bps), which management framed as accounting nuance rather than demand softening. AI net new ACV grew 65% YoY and year-to-date agentic AI consumption in production is up 13x.

GE HealthCare reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.5 billion, up 6.2% organically, with growth across all segments. Adjusted EBIT margin expanded 180 bps to 16.6% and adjusted EPS rose 25.1% to $1.34, while free cash flow reached $793 million. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for organic revenue growth (~4%), adjusted EBIT margin (15.5%-15.7%), adjusted EPS ($4.95-$5.05), and free cash flow (>1.6 billion), citing strong execution and margin expansion. Backlog grew 12% to $23.7 billion, though book-to-bill was 1.03 and Q4 growth is implied at 3%-4% due to a prior-year product hold comparison.

Artisan reported Q3 revenue of $313 million, up 1% sequentially and 4% YoY, with adjusted operating margin expanding 260 bps sequentially to 35.5% and adjusted EPS of $1.03 (up 1% YoY). But AUM fell 8% sequentially and 7% YoY to $169 billion on $10.6 billion of net outflows, of which ~$7.8 billion came from the US value team wind-down and a large Global Value client rebalancing. Management flagged short-term relative underperformance in International Value and Global Value, though it noted 75% and 84% of AUM outperforming over one and three years as of October 26. Q4 starts with lower AUM and an estimated $2.5 billion distribution-driven AUM reduction, with performance fees projected similar to last year's ~$29 million.

GSK reported Q3 FY2026 sales up 5% to GBP 8.9 billion at CER, core operating profit up 5% and core EPS up 1%, with strong cash generation of GBP 7.4 billion year-to-date and free cash flow up GBP 1.8 billion. Full-year 2026 guidance was reconfirmed rather than raised: sales and core operating profit expected in the upper half of the range, core operating margin above 31%, EPS growth in the low half of the range, and FX headwinds of -1% on sales and -3% on operating profit. The quarter was ordinary on the numbers, with specialty sales up 15% offset by vaccines down 2% and general medicines flat; management commentary was mixed, highlighting launch momentum and a large late-stage pipeline ramp but also acknowledging U.S. price pressure in the inhaled respiratory class, ViiV management changes, and an EXTEND 4M PK analysis still pending.

Record pre-tax income of $76.8 million, up 34% YoY, with diluted EPS of $0.50 beating the $0.43-$0.48 guidance range; originations rose 26% to $3.34 billion, risk-adjusted revenue rose 27% to a record $279 million, and net charge-off ratio improved to 3.1% from 3.4%. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $1.87-$1.92, though Q4 originations are guided down to $3.1-$3.2 billion on seasonality and higher borrower pricing. Net interest income grew 16% to a record $183 million with NIM at 6.05%, and a $15 million hedging gain and $12 million of one-time fair value benefits offset roughly $20 million of rate-driven markdowns. Management cited strong credit and a $5-$10 million expected Q4 provision benefit, but flagged a transition period as it pulls back on thinner-margin auto refinance and raises coupons through borrowers.

Alkami reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $134.9 million, up 19% YoY and above the high end of guidance, with subscription revenue +20% and 96% of total. Adjusted EBITDA was $26.3 million at a 19.5% margin, up over 530 bps YoY, and management raised full-year revenue to $530.5-$532 million (19.6-19.9% growth) and Adjusted EBITDA to $98-$99 million. However, gross margin of 63.1% came in below expectations on third-party product mix, Q4 revenue guidance of $139.7-$141.2 million is slightly below where some modeled due to an $800K one-time Q3 revenue shift and higher third-party costs, and YTD new logos of 16 trail the 21 average since IPO, which management attributed to strategic-review uncertainty. Live ARR grew 19% to $533 million with a $56 million backlog.

Hayward reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 6% to $260 million with adjusted diluted EPS up 29% to $0.18 and adjusted EBITDA up 9% to $65 million (24.8% margin, +60 bps). North America grew 9% (7% price, 2% volume) while Europe and rest of world fell 6%, largely on an in-transit shipment timing shift into Q4. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: sales growth now ~5%-6% (from ~5%) and adjusted diluted EPS $0.86-$0.88 (from $0.84-$0.87). Q4 sales implied flat to +3% with a less favorable price/mix as the mix shifts toward discounted Early Watch volume.

Hudson reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $59.4 million, down 20% year over year, as sales volume fell 9% and average watching price fell 17%; gross margin was 25% versus 32% a year ago, and net income fell to $2.0 million ($0.05 diluted) from $12.4 million ($0.27). Management reaffirmed its 2026 gross margin target at the low-to-mid 20% range and said it expects 2027 pricing to be roughly flat with 2026, while noting Q3 volume decline was intentional as it prioritized profitable sales.
