The company ended the quarter debt-free with $35.3 million in cash, up $10 million from June 30, but did not repurchase shares in the quarter despite the stock trading below book.

FinWise reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $10 million, or $0.73 per diluted share, with continuing operations at $10.4 million or $0.76, including a $6.5 million one-time bargain purchase gain from the Tallied transaction. Net interest income rose 17% sequentially to $41.9 million and originations reached $2.1 billion, well above the roughly $1.6 billion prior guide, while credit-enhanced balances nearly doubled to $146.2 million. Management guided Q4 originations to $1.5-$1.6 billion (below Q3 seasonality) and set that as the 2027 run rate, guided Q4 charge-offs to about $4 million versus the unusually favorable $2.6 million this quarter, and explicitly said the strong credit results are not a new run rate. The Upstart relationship ends September 30, 2026 with immaterial impact, and two partners have signaled intent to pursue bank charters, though their agreements run into late 2028 and early 2029.

Highwoods reported Q3 FFO of $0.89/share ($100.1M) and net income of $31.8M ($0.29/share), with no land sale gains or unusual items. Full-year 2026 FFO guidance was raised $0.025 at the midpoint to $3.51-$3.70, and excluding land gains the midpoint implies Q4 FFO above $0.90/share. Occupancy rose 130 bps sequentially, the lease rate reached 90.1%, and GAAP rent growth on 1.2M sq ft of second-gen leases was 29% (cash +4%). Cash same-property NOI was roughly flat at 0.2% versus GAAP +4.1%, with the gap attributed to free rent on new leases; management expects cash NOI to accelerate as that burns off, with free cash flow normalization pushed toward 2028.

Honeywell Aerospace's first standalone quarter delivered $4.6B in organic sales, up 2.4% versus expectations of flat to slightly up, with adjusted EBIT of $1.2B (up 4%) and adjusted EPS of $2.21; adjusted EBIT margin of ~25% included ~$50M of IEEPA tariff refunds worth over 100 bps. Full-year organic growth guidance was maintained at 4%-5% and pro forma adjusted EBIT narrowed around the same $4.4B midpoint, but Q4 organic sales are guided modestly below the full-year range and margin steps down to mid-23s as tariff refunds lapse. EPS guidance was raised to $7.85-$8.00 on lower below-the-line costs and second-half free cash flow guidance lifted to $1.2-1.4B, alongside a newly declared $0.40 quarterly dividend. Backlog rose 12% to over $19B and book-to-bill was 1.3, but output remains gated by roughly 70 constrained mechanical suppliers, with management explicitly deferring the acceleration to 2027.

Hope Bancorp reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $157 million, up 7% QoQ and 11% YoY, with diluted EPS of $0.28 (up 16% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.29. Net interest margin expanded 6 bps to 3.02%, and pre-provision net revenue rose 11% sequentially to $55 million. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 16-18% revenue growth and 23-25% PPNR growth, including the MANUBANK acquisition closed October 1. The deal adds $2.2 billion of loans and $2.6 billion of deposits, but CET1 is expected to drop about 200 bps to roughly 10.2%, and full cost savings are delayed to 2028.

Revenue fell 2.9% YoY to just over $2 billion (down 2.5% in constant currency and 1.9% QoQ, partly from the Symphony divestiture), but adjusted EBITDA rose 3% sequentially to $337 million with margin up 70 bps to 16.6%, and adjusted EPS rose 4% sequentially to $2.66. Commercial momentum was strong: gross wins up 27% YoY, record net wins of $3.15 billion (up 51% YoY), net book-to-bill of 1.56x, and free cash flow of $302 million. Management narrowed 2026 guidance, raising the revenue outlook to the high end of the prior range on higher pass-through activity (~low 30s as a percentage of revenue), and declined to give formal 2027 guidance while floating mid-single-digit revenue growth and higher single-digit earnings growth as a reasonable reference point.

IDEX reported Q3 FY2026 organic sales growth of 8% (above the 5%-7% guide), record adjusted EPS of $2.33 (above $2.20-$2.25 guidance), adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.8% (above the 27%-27.5% range), and adjusted gross margin expansion of 70 bps to 45.2%. Organic orders rose 13% to nearly $1 billion with growth in all three segments (HST +21%, FMT +11%, FSDP +1%). The company raised full-year 2026 organic growth guidance to 6.5%-6.8% from 5%-6% and adjusted EPS to $8.91-$8.96 from $8.70-$8.85, while tightening EBITDA margin to 27.1%-27.3%. Free cash flow was $214 million (124% conversion), leverage improved to 1.8x, and $75 million of shares were repurchased with plans for ~$75 million per quarter through 2026.

Adjusted EBITDA rose to $843 million with margin up nearly 400 bps sequentially to 13.6%, and adjusted operating EPS was $0.37, with North America packaging EBITDA up 56% sequentially to $663 million on $141 million favorable price/mix and $85 million favorable operations. But the full-year North America packaging EBITDA outlook was cut to $2.27-$2.31 billion, with ~$145 million of incremental headwinds (diesel, distribution, volume) reducing the midpoint by ~$110 million, and Q3 free cash flow was -$267 million. Q4 North America packaging EBITDA is guided to ~$700-$740 million; EMEA guidance was withdrawn ahead of the planned separation. Management said market conditions persist into 2027 and declined to guide 2027, while noting more price realization (September increase) remains ahead.

InvenTrust reported Q3 2026 same property NOI of $50.4 million, up 3.1% YoY, with NAREIT FFO of $0.53 per diluted share, up 8.2%, and core FFO of $0.50, up 6.4%. Full-year NAREIT FFO guidance was raised to $2.05-$2.07 and core FFO to $1.94-$1.96, while same property NOI guidance was updated to 3.75%-4.25% and net investment assumptions trimmed to $190-$255 million on deal timing. Leasing was a highlight with 86 leases, blended spreads of 14% (new 42%, renewal 11%), leased occupancy up 20 bps sequentially to 96.4%, and a signed-not-open pipeline of roughly 110 bps of occupancy and $4.3 million of ABR. The main change was management raising acquisition return hurdles by 25-50 bps and slowing external growth as private-market pricing has not adjusted to higher debt costs.

SiteOne reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 3% to $1.29 billion, with organic daily sales down 1% as roughly 5% volume decline more than offset 4% price. Gross margin expanded 80 bps to 35.5% and adjusted EBITDA rose 8% to $138.3 million (10.7% margin, up 60 bps), while SG&A rose 20 bps to 28.6% and net income grew 8% to $63.9 million. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance is $425-$440 million, and management now expects to take a $6-$8 million Q4 charge for workforce reductions and branch closures, with the 53rd week an additional $4-$5 million drag, while still guiding to slight full-year margin expansion. End-market demand remains soft, with new residential seen down double digits for the year and repair and upgrade stepping down on higher rates and weak consumer confidence.

JLL reported a record third quarter with revenue up 12% in local currency, advisory growth accelerating to 22%, adjusted EBITDA up 33% with margin expansion, and adjusted EPS up 52%. Leasing Advisory revenue rose 27% and Capital Markets investment sales rose 33%, both well above market growth rates. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $25.20-$26.30 (37% growth at the midpoint) and lifted the Leasing Advisory full-year revenue target to high teens from mid-to-high teens, while maintaining mid-teens Capital Markets and mid-to-high single-digit REMS targets. The quarter included $142 million of buybacks, a year-to-date total of $552 million, and an imminent $500 million accelerated share repurchase, alongside caution on higher bond yields affecting Capital Markets deal timelines and U.S. multifamily pricing.

Arch reported Q3 2026 after-tax operating income of $910 million, or $2.67 per share, a 16% annualized operating ROE, with an 81.2% overall ex-cat accident year combined ratio (up 70 bps YoY) and $179 million of favorable prior-year development. Reinsurance net premiums written fell 9.3% amid abundant capacity and lighter property/short-tail participation, insurance net premiums written rose 2.7% (low single-digit underlying growth after adjusting for middle-market program non-renewals), and mortgage underwriting income was $201 million on a 2.2% delinquency rate. Management returned $1.4 billion via 14.8 million share repurchases (109% of YTD net income), with buybacks preferred over special dividends, and flagged a modest upward glide in reinsurance ex-cat loss ratios (roughly 200 bps) as rates ease. No formal guidance raise or cut; competitive conditions are described as uneven with property/short-tail softening and casualty still priced at or above loss trend.

Align reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.0148B, up 1.9% YoY (2.4% constant currency) and in line with its outlook, with clear aligner shipments up 6.6% to 691,000 at the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP gross margin of 70.4% came in modestly below the ~71% outlook, while non-GAAP operating margin of 24.4% exceeded guidance; non-GAAP EPS was $2.80, up 7.3% YoY. Management lowered FY2026 reported revenue guidance to $4.11B-$4.13B, citing weaker Q4 systems and services revenue ($170M-$180M, down 7.6% in Q3) and slightly lower clear aligner volume and ASP assumptions, though it reiterated ~100 bps of non-GAAP operating margin improvement for 2026 and targets at least another 100 bps in 2027. The call also disclosed a CEO succession (Jennifer Davis effective December 31) and continued buybacks, with ~$500M planned for 2026.

FEMSA reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues up 9.8% YoY and operating income up 9.9% (9.4% and 13.4% respectively on a currency-neutral basis), with net consolidated income of MXN 10.6 billion, up 81% on an easy base including last year's MXN 3.1 billion discontinued-ops loss and a MXN 1.1 billion FX gain. OXXO México same-store sales rose 9.2% on 5.5% ticket and 3.5% traffic growth (traffic up 150 bps sequentially despite minimal World Cup benefit), while OXXO gross margin contracted 120 bps and operating margin 40 bps; excluding 140 store closures, operating income grew 8%. Coca-Cola FEMSA grew revenue 10.9% and operating income 15.4% (7.4% ex a one-time insurance benefit); Health operating income fell 63.2% on a MXN 430 million Colombia credit provision and Europe fell 24.8%. No formal guidance was issued; management said net new stores will come 'a bit short' of the 1,000 run-rate this year but the target stands for next year, and flagged a soft Mexico consumer, Brazil volatility, and a harder comparison base ahead.

Aon reported Q3 FY2026 organic revenue growth of 6% (highest of the year) with total revenue up 3% to $4.1 billion, adjusted operating income up 5% to $1.1 billion, adjusted operating margin expanding 70 bps to 27%, and adjusted EPS up 10% to $3.36; free cash flow was $1.1 billion. All four solution lines grew mid-single digits or better, led by commercial risk and reinsurance at 7% each, supported by 11 points of new business and mid-90s retention. Management reaffirmed prior standalone full-year 2026 guidance across organic revenue, margin, EPS, and free cash flow, and confirmed the USI acquisition remains on track to close in Q4 with $395 million of identified synergies. The quarter showed broad-based growth and margin expansion offsetting a softer P&C/reinsurance pricing environment and an 8% decline in fiduciary investment income.

Garmin reported Q3 revenue of $1.986B, up 12% YoY, with gross margin of 63.3% (+420 bps) and operating margin of 30.8% (+500 bps), aided by $33M of tariff refunds and favorable segment mix; pro forma EPS rose 39% to $2.76. Full-year guidance was raised to revenue of ~$8.15B (from $8.05B) and pro forma EPS of ~$10.80 (from $10.00), with gross margin now ~61% and operating margin ~29%. The key change versus prior periods is a memory cost headwind that management said will pressure gross margin in Q4 and return the consolidated gross margin profile to its historical range in 2027. Fitness grew 16%, outdoor 20%, marine 16%, aviation 5%, while Auto OEM fell 20%.

GBank reported Q3 results that management itself described as 'much lower than expectations,' with net interest income and NIM improving to 3.95% (up about 17 bps) and continued expense pressure. Interchange income fell because several online sports betting operators disallowed credit cards as a payment source, and gain-on-sale income was reduced by a timing change in SBA sales rules. Guidance was minimal: loan growth of 10%-15%, a normalized gain-on-sale margin of 5%-6%, and the statement that gaming FinTech programs will not be material near term. The CEO transition to Jeff Newgard was completed, and management said credit costs should normalize by 2027 while citing a $10 million reduction in early-stage delinquencies.

GE Vernova reported Q3 2026 revenue up 18% with adjusted EBITDA up 123% to $1.9 billion and margin expanding 690 bps, alongside orders of $29.3 billion (up 96% YoY) and backlog growing to $197 billion. Management raised 2026 revenue, margin, and free cash flow guidance, citing strong Q3 performance and confidence in Q4. The company announced a $9 billion acquisition of Trench Group (~36% 2028 EBITDA margin, mid-teens revenue growth) to be funded with equal parts debt and cash, and doubled the buyback authorization from $10 billion to $20 billion. Power reached 21% EBITDA margins, Electrification 19%, and Wind turned profitable.

Glaukos reported record Q3 FY2026 net sales of $211 million, up 58% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.47, non-GAAP gross margin near 88% (up ~400 bps YoY), and more than $50 million in cash generation. Epioxa contributed ~$53 million and iDose TR ~$76 million, driving U.S. glaucoma franchise sales of $118.6 million (+47%) and corneal health of $59 million (+154%). Management raised full-year 2026 net sales guidance to $775-$785 million from $680-$700 million (an increase of $90 million at the midpoint) and introduced preliminary 2027 revenue guidance of $1 billion. The primary risk flagged is the proposed iDose TR local coverage determinations, which management said the 2027 outlook already contemplates under downside scenarios.

Fortive reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $1.1 billion, up 8% reported and 7.2% core, with adjusted EPS of $0.77 up over 13% and adjusted EBITDA of $340 million up 10% (30.6% margin, +50 bps). Core growth accelerated sequentially for a fifth straight quarter, with IOS core up 9% on Fluke and FAL strength while AHS core grew only 3.1% and its adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 230 bps. Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $3.10-$3.14 (up ~15% at the midpoint) and guides full-year revenue just north of $4.4 billion with core growth just north of 5%. Adjusted gross margin fell 80 bps to ~63% on product mix, and Q4 carries a four-fewer-watching-day headwind of $15-20 million revenue and 150 bps to core growth.

Generac reported record Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.29 billion, up 16% YoY, with C&I up 28% to $553 million and residential up 9% to $744 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose 33% to $256 million (19.8% margin), and GAAP EPS was $1.83 vs $1.12, with adjusted EPS $2.54 vs $1.83. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 20.5%-21% from 20%-21% but maintained net sales growth guidance in the mid-to-high teens, with data center revenue now expected near $500 million vs ~$450 million prior. A long-term Amazon supply agreement drove data center backlog to ~$4.5 billion (nearly tripling QoQ) and 2027 data center revenue is expected to exceed $2 billion.

Fortinet reported Q3 FY2026 billings up 29% to $2.34B and total revenue up 20% to $2.08B, with product revenue up 37% to $765M and non-GAAP EPS up 23% to $0.91; non-GAAP operating margin was a Q3 record 38.2%, up 130 bps, above the high end of guidance. FY2026 billings guidance was raised for the third time this year to $9.568B-$9.718B (28% growth at midpoint) and revenue to $8.125B-$8.215B (20%), with operating margin and EPS also raised, though management flagged a services revenue shortfall tied to delayed service activation on large enterprise deals. Service revenue grew 13% to $1.31B, and management now expects improved service revenue growth in 2027 versus 2026, citing 26% service billings growth and 19% deferred revenue growth as leading indicators.

Arch reported Q3 2026 after-tax operating income of $910 million, or $2.67 per share, a 16% annualized operating ROE, with net income ROE of 18.1%. The overall ex-cat accident year combined ratio was 81.2%, up 70 bps YoY, and underwriting income included $179 million of favorable prior-year development (4.5 points) against $234 million of current-year catastrophe losses. Reinsurance gross premiums written fell about 8% and net premiums written 9.3% amid abundant capacity, while insurance net premiums written grew 2.7% with YTD underlying growth of low single digits. The company repurchased 14.8 million shares for $1.4 billion in the quarter, roughly 109% of nine-month net income, and added about $100 million of buybacks in October; no formal earnings guidance was provided.

FormFactor reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $280.5 million, up 9% sequentially and roughly 40% year over year, coming in $10.5 million above the high end of the $260-280 million outlook range, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.04 versus $0.82 in Q2 and non-GAAP gross margin of 56.5% (up 320 bps sequentially). Management guided Q4 revenue to approximately $285 million +/- $10 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.95 +/- $0.09, with gross margin around 54%, and raised its baseline gross margin framework to about 53% from 51-51.5% previously. Roughly $10.5 million (about 380 bps) of the Q3 gross margin came from non-recurring tariff refunds and favorable sub-component costs; 2026 Farmers Branch cash CapEx was cut to $100-110 million from a prior $140-170 million on timing only. TRITON revenue expectations rose to upwards of $30 million for 2026 from an initial $10-20 million, and the Teradyne partnership includes a $300 million investment in FormFactor.

AEP reported Q3 2026 operating earnings of $2.23/share ($1.2 billion) versus $1.80/share in Q3 2025, with all segments contributing higher earnings on constructive regulation, demand growth, and transmission/generation build-out. Management said it expects full-year 2026 operating earnings at or above the high end of the $6.25-$6.55 range, introduced 2027 guidance of $6.75-$7.05 and 2028 of $7.40-$7.70, and raised the long-term annual operating EPS growth rate to 9%-11% (from 7%-9%) through 2031 with a >10% CAGR. Backing this is a $100 billion five-year capital plan driving rate base from $87 billion in 2026 to $162 billion by 2031 (~13%+ CAGR), with 84 GW of contracted load through 2031 (up 15 GW from Q2). The main trade-offs are a more modest ~2% dividend growth target and $5.2 billion of incremental equity funding tied to the expanded plan.

Alphabet reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $127.6B, up 25% YoY in both reported and constant currency, with operating income up 30% to $40.6B and operating margin at 31.8%. Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7B with operating margin expanding to 36.2% from 23.7%, while Services grew 11% and Search grew 12% to $63.3B. Net income and EPS declined due to a negative $8.2B in OI&E from an unrealized SpaceX loss, and Q3 free cash flow was negative $9.1B on $51.4B of CapEx. FY2026 CapEx guidance of $195-205B was unchanged, Q4 faces a slightly larger FX headwind and slower Search comps, and Cloud margins face near-term pressure from ramping third-party capacity.

AerCap reported record adjusted EPS of $6.56 and record adjusted ROE of 22% in Q3 2026, with GAAP net income of $949 million ($6.17/share) on basic lease rents of $1.698 billion. It raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to approximately $20.70 (including $4.70 of year-to-date gains on sale, before any Q4 gains) and now expects full-year asset sales above $5 billion versus $4-$5 billion previously. Drivers of the raise were strong gains on sale ($353 million in Q3, a record), elevated net maintenance contribution ($453 million YTD) and higher other income. Management flagged that net maintenance contribution should normalize to about $50 million per quarter in 2027 and that higher jet fuel prices are pressuring some airlines, though order book is fully placed through end-2027 and 80% through end-2028.

Alphabet reported Q3 revenue of $127.6 billion, up 25% YoY in reported and constant currency, with operating income up 30% to $40.6 billion and operating margin of 31.8%. Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.7 billion with operating margin expanding to 36.2% from 23.7%, and Search and other advertising rose 12% to $63.3 billion. Net income and EPS decreased due to an $8.2 billion unrealized loss on the SpaceX investment, and free cash flow was negative $9.1 billion on $51.4 billion of CapEx. Full-year 2026 CapEx guidance of $195-205 billion was unchanged, but management flagged Q4 FX headwinds, lapping Search acceleration, and near-term Cloud margin pressure from third-party capacity.

Alphabet reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $127.6 billion, up 25% YoY in both reported and constant currency, with operating income up 30% to $40.6 billion and operating margin at 31.8%. Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7 billion with segment operating margin expanding to 36.2% from 23.7%, though the quarter was meaningfully aided by TPU system sales, and net income/EPS fell on an $8.2 billion unrealized loss on the SpaceX investment. Full-year 2026 CapEx guidance of $195-205 billion was unchanged and expected to rise significantly in 2027; the company flagged a slightly larger Q4 FX headwind, lapping pressure on Search growth, and Cloud margin headwinds from ramping third-party compute. Free cash flow turned negative at -$9.1 billion on $51.4 billion of CapEx, a $5.2 billion EC fine payment, and TPU inventory build, with future purchase commitments of $924 billion.

GPI reported Q3 2026 revenue of $5.4 billion, gross profit of $855 million, adjusted net income of $112 million and adjusted diluted EPS of $9.36 from continuing operations. U.S. new vehicle sales fell 4.6% same-store and U.S. used same-store sales dropped 10%, partly offset by record customer pay revenue with RO count up over 4% and customer pay revenue up 3.2%. Adjusted SG&A as a percent of gross rose to 67.7% and U.S. same-store customer pay gross profit growth decelerated, with management flagging no pricing room and an expected ~12-month wait for after-sales recovery. The Hennessy acquisition closed in early Q4 adding ~$1.7 billion revenue at ~7% EBITDA margin, with $1.1-1.2 billion of dispositions targeted by mid-2027; leverage rose to ~4x pro forma from 3.3x with buybacks paused until a return to ~3x.

Jersey Mike's reported Q3 FY2026 system-wide sales of $1.2 billion, up 11% on 9% net unit growth and a 3% same-store sales increase that accelerated from 2.3% in Q2 and was led by transactions. Total revenue rose 10% to $209 million and adjusted EBITDA grew 20% to $125 million, aided by a $9 million year-over-year benefit from the area director transition. Full-year guidance was reiterated at SSS of at least 2.5%, net unit growth of at least 8%, adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 20%, with Q4 implied comps near 3% reflecting a short-lived late-Q3 consumer softness. The board authorized a $100 million buyback and a $0.35 per-share special dividend, roughly $200 million of capital return within four months of IPO.

Kirby reported record Q3 EPS of $2.09, up 27% YoY, with marine transportation revenue up 17% to $569 million and operating income up 26% at a 20% margin, while Distribution & Services revenue rose 6% to $408 million with a 12% operating margin. Management narrowed FY2026 earnings growth guidance to 10%-15% and said results should land toward the upper end of that range, a modest tightening from the prior range. Inland revenue guidance was raised to low double-digit growth from mid-to-high single digits, driven by improving spot and term pricing as 35%-40% of the term book renews in Q4. Q3 free cash flow was $74 million on elevated working capital, and $112 million was returned via buybacks at an average price of $137.
